News.title: Port Tyne crane incident: Huge 999 response as person taken to hospital and scene described as 'horrific'
News.content:
Port Tyne crane incident: Huge 999 response as person taken to hospital and scene described as 'horrific'

Crews from North East Ambulance Service and the Great North Air Ambulance were sent to the scene in South Shields, Tyne and Wear

View 3 Images BG freight line ship on the port of Tyne with a collapsed crane (Image: Newcastle Chronicle)

One person has been taken to hospital after a crane collapse at a port in England.

‌



Crews from various emergency services were sent to the scene of the incident at the Port of Tyne in South Shields, Tyne and Wear. The incident involved a dockside crane and took place this afternoon, at around 1.02pm.

‌



Crews from North East Ambulance Service and the Great North Air Ambulance were sent to respond to the incident after one person was injured. A spokesperson for North East Ambulance Service said: "We were called to an incident in which a person was injured at the Port of Tyne, South Shields, at 1.02pm on 19 July.

‌



"We dispatched three double crewed ambulances, two clinical team leaders, a duty officer, three vehicles from our Hazardous Area Response Team (HART) and were supported by Great North Air Ambulance Service. One patient was taken to the Royal Victoria Infirmary.

"One of our HART vehicles remains at the scene on standby to support the fire service." Photos from the scene show damage to a crane and several containers on a BG Freight Line vessel.

View 3 Images A picture of the damaged crane (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

‌



Mike, who runs YouTube channel Urbex Drone View, heard about the incident online and saw the aftermath, ChronicleLive reports. He saw the emergency services at the scene when he was approaching from the north of the River Tyne.

Mike said: "When I arrived on the north side to get some drone footage, I was met with the tangled wreckage of the dockside crane, highlighting the sheer force of the incident. Behind a line of emergency service vehicles, I could also see that several cargo containers aboard the BG Orange had been dislodged from their original positions, as shown in the accompanying photographs."

Mike added: "It was quite horrific to see something like that. You don’t know who’s injured. I think certainly a major incident was declared. The amount of emergency vehicles there: fire engines, ambulances, and from what I've heard two air ambulances were deployed."

Article continues below

View 3 Images A dockside crane lies on the container ship BG Orange operated by BG Freight Line (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

The drone operator continued: "Seeing the extent of the damage brought home just how serious the incident was. It is difficult to imagine what those working on the dock or aboard the vessel must have experienced at that moment.

"My thoughts are with everyone involved and their families, and I sincerely hope that all those affected are safe and receive the support they need."

News.title: Lewis Hamilton punishment confirmed after Belgian GP incident left F1 star with broken leg fear
News.content:
Lewis Hamilton punishment confirmed after Belgian GP incident left F1 star with broken leg fear

A frightening pit lane incident at the Belgian Grand Prix saw Lewis Hamilton accidentally drive into a member of Ferrari's crew, sparking worries of serious damage

View 2 Images Lewis Hamilton hit a mechanic (Image: X)

Ferrari have been fined £25,512 after Lewis Hamilton accidentally hit a crew member with his car during a terrifying pit lane accident at the Belgian Grand Prix. Hamilton was shown the green light during a pit stop, signalling that it was safe for him to pull away and get back onto the track at Spa-Francorchamps.

‌



However, the seven-time Formula 1 champion stopped just moments later after hitting a member of his crew with a car, immediately checking in on the mechanic via his team radio. While the member of staff fortunately didn't sustain any serious damage, Hamilton has since admitted that his heart sank as he quickly remembered how Kimi Raikkonen had broke a mechanic's leg in Bahrain in a similar incident.

‌



Speaking after the Belgian GP, Hamilton said: "The green light went, and so I went. You're looking over here [at the light] and not over there [at the mechanic].

‌



Lewis Hamilton punished at Belgian GP after taking out George Russell in first-lap crash READ MORE :

"That's more on the team, ultimately. But when it happened, I noticed him and I stopped and what went through my mind at that moment was when Kimi hit and broke the leg, and my heart really sank for a second."

While the mechanic thankfully was not hurt in the process, Ferrari were unable to escape punishment for the incident, with the FIA announcing a sizeable fine to go Scuderia's way.

A notice read: "The competitor (Scuderia Ferrari HP) is fined €30,000 of which €10,000 is suspended for 12 months on condition that the Competitor does not commit a similar infringement in the meantime and on the further condition that within 14 days the Competitor submits a report to the FIA regarding the incident and protocols introduced to mitigate the risk of such an incident occurring in the future."

‌



It added: "The Stewards heard from the team representative and reviewed video evidence. As Car 44 was being released from its pit stop, a mechanic stepped in the path of the front right tyre as the F1 Car moved forward. He fell but was not injured.

Sky broadcasts every practice, qualifier and race throughout the season, as well as exclusive coverage of the Premier League, EFL, darts and golf.

"The team explained the incident occurred in the context of a complex and unusual combination of circumstances. HAM had been issued a 5 second time penalty for a driving infringement which had to be served before work could commence on the F1 Car.

‌



"LEC was in his pit box at the point HAM entered the pit lane. HAM told his engineer that he wanted a front wing adjustment but that was not conveyed to the super controller.

"HAM came into his pit box, served the time penalty and at the end of the 5 seconds one member of the team announced 'Go' and then '0.6 degrees,' the former being an instruction to commence the pit stop and the latter being an instruction for a wing adjustment.

"The tyre change was completed, the jack-man dropped the F1 Car and the super controller activated the green light signal for Car 44 to move off. Just as the driver moved off, another mechanic with a front wing tool moved forward into the path of the front right tyre. Before he stepped forward he had his head down looking at the tool and did not see the green light.

‌



View 2 Images Lewis Hamilton finished fourth in Belgium (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

"The team acknowledged that for Car 44 to have been released in these circumstances was unsafe and attributed the error to an inappropriately late instruction for the wing adjustment, a lack of clear communication and the mechanic’s failure to notice the green light.

"The team committed to undertaking a review of their pit stop procedures to ensure an incident such as this will not be repeated. The Stewards determined that the driver was in no respect at fault."

Article continues below

Hamilton endured a fourth-place finish in Belgium, with Kimi Antonelli winning the race while Charles Leclerc and Max Verstappen managed podium placements. As a result, Hamilton sits second in the Drivers' Championship standings, 45 points behind Antonelli.

News.title: Dog owner allowed Jack Russells to balloon into the 'most overweight' RSPCA had seen
News.content:
Dog owner allowed Jack Russells to balloon into the 'most overweight' RSPCA had seen

Following an investigation from the RSPCA, 68-year-old William Johns, from Swansea, south Wales, has been banned from keeping animals for 15 years and handed a suspended prison sentence

View 4 Images Lily weighed 14.2kg and was the most overweight dog the RSPCA inspector had ever seen (Image: RSPCA)

A dog owner allowed two Jack Russell Terriers to reach levels of obesity an RSPCA inspector had ever seen.

‌



William Johns, 68, has been banned from keeping animals for 15 years and handed a suspended prison sentence after pleading guilty to two offences under the Animal Welfare Act 2006. He also received an eight-month custodial sentence, suspended for two years.

‌



The RSPCA, which brought the prosecution, found the terriers - called Cai and Lily - to be grossly overweight when they went to Johns' home in Swansea, south Wales. The largest of the two animals weighed 14.2kg, and was the most overweight dog a vet and an RSPCA inspector had ever seen.

‌



Speaking this month after the sentencing, RSPCA Inspector Gemma Cooper said: "These poor dogs were allowed to balloon in weight by the defendant's inability to provide a balanced diet for them. One of them became so ill that he had to be put to sleep and had we not returned to the property, the second dog may also have become seriously unwell.”

View 4 Images The two dogs were rescued from the man's home in Swansea, south Wales (Image: RSPCA)

The animal welfare charity said Cai was suffering from heart failure and was so unwell that a vet decided the best course of action was to put him down, Wales Online reported. Lily was taken into the charity's care during a later visit.

‌



RSPCA animal rescue officer Ethan Griffin visited the defendant's home on September 24 last year, the court was told. During the visit, the officer found Cai in a collapsed state, with urine stains over his body. The court heard Johns agreed to allow the officer to take the dog to a vet.

Later, during a follow-up visit, Johns was advised to take Lily to a vet to be weighed and placed on a diet - however, the defendant refused to cooperate with RSPCA officers at that time. On December 14, RSPCA Inspector Gemma Cooper and officers from South Wales Police visited the home.

View 4 Images Cai had heart failure, the RSPCA said (Image: RSPCA)

‌



On that occasion, Lily was seized - and in a statement presented to the court, the inspector admitted she was shocked by how large the dog was. "When I went to take her from the police officer, it was difficult to hold her like a normal dog, as her torso was just so rounded and solid. In my 15 years as an RSPCA inspector, I have never seen a dog so overweight," she said.

After examining Cai, a vet said the dog was in the end stage of heart failure. He was extremely overweight with a body condition score of nine out of nine - with five considered a healthy weight. Lily also had a body condition score of nine out of nine, and a vet who examined her said that she was out of breath most of the time she was at the clinic.

"She weighed 14.2 kgs and the level of obesity was one of the worst I have seen," he stated. "She had difficulty moving around, and by keeping a dog in this abnormal state, the owner failed in their duty of care to provide a suitable diet and control their pet's weight. The dog suffered for a prolonged period of at least a month if not longer."

‌



View 4 Images Lily has made a good recovery since she was put on a diet by the RSPCA - and the charity will now rehome her (Image: RSPCA)

Following the investigation, Lily was put on a diet and lost more than 2kg in the first month in the RSPCA's care. She has since made a good recovery and will be rehomed by the charity.

In mitigation, the court was told the defendant was unable to care for the dogs because of a range of health issues, including suffering from Parkinson's and reduced mobility after having had a leg amputated. He had later agreed to sign Lily over to the care of the RSPCA.

Article continues below

The dog owner was also told to pay £400 court costs and a victim surcharge of £187 at the hearing on June 22.

News.title: Man fighting for life after 'targeted' stabbing in Manchester city centre
News.content:
Man fighting for life after 'targeted' stabbing in Manchester city centre

City of Manchester officers were on patrol when they found the victim in the early hours of the morning on Peter Street, Deansgate

View 2 Images A police cordon remains in place on Peter Street (Image: Jason Roberts /Manchester Evening News)

A man is in hospital in critical condition after being stabbed in a "targeted attack" in Manchester city centre.

‌



The victim, a 31-year-old man, was found with stabbing injuries on Peter Street, Deansgate, where a number of bars and restaurants can be found. The discovery was made by City of Manchester officers who were on patrol at around 3.40am today.

‌



The victim received first aid before being taken to hospital. He remains in critical but stable condition, a statement from Greater Manchester Police said.

‌



While an investigation was launched, no arrested have yet been made. A police cordon remains in place at the scene of the incident.

View 2 Images Police at the scene of the stabbing on Peter Street, Deansgate (Image: Jason Roberts /Manchester Evening News)

Article continues below

Chief Inspector Mike Tachauer said: "Whilst no arrests have been made, I’d like to reassure residents and the wider community that we believe this was a targeted attack and there is no wider threat to the community. Our investigation is working at pace to establish those responsible for this.

"There is currently a scene in place around Peter Street and officers will continue to be in the area to provide reassurance." Anyone holding any information about the incident is asked to contact the police on 101, quoting incident number 531 of July 19.

Crimestoppers can also be contacted anonymously on 0800 555 111.

News.title: 'Everyday life is a living nightmare as an eyesore landfill site looms over our village'
News.content:
'Everyday life is a living nightmare as an eyesore landfill site looms over our village'

Residents in Duckmanton, Derbyshire, say their lives have been made a misery by the huge landfill site, which has grown to tower over the once-picturesque village

View 10 Images Amy Russell and Veronique Picard live near a landfill site near Duckmanton

Residents claim their lives are being made a misery by a massive "eyesore" landfill site which now looms over their village — bringing with it swarms of flies and enormous clouds of dust.

‌



Furious locals in Duckmanton, Derbyshire, have watched the foul-smelling site grow dramatically in size over the years to the point where it has now spread across the hillsides overlooking homes in the picturesque village.

‌



They claim plagues of flies descend upon their living rooms and kitchens on a daily basis, and that they are "prisoners in their own home" due to the sheer volume of dust which renders their gardens unusable.

‌



One mum told reporters her children ask why their home smells so bad, a question she finds particularly upset. Another Duckmanton resident said her "bins become a haven for maggots" during the summer.

Valencia, which manages Erin landfill, said it has increased its "dust suppression efforts and will continue to monitor its effectiveness on a daily basis".

New rubbish rules mean man has to bolt his bin closed READ MORE :

View 10 Images This landfill site near Duckmanton, Derbyshire, is said to be causing issues with flies, dust, and bad smells

‌



'No mother should have to answer that question'

The recent hot and dry spell has also made the relentless stench emanating from the landfill "completely unbearable", yet residents fear they are trapped in their homes as selling up would prove virtually impossible.

Villagers have also raised concerns about the thunderous machinery at the tip, which has grown taller and taller over the years and now dominates the skyline above Duckmanton.

Amy Jackson, a mum-of-four from Duckmanton, said: "As a mother raising children in this village, I am deeply distressed by the appalling conditions created by the landfill site on our doorstep.

‌



"What should be a safe and nurturing environment for my family has become a daily struggle. The persistent stench, swarms of flies, dust, and relentless noise have turned our home into a place of discomfort rather than refuge.

"During the recent hot weather, we were unable to open our windows because the odour was so overpowering. My children have had to endure stifling heat indoors, unable to play outside without flies landing on their food, their faces, and their toys.

"No parent should have to watch their children suffer in conditions like these. The situation has deteriorated to the point where the odour is now seeping into our home even with the windows closed. My children ask why our house smells so bad. No mother should have to answer that question."

‌



View 10 Images

Amy revealed she has forked out a "significant" sum on fly traps, sticky tapes, and other preventative measures "simply to keep the infestation at bay" – yet this hasn't proved sufficient and flies persist in causing problems.

She continued: "The flies remain everywhere, making normal family life impossible. The situation is not only unhygienic - it is degrading.

‌



"What was once a peaceful rural community has been overshadowed by a site that is entirely inappropriate for a location so close to homes, schools, and public spaces. It is unacceptable that children are being raised in conditions that pose risks to their physical and emotional health."

View 10 Images

'It has got to be a health hazard'

Mum-of-four Marie Norman, 54, a carer, explained the issue has aggravated her asthma and left her battling depression.

‌



She stated: "They've filled the holes to capacity but then don't cover them up so the rubbish has now risen all up the hillside. It has got to be a health hazard. I have to use my inhaler much more often.

"Due to breathing issues I can't have my windows closed but when they are open my house gets covered in dust. I lose count of how many flies are in my house at any one times and I can't even put my washing out. The whole thing has left me really down and depressed as it's no way to live really."

View 10 Images

‌



Gary Berresford, 38, from Duckmanton, revealed that swatting flies has become an unavoidable part of his daily morning routine.

Gary, whose home sits just 50 feet from the landfill site boundary, said his fly traps fill up within days and he has even purchased a Bug-A-Salt – a plastic gun that fires salt to dispatch flies.

He added: "Every morning a new batch of flies manage to find their way through the gaps in the windows into the house. A part of my morning ritual every day is having my coffee and going around shooting flies for about 20 minutes. And the dust is unreal."

‌



View 10 Images

'I don't see how they can safely contain the waste and smell now'

Gary, who has called Duckmanton home for 26 years, said the stench becomes "unbelievably bad" on hot and breezy days.

He added: "It's like when you have a cold and you put your head over a bowl of water with a tea towel over trying to clear your sinuses – the smell is so bad right now that it feels like I'm doing that over a dust bin.

‌



"The original hole has been filled and they're more moved across the site. Now instead of filling a hole they are just adding to a hillside. I don't see how they can safely contain the waste and smell now. I think it's already on the limit.

"If they go much higher now than what they're doing, the first serious rain we get, all that is going to flood over onto the surrounding countryside."

The problem is also taking its toll on residents in the neighbouring village of Long Duckmanton, situated just over a mile from the landfill site.

‌



View 10 Images

'Often in summer our bins become a haven for maggots'

Catherine McConologue, a mum-of-two, said: "Our cars are constantly covered in dust, the flies are horrendous, and the stench is absolutely awful.

"With the flies comes the issue of maggots and that's really disgusting. Often in summer our bins become a haven for maggots.

‌



"You have maggots in your bins and flies all over your kitchen, it's mortifying. Things have gradually gotten worse and worse over the last few years with the smell and the flies, and I am worried it's a risk to public health.

"We don't even have people over in summer unless it's family because it's embarrassing. I'm not from here, and when I moved here with my husband, I wasn't familiar with the area. If was moving now, I wouldn't move here because of the landfill.

"With the problems getting worse in the last few years, you have to wonder what it does to property prices because this is becoming a far more widely known issue."

‌



View 10 Images Fly catchers in a house near a landfill site near Duckmanton (Image: Charley Atkins / SWNS)

Another local resident, who wished to remain anonymous, was left with no choice but to flee her home due to the unbearable stench.

She said: "I woke up at 2am Sunday morning to an alarm going off from the direction of the landfill.

‌



"I started gagging from the smell. I shut all the windows in the house even though it was hot, put the air purifier on, and the fan.

"I was poorly all day Sunday. Monday morning I was violently stomach-wrenching from the smell, and I phoned my dad to come collect me.

"The electricity bill is high, running fans, purifiers and air freshener and it still doesn't get rid of the stench."

‌



View 10 Images The site has now spread to the hills overlooking the properties in the scenic village

'I'm like a prisoner in my own home'

Another Duckmanton resident remarked: "It's an absolute eyesore which looms over our homes and I'm like a prisoner in my own home as I can't even sit in my own garden without being covered in dust and flies."

The Erin landfill site first opened its doors in 1999 at the former colliery location. Initially run by Viridor, it was later acquired by Valencia, which currently manages the facility.

‌



The site was scheduled to shut in 2021 – but secured permission to continue operating until 2036. In recent days, Valencia obtained approval to begin operations in a newly engineered landfill cell.

Cllr Mick Bagshaw, Staveley Town Council member for Duckmanton Ward, confirmed he has fielded numerous complaints in recent days.

He stated: "Residents in Duckmanton and Poolsbrook deserve to enjoy their homes, gardens, and sunshine. The shouldn't have to put up with smells, continuous purchases of expensive fly traps and sprays and having to throw away meals because flies land on them.".

‌



View 10 Images Some residents said they are 'prisoners in their own home' due to the amount of dust caused by the waste

Chesterfield MP Toby Perkins has likewise received multiple reports from Duckmanton residents raising concerns about the landfill site. He stated: "I have heard from many local Duckmanton residents that during the current hot spell, the odours emitted from Erin Landfill have become unbearable, with residents saying they cannot open their windows in this extreme heat and have even been physically sick from the smell.

‌



"These reports are totally unacceptable, people should not have to live like this and if the landfill operators cannot address this smell, the regulator must step in and take action.

"In the extreme heat being unable to open your windows is unthinkable, and so the operator must take this situation seriously, if it wants to maintain a licence to operate."

What has Valencia said?

A spokesperson for Valencia commented: "We continue to operate the landfill site in accordance with our environmental permit and planning conditions, this includes ensuring that any dust and odour is controlled within the site.

‌



"During the recent heatwave we have increased our dust suppression efforts and will continue to monitor its effectiveness on a daily basis. The Environment Agency regularly visit the site on to inspect for evidence of flies and have not found an issue in recent weeks.

"We have also increased our daily cover activity to further ensure that ageing waste is not able to cause unpleasant odour issues for residents.

"We would like to apologise for any inconvenience that the landfill odour has caused. In recent days, Valencia has received approval to start operations in a newly engineered landfill cell.

‌



"As part of this, stockpiled waste is being exposed before being tipped into the new cell. The team onsite have responded to the increase in odour by closing the site to waste deliveries, and increasing soil capping to reduce odours.

"We anticipated that all waste will have been tipped, and covered in the coming days, with landfill gas infrastructure then extracting the gas. The Environment Agency are aware of the actions we have taken."

An Environment Agency spokesperson said: "We are pressing the operator to take steps to mitigate recent odour issues at this site.

Article continues below

"The situation is gradually improving and operations on site are now focused solely on resolving this issue. Communities should not have to tolerate odours, and we understand the impact this can have.

"We are inspecting the site regularly and if we do not see improvements, we will not hesitate to take enforcement action if required."

News.title: Andy Burnham to promise 'more breathing space' on cost of living in first address to nation as PM
News.content:
Andy Burnham to promise 'more breathing space' on cost of living in first address to nation as PM

The pledge from the new Labour leader comes as he is expected to announce a policy blitz in his first week in No10 to help ease the pressure on cash-strapped households

View 3 Images Andy Burnham will deliver his first speech as Prime Minister on Monday (Image: ANDY RAIN/EPA/Shutterstock)

Andy Burnham will promise to “give Britain more breathing space” on the cost of living in his first major address to the nation as Prime Minister.

‌



The pledge from the new Labour leader comes as he is expected to announce a policy blitz in his first week in No10 to help ease the pressure on cash-strapped households.

‌



The ex-Greater Manchester Mayor will also acknowledge the turbulence in British politics as he replaces Keir Starmer just two years after Labour’s election victory.

‌



In his first speech to the country, he will insist he is “acutely conscious” of the chaos and being the sixth Prime Minister in 10 years to walk up the street, and stress the need for more stable and responsible politics.

Mr Burnham will also describe the moment as one of "reflection and resolution" and insist the country must be honest about the challenges it faces.

Labour’s deputy leader, Lucy Powell, insisted on Sunday he will set out a “bolder more ambitious” vision for fixing Britain’s thorny problems.

‌



Andy Burnham's 10 major challenges and headaches as he enters No10 as PM READ MORE :

View 3 Images Andy Burnham will be the sixth PM in 10 years when he replaces Keir Starmer (Image: Getty Images)

This includes the crisis-hit social care sector, which he promised last week to “expend quite a lot of political capital” on.

Allies also said he will conclude his speech on a message of optimism, after telling Labour members last week he wanted to give voters “hope back”.

‌



Mr Burnham will become Prime Minister after Mr Starmer formally offers his resignation to the King at Buckingham Palace around lunchtime on Monday.

The new Labour leader will then “kiss hands” with the monarch, who will then invite him to form the next government - before setting out his vision to the country outside Downing Street.

After addressing the nation, he will be greeted by the Cabinet Secretary, Dame Antonia Romeo, behind the famous black door before receiving briefings from officials.

‌



The former Greater Manchester Mayor, who spent the weekend with his family and putting the finishing touches to his Cabinet, will then announce his top team.

There has been feverish speculation over the role of Chancellor, with Shabana Mahmood, the current Home Secretary, widely tipped to replace Rachel Reeves.

It has sparked tensions among some on the left of the party, who are hoping the position will go to the former leader and Energy Secretary, Ed Miliband.

‌



The incoming Prime Minister is also expected to receive congratulatory calls from world leaders, including US President Donald Trump.

WASPI new hope as Andy Burnham set to meet campaign over redress options READ MORE :

View 3 Images Andy Burnham was crowned Labour leader on Friday (Image: Henry Nicholls/Pool AFP via AP)

On Sunday, Mr Trump claimed people in Aberdeen will be “dancing in the streets” following reports Mr Burnham could back new oil and gas drilling in the North Sea.

‌



Mr Burnham has not confirmed reports that he is considering approving new fossil fuel production, particularly in the North Sea’s Rosebank and Jackdaw fields.

But in a post on his Truth Social platform on Sunday, Mr Trump, a vocal supporter of fossil fuels, prematurely claimed Mr Burnham had said he would.

He said: “The People of Aberdeen, in Scotland, are dancing in the streets because the new Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, has stated that he will be opening up, all the way, the invaluable North Sea Oil!”

‌



Reports over the weekend also suggested Mr Burnham to put crisis-hit Thames Water - which is battling a £20 billion debt pile - into a special administration regime (SAR).

The ex-Greater Manchester Mayor has previously said he wants to see more public control of key utilities, including water.

On Sunday, Labour’s deputy leader Ms Powell - a close ally and friend of Mr Burnham - also fuelled speculation by saying privatisation of water “hasn’t worked”.

‌



She told Sky News: "This has been an ongoing issue and concern in government and has been around for many months now.

“The government has powers to bring a distressed water company under special measures, and let's see if the government needs to - wants to - use those powers.”

Promising a “reset of priorities”, Mr Burnham has already announced over the weekend he will scrap Mr Starmer’s flagship digital ID programme in order to focus money and attention on the cost of living.

‌



Earlier this month he also announced plans for the biggest council house building programme since the post-war era.

And he has already said he wants to devolve power away from Westminster as one of his key priorities, driving that agenda with a new “No 10 North” in Manchester, which he is expected to visit later in the week.

The Mayor of West Yorkshire, Tracy Brabin, said the new Labour leader’s plans to establish a No10 North was a “game-changer”.

Article continues below

She told the BBC : “It’s not just a gimmick, it’s not vacuous, it’s absolutely about taking power from the South and putting it in a different part of the country so that we govern for the whole country.”

News.title: Two British Eventing riders, 34 and 42, die at horse events on same day
News.content:
Two British Eventing riders, 34 and 42, die at horse events on same day

British Eventing has announced the deaths of riders Sophie Fouracre and Kerry Donoghue following separate incidents on Saturday

View Image Two people have died at separate horse events (Image: Getty Images)

Two horse riders have died following separate incidents at events held on the same day. British Eventing has announced the deaths of riders Sophie Fouracre and Kerry Donoghue following separate incidents on Saturday.

‌



Fouracre, 34, was fatally injured in a cross-country accident riding Rhubarbsfox Brittania at Swalcliffe Park in Oxfordshire.

‌



Donoghue, 42, died hours later following a cross-country accident riding Carneyhaugh Rua at Penrith, Cumbria.

‌



In accordance with British Eventing procedures, comprehensive reviews of the accidents will be undertaken, reports PA.

Both horses were examined by vets and found to be uninjured.

Article continues below

British Eventing chief executive Rosie Williams said in a statement: “The British Eventing community is heartbroken.

“On behalf of everyone at British Eventing, I want to extend our deepest condolences to Kerry and Sophie’s families, friends and loved ones at this devastating time.

“The loss of two members of our eventing family on the same day is almost beyond words, and we know the sadness of these events will be felt profoundly across the sport for some time to come.”

News.title: Girl, 14, dubbed 'true heroine' as she risks her life to try to save drowning boy
News.content:
Girl, 14, dubbed 'true heroine' as she risks her life to try to save drowning boy

Shelby Quigley jumped into the River Wyre in Lancashire to try to save 15-year-old Lotus Bowker from drowning — the teen's courage has now been recognised with a rarely awarded honour

View 3 Images Shelby Quigley has been awarded with a bravery medal

A teenager has received a bravery award after she risked her own life to save a drowning boy.

‌



Shelby Quigley jumped into the river after seeing 15-year-old Lotus Bowker disappear below the surface. Shelby, 14, removed her heavy clothing and walking boots, plunged into the River Wyre and managed to drag the boy to the surface against strong currents.

‌



She held him above the water despite being repeatedly submerged herself, until a man entered the river and helped drag the boy to the bank, where attempts were made to resuscitate him. The boy was taken to the hospital, where he tragically passed away the following day.

‌



But Shelby, who was participating in a Duke of Edinburgh Bronze Expedition at the time, was praised for her courage and selflessness at the time and now the youngster, of Lytham St Annes, Lancashire, has been given a rare honour.

View 3 Images Lotus Bowker tragically died in hospital the following day (Image: Gofundme)

Shelby has been recognised with the Royal Humane Society Silver Medal - a rarely awarded honour for exceptional courage in saving, or attempting to save, a life. Andrew Chapman, Secretary of the Royal Humane Society, praised the girl's actions and said she gave the boy the best possible chance of survival, Lancs Live reported.

‌



"What she did was truly incredible for one so young," he said. "Sadly the boy died in hospital later but without doubt Shelby gave him the best possible chance of survival. Few people would have persisted in the way she did when they were so close to drowning themselves.

"Somehow though she stayed calm and showed incredible bravery. Very few people are awarded our silver medals but she richly deserves it. She was a true heroine."

An inquest carried out after Lotus' death heard that the teen went into the River Wyre near Garstang Cricket Club with three friends on May 17, 2025, despite being told not to by his parents, as he could not swim properly and was only able to doggy paddle.

‌



Lotus, from Kirkham, Lancashire, had a Developmental Learning Disorder, which meant he had some communication issues and "didn't know risk", but he tried to deal with the condition by "copying his peers," and his mum, Andromeda, also said he was "easily led".

View 3 Images Andrew Chapman praised the girl's actions (Image: MPCT)

The coroner said that Shelby took care not to jump to avoid cold water shock and swam over to where Lotus was. "She managed to hold him at the top of the water but she was really struggling and she had to let him go," the coroner said.

‌



Neil Quinn was walking past with his family when he saw Shelby attempting to save Lotus. He managed to get Lotus to the bank after he had been under the water for around eight minutes. The two then started CPR.

Off-duty anaesthetist Steve Wiggans, who works at Blackpool Teaching Hospitals, also happened to be passing. He used equipment from a police officer's first aid kit to remove vomit from Lotus's stomach and airway. The boy was first taken to the Royal Preston Hospital and had a spontaneous return of circulation prior to arriving.

He had been in cardiac arrest for 28 minutes. He was also severely hypothermic with a core body temperature of just 30.6C. Lotus was then transferred to the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital. In the early hours of Sunday, May 18, he suffered two more cardiac arrests, and doctors advised his parents that he would continue to worsen and had likely suffered a severe brain injury due to a lack of oxygen.

Article continues below

He suffered a third cardiac arrest at 5.25am and was pronounced dead at 5.35am. The cause of death was recorded as drowning, with the Developmental Learning Disorder listed as a contributory factor.

News.title: Burnham to promise 'more breathing room' in first speech as PM
News.content:
Andy Burnham will promise to give people "more breathing room" when he gives his first speech as prime minister outside No 10 on Monday.

He is expected to say he is "acutely conscious" of the UK's high turnover of prime ministers - and that politics needs to be more stable and responsible.

And he is expected to characterise the moment as one of "reflection and resolution", arguing Britain must be honest about the challenges it faces.

Burnham will officially replace Sir Keir Starmer and become the UK's 59th prime minister - and seventh in 10 years - on Monday, following a meeting with King Charles III.

Earlier, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said the incoming prime minister was a "people pleaser" at a time when the country needed someone who could "take tough decisions, who can face down Labour MPs".

"The job is not a popularity contest. It is making the lives of all of the people outside this building better. And he has not said what he's going to do. It's all airy-fairy stuff," she said.

Burnham was officially declared Labour Party leader on Friday following a short contest in which he was the only candidate, having secured the backing of 379 MPs.

Some opposition parties have urged Burnham to call a general election in order to ensure he has a mandate for his premiership.

However, earlier Labour's deputy leader Lucy Powell insisted Burnham would stick to the promises made in Labour's manifesto in the 2024 general election but will be more ambitious.

"He really understands the bigger, bolder measures that are needed to live up to the manifesto promises," she told the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg programme.

In his maiden speech on Monday morning, Burnham will reportedly set out his domestic priorities.

The Makerfield MP and former mayor of Greater Manchester is expected to argue that political stability must deliver "tangible" improvements along with "giving people more breathing room" on the cost of living.

But it is not yet clear who Burnham will appoint in his top team. He is expected to start appointing his senior ministers once inside No 10.

There has been fevered speculation as to who will get which job, particularly the crucial position of chancellor.

Energy Secretary Ed Miliband had initially appeared the most likely candidate, but in recent days Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has emerged as another potential replacement for Rachel Reeves at the Treasury.

News.title: Record numbers of honours for working class heroes
News.content:
"I always had the perception that you only got an honour if you were rich or famous," says Clive Lawrence.

His start in life had been free school meals and growing up on a council estate in Derbyshire, but the former head teacher has been made an Officer of the British Empire (OBE).

He's part of a quiet revolution in the honours system, which has deliberately sought to make the awards less socially exclusive and to have a fairer spread of winners around the country.

That change followed an analysis by the BBC last year of the New Year Honours in 2025 which showed that among higher winners - such as Commanders of the British Empire (CBE), knighthoods and damehoods - only 4% of recipients had grown up in working class backgrounds.

Cabinet Office figures for the New Year Honours 2026 show that for higher awards that has now risen to 31%, a record level.

News.title: Bruno Mars has an unexpected opening before Wembley party starts
News.content:
Bruno Mars appeared determined to lift the nation's mood during the first of his six nights at Wembley Stadium.

His last UK performance came in July 2018, shortly after England had been knocked out of the men's World Cup semi-finals. Eight years later, history had repeated itself.

But wearing an England football scarf, Union Jack bucket hat and clutching a Paddington Bear, the showman energised a 75,000-strong, multi-generational crowd.

After nearly a decade away from UK audiences, Mars proved why fans had snapped up tickets in record numbers, external.

News.title: Chinese firm seeks compensation over British Steel nationalisation
News.content:
The former owner of British Steel has said it will pursue the British government for compensation after the loss-making firm was nationalised.

The UK took control of the Scunthorpe steelworks a year ago after China's Jingye Group said it planned to close the site because it was not financially viable, and fully nationalised the plant on Thursday.

In a statement on Sunday, Jingye said it will seek "full compensation through legal means to the very end" over the UK's move.

A government spokesperson said draft compensation regulations due to be released in the autumn will set out a compensation process through which an independent assessor "would determine what, if any, is payable".

Jingye bought the Lincolnshire steel plant in 2020, but in March last year the firm launched a consultation on its closure saying the plant was losing Â£700,000 a day.

The government took control of British Steel operations in April 2025, but until this week it remained under Jingye's ownership which limited the government's ability to shape the firm's future.

On Thursday the UK government said it was taking the firm into public hands in order to safeguard a "vital national capability", giving the government the power to decide the plant's future.

The decision to nationalise British Steel has threatened to strain the relationship between London and Beijing just as Andy Burnham prepares to enter Downing Street as prime minister on Monday.

News.title: Digital ID plan to be scrapped in Burnham's first major policy pledge
News.content:
"This reprioritisation of public resource shows a change in direction towards improving everyday life and strengthening local economies over expensive national government schemes."

Plans for a digital ID scheme had initially been introduced by Sir Keir ahead of Labour's conference last year.

At the time, he argued that mandatory digital ID for workers would make it easier to clamp down on immigrants working illegally and modernise the state.

As well as tackling illegal immigration, Sir Keir said a digital ID system would enable citizens to prove identity to access key services quickly instead of having to hunt for utility bills.

The Office for Budget Responsibility estimated last November that the programme would cost Â£1.8bn over three years, but Downing Street rejected this figure.

In January, after nearly three million people signed a parliamentary petition opposing the introduction of digital IDs, the government changed its approach.

Instead, ministers ditched the compulsory part of the scheme and relaunched it as voluntary, saying digital IDs could eventually allow people to do everything from managing their childcare to filling in tax returns on a "one stop" app.

Soon after, Home Affairs Committee Chair Dame Karen Bradley said the government was right to introduce digital ID but had botched the launch.

In a report setting out the committee's investigation into the launch and subsequent changes to the policy, Dame Karen called attempts to set out the plans "nothing short of a fiasco" which "raised fears of government over-reach into people's lives".

Burnham will become prime minister after meeting with King Charles III on Monday, and his office said "one of the first things this government will do is put its focus where people need it right now".

Scrapping digital ID, the spokesperson said, will mean "redirecting the resources earmarked for the scheme towards people's everyday priorities".

Speaking to Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, deputy Labour leader and Burnham ally Lucy Powell said the money saved by scrapping the scheme was "not an insignificant amount" and would be "reprioritised and redistributed in different ways".

"But it's not just about the money - it's actually about the attention and the focus, so that the whole of government machinery can work in service of the agenda and the vision that the Labour government is setting out under Andy Burnham," she said.

News.title: Messi on the brink of history - will it be his last World Cup game?
News.content:
If Messi decides to carry on with Argentina to 2030, then he would become the oldest outfield player to appear at a World Cup, at the age of 43 - unless, of course, Cristiano Ronaldo opts to keep going for Portugal.

Not only could Messi add a new record to his long list, but he would have the chance to play in one of the centenary matches held in Argentina at the start of the next World Cup.

Spanish football expert Guillem Balague doesn't think this is the last fans will be seeing of Messi at the World Cup.

"Even if you hear it is the end, I doubt it but we'll see. I just see him with the national side, simply because he enjoys it," he said.

"I don't see him being at Inter Miami in the MLS, still performing and then saying that's it and he's going to play out the rest of his career with Inter Miami."

Messi's 2026 World Cup has been nothing short of sensational. He has scored eight goals in seven games - two goals behind tournament top scorer Mbappe - and has carried Argentina into the final with a series of virtuoso performances.

Argentina boss Scaloni hailed Messi as the greatest player ever, saying: "He is history, a legend. I feel proud, he is the best footballer the world has ever seen and reaching a final at 39 is something unbelievable - and that is why I said we must enjoy him.

"With Diego Maradona, we still miss him but Messi is still with us so we must enjoy him.

"I have no idea if this is Leo's last game, you will have to ask him. We haven't discussed it."

His displays in North America continue a quite remarkable late career resurgence for Messi at World Cups. Fifteen of his 21 tournament goals have come since his 35th birthday.

Having already lifted the World Cup in Qatar in 2022, Messi showed he had the motivation to keep going in 2026. The question is whether that continues to 2030.

"I feel that he hasn't said the last word yet," said Balague. "He finishes games, 120-minute games, at 39.

"In the first 90 minutes against Cape Verde, he covered 6.5km and 62% of that is walking.

"You can add a bit more walking. The passion is still there. All of that means he's not going to leave the national side."

There is also the factor of Messi playing at a World Cup in front of a home crowd.

The 2030 World Cup will have six host nations. While the majority of matches will take place in Spain, Portugal and Morocco, at least one game will be played in each of Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay. A world stage game in front of an Argentine crowd may be too much for Messi to resist.

Messi himself hinted that the 2022 final would be his international swansong.

"I am very happy for finishing my journey in World Cups in a final, to play the last game in a final. That is really very gratifying," he said before the 2022 showpiece.

"There are a lot of years from this year to the next one. I don't think I will be able to do that. To finish this way is brilliant."

That has obviously proved to not be the case. So regardless of what might be said after the 2026 final, keep an eye on 2030.

News.title: I've been a World Cup official - I promise you there is no favouritism
News.content:
Conspiracy theories and accusations of bias cause real damage and lead to abuse for referees. It can be difficult to deal with.

Pierluigi Collina, who oversees all the referees at the World Cup, had to issue a defence of his referees after Argentina's 3-2 win over Egypt in the last 16. He underlined their integrity and independence.

Egypt had made strong accusations that referee Francois Letexier and his team had deliberately favoured Argentina. That they had in some way been instructed to go against their natural instincts.

Collina was right to say that narrative can lead to threats against a referee's family, and I've seen it before myself.

I'm very lucky that it did not happen to me personally, but I think it's partly because I'm an assistant referee and not a referee.

We officiated the final between Spain and the Netherlands in 2010. A proud day for us all.

The game, which Spain won 1-0, was extremely challenging to officiate. There were 14 yellow cards and Dutch defender Johnny Heitinga was sent off. Nigel de Jong could have seen red too.

There was a lot of criticism from Netherlands coach Bert van Marwijk. That is what you have to deal with just for making genuine decisions.

Sometimes it is worse than that. Our own English referees at this World Cup, Michael Oliver and Anthony Taylor, have received threats in past years.

It is totally unacceptable and it is heightened by these unfounded whispers which question a referee's impartiality.

I support England, I love England, and obviously we lost to Argentina.

The referee was, in my opinion, a little bit too lenient in the first 25 minutes. But ultimately, the reason why we're not in the World Cup final is not down to the referee.

Really, it's frustrating when you hear about conspiracy theories.

I can't think of many other professions in the world where there is one person with all that pressure on them.

The referee is making multi-million-pound decisions - and they have got one second to make their mind up.

Mistakes have been made on the pitch, of course they have. But they do not add up to a conspiracy.

In thr group stage, I think Germany's goal against Ecuador should have been disallowed for a high foot. Ghana could have been awarded a penalty against England for a mistimed challenge by Ezri Konsa. And when they were 1-0 up against Scotland, Brazil scored a goal that should have been allowed to stand, but was ruled out.

There have been 103 matches so far. That's effectively 10 rounds of Premier League football, isn't it? So, of course, there are going to be errors made. It's almost impossible to go through that many games without one.

Slovenian referee Slavko Vincic will take charge of Sunday's final.

It will be the pinnacle of his career. You only need to look at his emotional reaction when Collina read out his name at the referee briefing the other day.

Having been fortunate enough to officiate a World Cup final myself, I can assure you that that Vincic will not care one jot who wins.

All he'll be hoping for is what every referee hopes for, and that is to come off the field without any incorrect decisions that impact the result.

That will be all he cares for.

All these conspiracy theories are bogus.

The only thing in your mind, I assure you, is getting the decisions correct.

Darren Cann was speaking to BBC Sport's Dale Johnson.

News.title: Trump presence means tight security for World Cup final
News.content:
Supporters faced long queues to get into New York New Jersey Stadium amid heightened security for the 2026 World Cup final.

Spain face Argentina at the 82,500-seater venue, with kick-off at 15:00 local time (20:00 BST).

There is increased security partly because United States president Donald Trump is attending the final - the only World Cup match he is watching in person.

As a result, the United States Secret Service took over security for the game - leading to long waits for supporters to get into the ground.

BBC Sport understands people were having to queue for about two hours.

But after the long queues, it is understood most fans had no issues scanning tickets and accessing the stadium.

News.title: Burnham will be bolder but stick to Labour manifesto, deputy leader says
News.content:
Burnham was officially declared Labour Party leader on Friday following a short contest in which he was the only candidate, having secured the backing of 379 MPs.

Some opposition parties have urged Burnham to call a general election in order to ensure he has a mandate for his premiership.

However, Powell insisted Burnham would stick to the promises made in Labour's manifesto in the 2024 general election.

"Our manifesto did talk about the redistribution of power, it did talk about the rewiring of our country, it did talk about taking on some of those vested interests," she said.

"He [Burnham] really understands the bigger, bolder measures that are needed to live up to the manifesto promises."

She also said his leadership was a chance to "reset" and that scrapping the digital ID scheme was a "small example of reprioritising".

In one of his first announcements since becoming Labour leader, Burnham said he would ditch the plan announced by Sir Keir last year.

Powell said the scheme would have cost a "not insignificant amount of money" but would also have diverted attention from the government's priorities.

Separately, the BBC has been told Burnham's government will announce plans for new oil and gas drilling in the North Sea.

Powell said Burnham would be "pragmatic" on the subject, adding: "I don't think it's a change of policy. It's more a change of emphasis."

US President Donald Trump applauded the move, writing on social media that tapping into North Sea oil resources would make the UK "one of the Richest Countries anywhere in the World".

The announcement is expected to be part of a package of measures including plans to take water and energy companies under public control and a new council house-building programme.

Burnham has previously said he wants to see "greater public control" of the water and energy sectors and has called for Thames Water to be nationalised.

In her interview with the BBC, Powell also backed increased public ownership, arguing the economy had been "overly privatised" and the "utilities and essentials of life don't work in the interest of ordinary people".

She said bills were "going up and up because they are run in the interests of private interest, not for the consumers or for taxpayers".

But, speaking to the same programme, former Conservative minister Jacob Rees-Mogg said: "The water industry needs private capital or it has to have taxpayers' money - no other money is available."

News.title: Britain 'set for bumper year' for butterflies
News.content:
A butterfly charity says the UK could be set for a "bumper" year of the insects as it launches its annual appeal for the public to count them.

Butterfly Conservation, based at East Lulworth, in Dorset, said the hot and dry spring meant it was already seeing an increase in several species.

On Friday, it launched its Big Butterfly Count, a yearly event asking members of the public to report the butterflies they see.

Dr Dan Hoare, director of nature recovery at Butterfly Conservation, said it was an opportunity for them to "colonise and reach out to new places".

"I have seen three or four species in the south of England... wandering away from their normal places," he said.

News.title: Is Burnham promising a new dawn for North Sea oil and gas?
News.content:
The final weekend before Andy Burnham enters Downing Street is being dominated by suggestions he'll announce plans for new drilling in the North Sea.

On Saturday, the BBC reported the in-coming prime minister would stick to the party's 2024 manifesto pledge to issue no new oil and gas licences but would honour existing ones.

That line has been confirmed as the hours count down to the Burnham premiership.

Speaking on Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, Labour's deputy leader Lucy Powell said Burnham would stick to the party's manifesto commitments, but there would be a "change of emphasis" on North Sea oil and gas.

"We've been really clear that the way to achieve in the long term energy security and lower bills is by ensuring that we do have our own homegrown, clean, much cheaper energy," she said.

"But we've been absolutely clear that North Sea gas and oil is an important part of that transition.

"It's an important part of the mix, and I think what Andy's talking about is taking a more pragmatic approach and working with the industry to make sure that it can contribute to that [energy] transition and to the mix that is needed over the long term."

News.title: Parts of UK to get break in heatwave but dry spell to continue
News.content:
Cooler temperatures are on the way for some parts of the UK after a first half of summer dominated by warm, sunny and largely dry weather.

Parts of England have experienced more than two weeks of heatwave conditions, and some central areas have had the longest dry spell since 1997.

But the third heatwave of 2026 is now easing as northerly winds introduce some fresher air - although most places still won't have any significant rainfall.

The slightly cooler spell may be very brief for some parts of southern England and south Wales, where we could see heatwave criteria being reached again later this week.

News.title: Twins share uni, course, grade and graduation day
News.content:
Ainsley said going through university with his brother had made the experience "a lot easier".

"It's kind of like going with a best friend but he's my brother and we can spend even more time together," he said.

Despite being a support for one another, Ainsley said they had a healthy level of competition during their studies.

"We always end up thinking we have to one-up each other. We made these small bets, where if I got a higher grade than him he would have to buy me a McDonalds, for example, it was those little things that made the competitiveness."

Adrian, who is older than Ainsley by a minute, said the competition helped push him academically.

"At the end of the day, we do wish each other the best. Obviously, we always aim to go high in our grades but it's just a bit of a light-hearted thing to push us more.

"I had a couple of exams and assignments where I did lower than Ainsley but that's what pushed me."

Graduating together made it easier for their parents, as they followed one after another in the ceremony.

"It felt surreal. Even from the get-go being able to get ready with my brother for our big day, seeing ourselves together, I felt proud.

"Walking down that aisle hearing my name was great, and knowing my brother was right behind felt great," said Adrian.

For now, the brothers are continuing to stick together as they begin internships â¯in Milton Keynes.

"The only time we'll be separated is in an actual job now," said Ainsley.

News.title: I'll lose my bowel because my pain was dismissed until my husband spoke up
News.content:
An operation nearly 20 years ago left Donna Davies in constant pain but she only felt believed by medics after her husband spoke up.

Donna, 56, now requires her large bowel to be removed because of her vaginal mesh medical device, which was removed after she felt it cutting into her.

It was fitted after Donna, from Swansea, developed stress urinary incontinence in her 30s, and the procedure has since been paused by the NHS.

She was invited to attend a women's health summit in Wales this week, which looked at how women's pain is too often dismissed as "normal" within healthcare.

Donna is one of an estimated 100,000 women in the UK who had the procedure to treat incontinence or prolapse.

She said: "The mesh was leaving me in daily pain - the only way I can explain it was that I was being cut by glass every time I moved.

"I didn't feel as if I was believed and I didn't feel my pain was acknowledged until my husband spoke up about an incident we had and then I felt that the surgeon believed my husband."

The device was eventually removed and a "sling" made from her own muscles was created at the same time as a total hysterectomy.

"I've never recovered from this operation - I'm still in constant pain, neuropathic pain as well and sadly I'm about to lose my large bowel and have a permanent stoma.

"I feel that women in Wales are being forgotten. There are no specialist services in Wales for women like myself, yet nine specialist centres in England - we do feel forgotten."

Delyth Jewell, the women's health minister in the Senedd, said she wanted rules to be strengthened so that health boards are required to include women in the design of services for them.

"I am determined to strengthen women's voices so that women will be believed about their bodies," the minister said at the women's health summit.

"I wonder how many women will have heard the words 'this might hurt' when they go to the doctor?

"That shouldn't be normal. Too often women's health services are considered a 'should' not a 'must'.

"We need to make sure that in theatre space they are prioritised more, we need to be making sure that training is improved."

News.title: Eight released over alleged threat to Islamic event
News.content:
Eight more people have been freed from custody, as police continue to investigate an alleged extreme right-wing threat to an Islamic event in Suffolk.

Officers became aware of the threat to the UK Ijtima event at Shrubland Hall, near Ipswich, last weekend.

Thousands of people attended the gathering but it closed early on police advice.

The Metropolitan Police said on Saturday, external that seven men were released from custody without charge, while another man was released on bail with strict conditions pending further inquiries.

The force said the investigation involved searching homes and vehicles, and more than 35 digital devices were seized.

Following those searches, a 42-year-old man was charged with two counts of possession of offensive weapons, extendable batons, and possession of a stun gun.

Police said the charges were not believed to be connected to the alleged threat on UK Ijtima.

The man was remanded in custody to appear at Reading Magistrates' Court on Monday.

Four other people were previously released on bail pending further inquiries.

News.title: Woman killed while asleep with baby ‘was my world’, sister says
News.content:
The sister of a 24-year-old mother who was stabbed and killed as she lay in bed with her husband and baby in west London has said "she was my world".

Kirandeep Kaur, who was originally from India, was fatally attacked at her home in Hayes on 12 July.

Speaking through a translator from the Majha region of Punjab, India, her sister Gursharan told BBC London: "She is everything for me, she video calls me and my mum. What are we going to do without her?"

A man has been charged with Kaur's murder.

Gursharan, who is 21, said her sister came to London looking for a better job so she could support her family.

"My sister moved to the UK in September 2024 to study at Buckinghamshire New University.

"She completed her studies and worked at a grocery store.

"We spoke to each other on the phone. But she hasn't been back, so I haven't seen her.

"When she reached London, she told me it was beautiful and she was happy."

Gusharan said her sister was "very intelligent".

"She was the top of her class here in India when she was studying, she's a very hard worker. She loved us all very much.

"Our family is very poor. She always thinks about us first. She was very supportive to me. She was my world. My heart hurts."

News.title: Kimi Antonelli extends F1 title lead after emotional George Russell crashes out
News.content:

Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. An emotional George Russell said he has grown “numb to disappointment” after he crashed out of the opening lap of a Belgian Grand Prix won by championship rival Kimi Antonelli.

Antonelli cleared Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc with 10 laps remaining at Spa-Francorchamps to take his sixth win of the season, and double his title advantage over Russell from 25 points to 50.

Leclerc, unable to follow up his British Grand Prix triumph a fortnight ago with another win, crossed the line 1.9 seconds back from Antonelli with Red Bull’s Max Verstappen third.

open image in gallery Kimi Antonelli claimed his sixth win of the season in Belgium ( Reuters )

Lewis Hamilton finished fourth. He endured an eventful afternoon in the Ardennes, first colliding with Russell – for which he was sanctioned with a five-second penalty – before he ran over his own mechanic in the pit lane when he was erroneously given the green light to rejoin the track. The mechanic appeared to escape without significant injury.

Hamilton was able to take advantage of Russell’s demise to move back up to second in the championship, albeit now 45 points behind the impressive Antonelli.

Antonelli, not 20 until next month, might have started from pole but he had to work for his win after Leclerc benefited from a Virtual Safety Car and was able to assume the lead of the race.

Leclerc’s advantage stood at three seconds, but Antonelli reeled the Monegasque in before blasting past the Ferrari on the Kemmel Straight on the 34th lap and keeping him at arm’s length for the remainder of the fixture.

Antonelli’s fine victory compounded a disastrous afternoon for Russell, who has now failed to score in three of the 10 rounds so far, and has just two wins to Antonelli’s six.

Russell qualified third and started well, but another mechanical glitch in his Mercedes saw him gobbled up by Verstappen, Oscar Piastri and Hamilton on the 200mph opening stampede to Les Combes.

open image in gallery George Russell spins out of the race after contact with Lewis Hamilton

Russell drew back alongside Hamilton under braking for the right-left combination, and then briefly ahead, but he was not afforded enough room by his former Mercedes teammate.

Top 10 – Belgian Grand Prix 1. Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) 2. Charles Leclerc (Ferrari) 3. Max Verstappen (Red Bull) 4. Lewis Hamilton (Ferrari) 5. Oscar Piastri (McLaren) 6. Isack Hadjar (Red Bull) 7. Lando Norris (McLaren) 8. Gabriel Bortoleto (Audi) 9. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) 10. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)

The left-front tyre of Hamilton’s Ferrari made contact with the rear-right of Russell’s Mercedes, sending the latter out of control and into the gravel trap. Russell’s race was instantly over.

“The incident with Lewis was a racing incident,” said a downcast Russell. “He didn’t do it on purpose. He was more to blame than I. But he didn’t do anything reckless.

“I was just angry I was in that position in the first place. I got a great start and I was ready to fight the two guys ahead of me up to turn five, and instead, I get swamped by three drivers because of another problem.

“I am numb to the disappointment. When it happens so often you just get used to it.”

The safety car was deployed after the first-lap drama, and the race resumed on lap five with Antonelli in control. It remained that way until the sole round of stops with Leclerc, the last of the leading trio to stop, capitalising on a VSC deployed for debris, to take the lead.

open image in gallery Lewis Hamilton endured a chaotic afternoon ( Getty )

However, Leclerc could not prevent Antonelli from blasting past to take his first win since the Monaco Grand Prix on 7 June and lay down another championship marker.

Hamilton leapfrogged Piastri on the 40th lap but has lost another 13 points to Antonelli in his bid for a record eighth world title. Lando Norris started 13th following an engine penalty and drove back to seventh, a position behind Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar. Oscar Piastri finished fifth.

“It is great to be back on the top step after a few difficult rounds,” said Antonelli. “It was a hard-fought race. We lost the first place with the VSC, but we made our way back. But it was a tough win because Charles was quick and we had to hold on to that.

“The [championship] momentum was always there. It was just about getting the results and today we were a bit lucky, in terms of what happened in the championship, but you have to take every opportunity because we can see how much it can swing. We have to keep performing, getting the results, and we will see what happens at the end of the year.”

News.title: This 28-storey London hotel offers panoramic views of the capital
News.content:

This five-star hotel near Hyde Park is the tallest building in Mayfair, looking out over landmarks including Buckingham Palace and The Shard

Location

Located less than a 10-minute walk from both Hyde Park Corner and Green Park Tube stations (albeit in different directions), London Hilton on Park Lane is right in the middle of Mayfair.

The hotel is a five-minute walk from Hyde Park, and upmarket shopping destination Bond Street is a 10-minute stroll. Piccadilly Circus, Oxford Street and Buckingham Palace are all within a mile of the hotel. Between Green Park and Hyde Park, this skyscraper stay blends a central city location with nearby greenery and open space. You can even spot Hyde Park’s famous green parakeets from the windows.



The vibe

open image in gallery The hotel is located right in the middle of Mayfair ( London Hilton Park Lane )

This is a bustling hotel with a vibrant atmosphere. Guests include business people, families and those enjoying after-work drinks or dinner. Because of its expansive lobby area, even at busy times the hotel doesn’t feel packed. The style combines classic with contemporary, from its sleek modern interiors, which feature statement lighting, rugs and artwork, to more timeless details such as marble floors and large mirrors.

Service

The team are welcoming and pay attention to detail, from the reception staff to those working in the bar and dining areas. Arriving at the hotel during a heatwave, when reception staff were busy checking in guests, those waiting were seamlessly ushered to another area (so they didn’t need to hang around too long).

In the Revery Bar, team members are happy to talk through the drinks menu, taking the time to ask which flavours guests usually opt for. Similarly, at Park Corner Brasserie, staff are helpful with catering to dietary requirements.

Bed and bath

There are 453 rooms, including 56 suites. They start at the queen or twin guest room sizes and move up to two-room options, with family and interconnecting rooms available too.

Rooms either look out onto Mayfair or Hyde Park. With there being 28 floors, the higher up you are, the further out you can see – this is a major highlight, and having a view over the rooftops below sets this stay apart from other city hotels. Being on a top floor room could be a bit dizzying for those who don’t like heights, but at the same time that’s testament to how dramatic this element is.

open image in gallery Rooms are airy and unfussy ( London Hilton on Park Lane )

The decor is chic and stylish while being airy and unfussy, and this adds to the open feel given by the expansive views. Furnishings are plush; pale blue statement pieces are combined with gold trims, marble sinks, modern artwork and geometric-patterned carpets.

All rooms have walk-in showers, while executive rooms and suites have freestanding baths as well. For the executive rooms and above, there are full-size Molton Brown toiletries in the bathrooms, while the other guest rooms have products from Crabtree & Evelyn.



Food and drink

The bar and restaurant options are Park Corner Brasserie, Revery Bar, Mr Porter and Shanghai Me. Additionally, The EL&N Deli & Bakery offers a patisserie and drinks menu with the option to sit in or order a takeaway.

Park Corner Brasserie is the hotel’s light-filled main eatery for breakfast, lunch, afternoon tea and dinner. Expect seasonal fare and hearty classics including scallops, pork belly and fish and chips. Also on the menu are showstoppers such as the goat’s cheese mousse starter, which is presented in a honeycomb shape. Its delicious flavours include pear cinnamon puree, salted caramel and black truffle honey.

open image in gallery There are four bars and restaurants to try at London Hilton on Park Lane ( London Hilton on Park Lane )

Breakfast is a combination of buffet-style picks covering a plentiful spread of fresh fruit, pastries, and more; plus hot options including omelettes, pancakes and a full English.

Shanghai Me has a dramatic ambience and presents dishes that blend Chinese and Japanese flavours and culinary techniques. It’s open for dinner during the week while at the weekend you can book a table from midday onwards. Alternatively, Mr Porter is a steakhouse where you can enjoy cocktails in a stylish lounge.

Revery Bar is the hotel’s chic ground-floor destination for mixed drinks, and you can also get breakfast and bar meals here. Its decor exudes opulence, with marble detailing, deep red furnishings and gold detailing throughout. The menu is separated into chapters that list its unique drinks (with varying strengths and flavours available), adding to the playful experience.

Facilities

The hotel has a small but well-equipped 24-hour fitness centre, plus a sauna and steam room. Guests staying in a suite get access to the Executive Lounge, which is a private first-floor area offering food and drinks throughout the day.

open image in gallery The view from the lounge of one of the rooms ( London Hilton on Park Lane )



Accessibility

There are five accessible bedrooms and step-free access in most of the public areas. Induction loops are available at the main reception desk and at the gym reception. All bedrooms have a speaker, as well as a vibrating and visual alarm system built in. A dedicated guest disability assistance team is available for all queries and feedback.

Pet policy

Pets are allowed with a £50 fee per stay. One animal is allowed per room, with a 24lb maximum weight limit.

Check-in/check-out

Check-in is 3pm, check-out is noon.

Family-friendly?

Children are welcome and both family and interconnecting rooms are available. Kids aged 12 and under get free breakfast, and there’s a children’s menu at Park Corner Brasserie, as well as the Disney Princess afternoon tea. Cots are also available on request.

open image in gallery The bathrooms feature marble detailing and Molton Brown products ( London Hilton Park Lane )

At a glance

Best thing: The hotel’s great location.

Perfect for: Enjoying unparalleled city views or celebrating a special occasion.

Not right for: Those with a fear of heights.

Instagram from: The stylish Revery Bar or your bedroom while overlooking the skyline.

Address: 22 Park Lane, London W1K 1BE

Phone: 020 7493 8000

Website: hilton.com



Helen was a guest of London Hilton on Park Lane

Donald Trump has declared that the World Cup should return to the United States “immediately” and claimed he would ask Fifa president Gianni Infantino to help stage another tournament during his presidency.

The hosting rights for next two World Cup have already been decided. The 2030 edition will take place in Morocco, Portugal and Spain, following opening matches in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay to mark the tournament’s centenary, while the 2034 tournament will be held in Saudi Arabia.

Fifa’s rules for its World Cup bidding process prevents countries belonging to confederations that hosted the two preceding tournaments to host the next one, which means the United States are not eligible until 2038.

Trump, who will be attending his first match of this summer’s tournament at Sunday’s final between Argentina and Spain and will present the winning team with the trophy, said in a pre-match interview with Fox Sports that he had a “great idea” for Infantino to host the World Cup in the United States again.

He claimed that demand for the World Cup resulted in matches “overflowing” with fans. According to Fifa’s figures, the inaugural 48-team World Cup, held across 16 cities in the United States, Mexico and Canada, had an overall attendance of 6.6 million, more than the two previous World Cups combined.

“Based on the numbers we will be requesting it immediately,” Trump said, while acknowledging there would be “shock” and “anger” at such a decision. “We have to do this again, and we have to do this again while I am around, hear that Gianni?”

( AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin )

Trump also predicated that Argentina would beat Spain in Sunday’s final and would successfully defend their World Cup title, adding that “it’s hard to bet against Messi”.

The US president’s relationship with Infantino was one of the many controversies to cloud the build up to this World Cup, along with ticket prices, visa issues and the ongoing war with Iran, a competing nation, during the tournament.
