Comedian Bill Maher took aim at Democrats in the party’s progressive wing with a stinging three-word insult as he suggested that he could support a Vice President JD Vance for the top job in 2028.

Maher made the remarks in an interview that aired Sunday on ABC’s This Week, a few weeks after he was honored at the Kennedy Center in Washington, D.C. with its annual Mark Twain Prize for American Humor.

Past recipients of the award have included Conan O’Brien, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Jerry Seinfeld, and Dave Chappelle. Maher, an occasional critic of Trump’s, dined at the White House last spring at a meeting arranged by Kid Rock aimed at smoothing over their sometimes-strained relationship. Afterwards, he claimed that Trump “definitely has a form of Tourette syndrome.”

In the interview, the HBO star quipped that the “level of nutty” he said was represented by the party’s new progressive insurgents were a bridge too far for him, telling ABC’s Jonathan Karl that he’d abandon the party if its “communist” wing took over.

”This wing of the party, this new wing with all the energy ... It's just a level of nutty that I'm so glad that whenever it was I was like no, I'm not going along because this is where it ends," he said. ”My vote is in play [in 2028] because it can't be Trump running, so I'm not living in communist America.”

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

Maher answered directly “yes,” when asked by Karl if he could support Vance for president in 2028 if a progressive Democrat was the nominee. Vance is widely considered to be the most likely successor to Trump for de facto control of the Republican Party, but faces potential competition from others such as Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

The host also noted that he advised Vance to quit with the conspiracy theories about the 2020 election if he wanted the support of moderates: "This stuff that's going on now, as I said to the vice president, this s*** has to stop.”

But Maher isn’t ready to jump ship just yet, adding that he thought there were “talented” Democrats who could run for the presidency from younger generations.

"I hope we can have an eight-person presidency next time because I can't pick between this crop of geniuses,” Maher said sarcastically, before adding seriously: "No, there's some very talented people.”

open image in gallery Sen. John Fetterman and his wife attended the Kennedy Center event honoring Maher for receiving the Mark Twain Prize for American Humor ( Reuters )

He ripped into the Democratic Party as “cowardly”, however, because he claimed that many Democrats were avoiding his show and coming face-to-face with his criticism.

"The Democrats don't come on [my show], and yet they got my vote. It's just odd, isn't it?" he remarked to Karl.

Maher has signaled his distaste for the progressive left before, even though his own record on the issue is muddled. He endorsed Sen. Bernie Sanders for the Democratic nomination over Hillary Clinton in 2016, though he soured on the “Bernie or Bust” movement when it became clear that Clinton had won the primary.

open image in gallery Maher endorsed Bernie Sanders in 2016 but has recently clashed with the progressive wing of the Democratic Party and the Democratic Socialists of America ( AFP/Getty )

Sanders is one Democrat who has made repeat appearances on Maher’s show, and others have joined the program in separate appearances including Rep. Ro Khanna, Sen. Elissa Slotkin and Sen. John Fetterman.

Maher’s criticism comes as the progressive wing of the party has clashed with both Democratic Party leadership as well as the general seniority of the party’s membership on Capitol Hill while targeting incumbents with primary challenges this cycle.

The left has brushed off the criticism from the center and portrayed the wave of primary challenges against incumbents as the inevitable result of the anger openly displayed by the Democratic base over 2025 in the face of the onset of the second Trump administration, which began with the DOGE-ification of the federal government. Party leaders acknowledged that voters were furious last year over a perception of non-resistance hanging over the Democratic House and Senate caucuses. A shutdown fight over federal Obamacare subsidies, which expired at the end of the year, added to that perception when Senate Democrats eventually backed down.

Maher’s selection by the Kennedy Center for the Mark Twain prize sparked controversy online as many saw the news as the Trump-controlled board of the Kennedy Center picking someone who is relatively friendly to the president to receive the prize.

Trump launched a full takeover of the Kennedy Center last year, complete with an unsuccessful attempt to add his name to it without congressional approval. An effort to alter the Center’s programming was met with stiff resistance from both artists who pulled out of hosting shows at the venue and audiences who departed in droves.

The board of Trump-installed directors announced earlier this year that it would close and undergo a two-year renovation process after several months of declining ticket sales.

The lineups for the World Cup final have been confirmed as Spain stick with their tried and tested formula but Argentina opt to ring the changes.

The current European champions and the reigning world champions are going head to head in a fascinating encounter in New Jersey, as this historically large World Cup plays its 104th and final match.

Spain are the favourites after brilliantly beating France 2-0 in a surprisingly one-sided semi-final, so perhaps it is no surprise that Luis de la Fuente has opted for an unchanged starting XI from that fixture.

Ahead of the final, De La Fuente had said that Tottenham full-back Pedro Porro was dealing with muscle tightness but he is deemed fit to start and Barcelona superstar Lamine Yamal has had his workload managed throughout this World Cup following hamstring and groin injuries but he too is fine to play from the off.

Yamal will be joined in attack by Mikel Oyarzabal and Dani Olmo, while Man City defensive midfielder Rodri – described as the “real player of the tournament” by our Senior Football Correspondent Richard Jolly – captains the side.

Lionel Messi, of course, captains Argentina as they hunt back-to-back titles but Lionel Scaloni makes three changes from the side that started the semi-final victory over England.

open image in gallery Pedro Porro is fit to start for Spain despite muscle tightness ( Reuters )

Nahuel Molina, Giuliano Simeone and Leandro Paredes all drop to the bench, with right-back Gonzalo Montiel and midfielders Rodrigo De Paul and Nico Gonzalez starting instead.

Messi’s partner up top will once more be Julian Alvarez, while the much-maligned duo of Cristian Romero and Lisandro Martinez are the starting centre-backs again.

Teams for Spain v Argentina in World Cup 2026 final

Spain XI: Simon; Porro, Cubarsi, Laporte, Cucurella; Rodri; Baena Ruiz; Yamal, Oyarzabal, Olmo.

Subs: Raya, Garcia, Pubill, Grimaldo, Garcia, Llorente, Merino, Gavi, Zubimendi, Pedri, Torres, Pino, Williams. Munoz, Iglesias.

Argentina XI: E. Martinez; Montiel, Romero, Lis. Martinez, Tagliafico; Gonzalez, Enzo, De Paul, Mac Allister; Alvarez, Messi.

Subs: Musso, Rulli, Senesi, Otamendi, Medina, Molina, Paredes, Barco, Lo Celso, Palacios, Almada, Simeone, Paz, Lopez, Martinez.

New Zealander Ryan Fox kept his head while all around him were losing theirs to make his major breakthrough at the age of 39 with a brilliant birdie at the last for a one-shot victory at the Open.

He was one of only three players in the final 12 groups to shoot under par on a chaotic final day when Royal Birkdale finally showed its teeth after two days of back-to-back record-equalling rounds of 62.

After Cameron Young posted the nine-under target after a best-of-the-day 64 a couple of hours earlier, double figures was the aim for those out on the course.

Fox headed down the last – Birkdale’s most difficult hole – needing a birdie to overtake the American, for so long the PGA Tour’s perennial runner-up, and hit his approach inside 12 feet.

The son of All Blacks fly-half Grant held his nerve, as he had done all day and punched the air as he became New Zealand’s second Open champion after Sir Bob Charles in 1963.

Fox started at eight under, two behind, and was never more than one better or one worse all day until delivering the coup de grace at the last – only the fifth birdie on the hole all day – showing a level of composure lacking by some of his rivals.

Playing partner and overnight leader Sam Burns got to 11 under after three holes but dropped three strokes, Si Woo Kim gave back four from 10 under while defending champion Scottie Scheffler and home favourite Tommy Fleetwood both threatened before coming up three short.

open image in gallery Ryan Fox is a major champion (Jacob King/PA) ( PA Wire )

A pivotal hole for Fox was the 241-yard par-three 15th when an unlucky bounce left him with an almost unplayable lie under the lip of a bunker.

With very little fuss, in keeping with his no-nonsense approach, he took his medicine, splashed out back down the fairway and made bogey.

It could have derailed many players but he holed a 10-footer at the next for a birdie and was left with two holes to pick up one more and the fact he did it on the last, rather than the par-five 17th, was a nod to his quality.

That had been in evidence the day before when he carded one of three 62s scored this week to put him into the final group for the last day.

“I don’t really know what to think at the moment,” said Fox, only the third Kiwi to win a major after Charles and Michael Campbell, at the US Open in 2005, after a final-round 68.

“I spoke to my kids last night and they said ‘bring back a trophy’. I think this is a pretty cool one to bring back for them.”

Fox added: “My nerves are all over the place, I’m not sure how I hit that putt on 18.

“It’s a dream come true looking at this trophy right now. It’s the first time I’ve seen it close up and it’s pretty amazing.

“I played really solid early and then hit some great shots down the stretch. I stood on the final tee and said to my caddie ‘We’re going to win this’. Champion golfer of the year has a nice ring to it.”

Fox has a reputation for playing fast and there were just 22 seconds between Burns holing out on the last and Fox sinking his championship-winning putt.

“It’s always been ‘see a shot, hit a shot’ and as soon as I start thinking about it some bad stuff sinks in,” he said.

Lewis Hamilton has avoided a post-race penalty after a close call with a Ferrari mechanic during a pit-stop at the Belgian Grand Prix.

The seven-time world champion endured a frustrating day at Spa-Francorchamps as he was handed a five-second penalty early on for a collision with George Russell, who spun out on the first lap.

Then, during his pit-stop where he served such a penalty, Hamilton left his pit-box but ran over his own mechanic’s leg after being erroneously given the green light to rejoin the track.

Hamilton paused in a state of worry before continuing but the mechanic escaped significant injury. The FIA stewards said they’d investigate after the session under a potential “unsafe release”.

However, the decision came a few hours after Hamilton finished fourth that the team had been fined £25,500, of which £8,500 is suspended for 12 months, but they have not suffered a damaging sporting penalty.

“I damaged the car, then when they rebuilt it, they missed the suspension so the balance was completely different,” Hamilton told Sky Sports F1 afterwards.

“I was three-tenths slower; it was a domino effect from a mistake from myself. The team have been doing a great job with strategy, pit stops, we are continually improving our car, I think without the damage... we could have challenged for the win.

On the incident with the mechanic, Hamilton said: “The green light went, you're looking ‘over here’ not ‘there’, it’s more on the team ultimately.

“When it happened, I noticed him, I stopped. Back when Kimi [Raikkonen] broke the leg, my heart really sank for a second, glad he's OK.”

Asked about a difficult race as a whole, Hamilton admitted: “This weekend was unfortunate. I think it's pretty great to see the performance improving the car constantly, more stuff in the pipeline to try and close that gap down.

“To be here and have the pace we had as a team is really encouraging. There's still a long way to go, can't afford weekends like this in terms of my performance yesterday [crash in practice], so am going to step it up in performance level next week.”

Despite finishing outside the top three, Russell’s retirement means Hamilton moves up to second in the championship standings and is Kimi Antonelli’s closest challenger, lying 45 points behind.

The next race is the Hungarian Grand Prix next weekend, the final round before the F1 summer break.

News.title: Antonelli wins Belgian Grand Prix to extend championship lead after Russell crashes out
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix from Spa-Francorchamps. The story of yesterday and in fact the weekend was of everyone trying to dislodge Kimi Antonelli from the top of the timesheets. Spoiler alert if you did not watch qualifying: they failed.

That is not to say the fight wasn’t a half-decent one. Max Verstappen and Red Bull were the closest challengers in the end, demonstrating an element of revival during a tricky season. Whether that will continue during the race is hard to know. Verstappen certainly thought he would have been further down the field without the tremendous tow he received from Isack Hadjar, his Red Bull team-mate, in the final sector.

Lando Norris also pushed Verstappen, though was almost half a second down on Antonelli’s time in the end. Unfortunately he will not be able to take advantage of a start from third place because he takes a 10-place grid penalty. George Russell, who has managed to reduce his Mercedes team-mate’s advantage to just 25 points in the past few rounds, was fourth and will start third. He did however, have a difficult session once again, finishing more than half a second off his team-mate.

He was at a loss to explain this. Well, he knows where he lost most of the time: on the straights. But he still does not understand exactly why it is happening. The good news for him is that third place is often the most optimal starting position at this track.

Will that be the case today? Let’s see...

News.title: England win gives Borthwick breathing space after late try controversy
News.content:
And in doing so he may have just saved Borthwick’s job.

The Rugby Football Union, following its review into England’s Six Nations campaign that yielded just one victory, had publicly offered its backing to its head coach through to the World Cup. But in reality, there are no guarantees. It needed evidence of England’s progress.

Two wins from three rounds of the Nations Championship is likely to convince RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney to back his man. But Borthwick will know that nothing can be taken for granted.

Four years ago, Eddie Jones, facing similar scrutiny from his employers, looked to have salvaged his job by winning the last two matches in a three-Test summer tour of Australia. But it did still not save him from the sack the following November.

Still. There was enough character and attacking prowess to convince the RFU that, despite the flaws in this display, the team are on the right track again.

It was still far from an 80-minute performance, but this was England’s first away victory in a year, in a hostile environment and after all the challenges, both physical and mental, the players have faced in travelling to three continents over three weeks – clocking up more than 25,000 miles – at the end of a long season.

England wobbled alarmingly earlier in the second half but remarkably found the resilience to drag themselves back into the game just as it looked like it was slipping from their grasp. That is clear evidence of players playing for their coach and each other.

Discipline, however, remains a major problem for Borthwick’s England. They had been cruising to what would looked to have been a statement victory at half-time following tries by Tommy Freeman and two by Ben Earl, in what had been their finest half of rugby this year.

And yet, once again indiscipline undermined their efforts. Remarkably, they were shown four yellow cards – Jack van Poortvliet, Alex Coles, Pollock (to more booing) and Emmanuel Iyogun – in the second half to take their total to 14 in their last 10 Tests, and at one stage were down to 12 men but, significantly, this time it did not prove fatal.

News.title: Tuchel learns lesson as England clinch third place in 10-goal thriller
News.content:
Neither England nor France wanted to be playing this game in Miami, but they can have no complaints about the nature of their semi-final defeats.

Tournament favourites France were comprehensively outplayed by Spain, with their feted front four of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Bradley Barcola and Michael Olise all turning in below-par performances.

England’s defeat by Argentina was perhaps not as much of a surprise, but the nature of Thomas Tuchel’s team’s second-half collapse was just as alarming as France’s no-show.

England’s manager was fiercely criticised for replacing Anthony Gordon with Ezri Konsa and switching to a back five in the 72nd minute, but Tuchel has since defended his decisions.

“If you are asking if I regret my decisions, if this is the question, then I say no. I don’t regret my ‌decisions because I ‌felt that we became ⁠too passive,” said Tuchel.

“I took several decisions, trusting my instinct, my intuition, my experience, trusting my competitiveness, and I took the decision in order to help the team and get the result.

“I would regret if I didn’t help. I would regret ⁠if we didn’t react, but I have no regrets over the decision itself.”

Quite how strong Didier Deschamps and Tuchel decide to go with their teams is anyone’s guess. There has been some suggestion that Mbappe will start to give him the chance to beat Lionel Messi to the Golden Boot.

Some of England’s regular starters, such as Declan Rice, look physically spent, so there could be some rotation, and even a chance for players such as Kobbie Mainoo who has not played a minute of football at the tournament.

The third/fourth-place play-off has been rebranded as the “Bronze Final” for this tournament, and Tuchel was keen to point out that finishing third would be England’s best World Cup result since 1966. They lost this fixture against Belgium in 2018, but the way that game has been widely forgotten speaks volumes.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Scotland fight back to claim victory against Fiji in Nations Championship
News.content:
A barrelling Schoeman finished an initial break by match captain Stafford McDowall, then Dobie burrowed over beside the posts in the 61st minute to put Scotland in front for the first time in 40 minutes.

Scotland glossed up the scoreline with two more tries in the last six minutes by Cummings and Dobie again to send home a crowd of 55,000 happy.

“I thought our bench did really well,” Townsend told the BBC. “Something I’ve learned over the last 12 months, the bench can help you change momentum. The players can come up with solutions themselves but the bench can give you energy and solutions but also bravery. We’re a team that will back our decisions and that put real pressure on Fiji.

“I felt [Fiji] picked their strongest side today and it took a lot of work for us to break them down but also it took a really good defensive performance,” Townsend added. “Fiji didn’t really break us that often [and] in that final quarter the guys were outstanding. We’ll take a few positives from that.”

Fiji had never beaten Scotland at Murrayfield but would have sensed the chance of making history by half-time. The Fijians were tough and clinical in a huge turnaround from last weekend when they were humiliated by England 73-8 in Liverpool.

News.title: Hometown hero Tommy Fleetwood facing tough ask to end 57 years of Open hurt
News.content:
Never mind Bryson DeChambeau stomping around in the rough as he improved his lie, for so long this Open Saturday turned into Tommy Fleetwood walking in his Royal Birkdale wonderland as he enhanced the mood of seemingly everyone in attendance.

Alas, the fun could not last and, even though he still has a chance of becoming England’s first Open winner on English soil since 1969, that finish looked costly. Fifty-seven years of hurt and all that...

On five under, Fleetwood is in a tie for ninth, five off the lead held by Sam Burns, the American who, after a 65, is two clear of New Zealander Ryan Fox and South Korean Kim Si-woo. DeChambeau is alongside Swede Ludvig Aberg, in a tie for sixth on six under, after a 69.

He was heckled on the 18th because of the two-shot penalty he received on Friday night for “inadvertently improving his lie” on the fifth. “You’re a cheat, Bryson,” the fan shouted.

It was a sour point that was in no way in keeping with the mood of this Saturday that had been overwhelmingly positive. With Fleetwood as the focus, of course.

The enormous crowd cheered and sang and backed their fellow Merseysider all the way as Fleetwood launched his charge into contention at this Southport links which he would once sneak on as a child. His playing partner, Jon Rahm, was taken aback by the level of support.

“The best way I can explain it, it was so intense that, without meaning any disrespect I’m glad England didn’t win the semi-final [of the World Cup] because I would have been having a heck of a three days with the fans if they had been playing Spain in tomorrow’s final,” Rahm said.

News.title: Sloppy Springboks still strong enough to pulverise Wales
News.content:
If one image summed up South Africa’s complete control, it was in the 12th minute when Wales had a scrum on their own five-metre line. When the Springbok shove came, the Welsh pack went backwards like they were on roller-skates. The poor Welsh front row are going to have to check under their beds for snarling Springboks props for quite a few sleepless nights to come.

Wales’ best period of the game came just after the Springboks’ fourth try when they had three line-outs and took three tap penalties deep inside the South Africa 22. It amounted to absolutely nothing.

You can point fingers at head coach Steve Tandy’s selections and preparation if you wish, but there was little he could have done to change the result. It was only the manner of their hammering, he could have potentially affected.

Wales are not alone in this. Scotland and England may have posed a few more problems but they were still dispatched with ease. South Africa are truly in a league of their own, although New Zealand’s resurgence under Dave Rennie should at least provide a serious level of competition that the British mainland failed to provide.

In truth the best thing that Tandy could do is burn the tapes and hope that this is consigned to the deepest recesses of their collective memory. Tighthead Dillon Lewis especially may need one of those Men in Black memory wipers.

If you squinted hard enough, there were a couple of positives: the maul defence and high-ball contest. They were at least competitive. Aaron Wainwright had the unenviable job of packing down at the back of a retreating Welsh scrum but did a heroic job in the circumstances. Jac Morgan, too, was bravery personified in attacking the breakdown with the ferocity of the Springboks clean-out operation.

But in the infrequent periods when South Africa got on a roll without knocking on, there was precious little Wales could do to stop the green wave. The first try was a case in point. Emanating from a loose kick from Tomos Williams, full-back Aphelele Fassi broke the first line of Wales’ defence and then they kept coming through Cobus Wiese, Damien de Allende before Jasper Wiese accelerated through Morgan’s tackle and over the line.

News.title: Santos impresses in first Man Utd appearance but cannot prevent defeat by Wrexham
News.content:
United were without the players who have featured at this summer’s World Cup – including new signing Youri Tielemans – as well as Benjamin Sesko, but Michael Carrick put out a strong starting XI in front of 20,000 spectators in the Finnish capital.

Santos, who became United’s first summer signing when he joined from Chelsea at the start of the week for an initial £48m, took his place at the base of midfield alongside Mason Mount.

Speaking just before the match, Michael Carrick had praised the 22-year-old’s attitude, saying: “He’s settled in really well, he’s a fantastic character. He’s buzzing to be here, you can see that.”

The Brazilian’s first involvement was to clear the ball away after Tom Heaton failed to gather under pressure from Smith seconds into the game.

Santos was left on his backside by Lewis O’Brien eight minutes in but the chance came to nothing for Wrexham as the flag went up. More encouraging was his sliding block on O’Brien moments later and he soon settled in, showing a good range of passing and winning several duels in a busy display.

However, Phil Parkinson’s side, who played their first pre-season friendly against Wisla Krakow in Poland last weekend, were looking brighter and threatened again when Bailey Cadamarteri nicked the ball off Ayden Heaven on the edge of the box before the defender recovered.

United’s first chance was a Joshua Zirkzee shot that fizzed wide in the 24th minute and they almost went ahead when Smith tried to clear a cornerm but instead sent a header on to his own crossbar in the 36th minute.

Sports.title: Who is Rodri’s girlfriend Laura Iglesias? Meet Ballon d’Or 2024 winner’s medical student partner
Sports.content:
RODRI’S girlfriend Laura Iglesias is a medical student training to become a surgeon, but she still makes time to support him on the pitch.

The highlight of the Manchester City star’s career is winning the 2024 Ballon d’Or after a stunning season for both club and country.



And his partner Laura was right by his side to cheer him on.

Who is Rodri’s girlfriend Laura Iglesias?

Rodrigo Hernández‘s girlfriend Laura Iglesias is a medical student.



She is training to become a surgeon.

Laura supports him in her free time and was seen with him at the French Open in May 2024.

The couple do not have any children together, and keep their lives off social media.

Rodri has previously said that she records her reaction to his goals which he watches later.

Rodri is a defensive midfielder who plays for Manchester City after joining them in 2019.

He began his career at Villarreal, where he played for the senior squad from 2015-2018.

Rodri is also a Spanish international, winning Euro 2024 with the national team.

And picked up the biggest individual prize in football after receiving the 2024 Ballon d’Or award.

How long have Rodri and Laura Iglesias been dating?

Rodri and Laura met during university.



He was studying business studies and economics at the Universidad de Castellon in eastern Spain.

Rodri even lived in student halls in a shared place.

His friend Valentin Henarejo told Marca about their time at university: “People were shocked when they saw Rodri, who was playing in the top flight but still living at the university residence.

Sports.title: Who is Lionel Messi’s wife Antonela Roccuzzo and what is her job?
Sports.content:
LIONEL MESSI is one of the greatest players ever to touch a football.

The Argentinian superstar has won everything for club and country – not to mention his eight Ballon d’Ors.



And wife Antonela Roccuzzo has been there every step of the way.

Here is what SunSport know about his long-term partner.



Who is Antonela Roccuzzo?

Antonela Roccuzzo was born Argentina‘s third largest city of Rosario, just like Lionel Messi.

She has known the Argentinian legend since she was five years old as her cousin, Lucas Scaglia, was a childhood friend of his.



If Messi has a reputation of being shy, this was certainly not the case in his pursuit of Antonela, as he regularly visited her home from a young age, just to see her.

It is not known how long the pair have been together behind closed doors, but they went public with their relationship in 2008.

The bond between the couple was believed to have strengthened in 2007, when Messi flew back to Rosario to comfort Antonela after the death of her friend.



What is Antonela Roccuzzo’s job?

Antonela Roccuzzo initially trained to be a dentist at university.

But she ultimately switched to becoming a social media influencer.

She has worked as a model and also co-founded Enfans, a children’s clothing brand, along with her cousin Andrea Lo Menzo.

And Antonela describes herself as a “Digital creator” on her Instagram page, where she has more than 40 million followers.

Where did her wedding with Lionel Messi take place?

The Barcelona striker married Antonela in a party billed Argentina’s ‘wedding of the century.’



It took place at the plush City Centre Hotel and Casino in their hometown of Rosario in Argentina.

Premier League stars Cesc Fabregas and Sergio Aguero were present, while Barcelona legends Xavi Hernandez, Carles Puyol and Samuel Eto’o were also in town.

It has been reported that as well as guests having their phones banned, staff were sworn to secrecy – and over 450 police officers were brought in to manage the situation.

And the couple looked overwhelmed to tie the knot in front of their young sons Thiago and Mateo.

On March 10, 2018, Antonella gave birth to the couple’s third son, Ciro.

Sports.title: World Cup final chaos with huge queues outside MetLife Stadium and TWO HOUR wait simply to get inside
Sports.content:
FANS who splashed the cash to snap up a World Cup final ticket are facing queues of more than TWO HOURS to get into the MetLife Stadium.

Argentina, who ended England’s hopes of glory with a dramatic late comeback on Wednesday, are set to lock horns with Spain in the showpiece.



The final is set to become the most expensive sporting event in history – with the cheapest ticket available on Fifa’s official resale website on the eve of the showdown being priced at close to £6,000.

But there is chaos outside the 82,500-capacity arena on the outskirts of New York.



There have been technological glitches at the turnstiles, leading to some tickets not scanning.

And that has resulted in huge queues forming as security staff struggle to manage the massive crowds battling to reach their seat for the World Cup final.



SunSport’s reporters who will be covering the clash have also been waiting to get inside the home of the New York Giants and New York Jets for two hours as the mayhem unfolds.

Media members are facing extra checks from the secret service because of carrying laptops and filming equipment.

Disgruntled fans, who were told to arrive FOUR hours ahead of kick-off, have also been misdirected by stewards when they have been desperately trying to find the correct entry point.

Sports.title: Who is hosting World Cup 2030 and will they gain automatic qualification?
Sports.content:
WE have reached the final stage of this year’s World Cup – and two huge nations will battle it out to lift football’s biggest trophy in TONIGHT.

Argentina look to defend their title against Spain in the grand finale.

But once this mouthwatering showpiece concludes, all attention will turn to the 2030 tournament.



And SunSport can fill you in with all the details ahead of the next iconic competition.



WORLD CUP FINAL LIVE: ALL THE LATEST FROM SPAIN VS ARGENTINA

Who is hosting the World Cup 2030?

For the first time in World Cup history, there will be three countries from two different continents that are set to host the World Cup 2030.

These three countries are Spain, Portugal and Morocco.

This is due to it being the 100th anniversary of the first-ever tournament back in 1930.



And to commemorate such a special celebration, there will be matches held OUTSIDE of the host nations.

Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay will host group matches to mark the 100th year anniversary.

When does the World Cup 2030 start?

World Cup 2030 will get underway on Thursday, June 13 and it concludes on

The first match of the competition is scheduled to be played at the Estadio Centenario in Montevideo, Uruguay, where the first World Cup was held.



As it stands, there will be 48 teams from six confederations battling it out to lift the prestigious trophy but Chief Executive of FIFA Gianni Infantino confirmed that he is considering expanding the tournament to 64 teams.

Will all host nations gain automatic qualification to the World Cup 2030?

To put it simply, yes.

All three main host nations gain automatic qualification to the World Cup 2030 and so will the 100th-anniversary group match hosts.

This means six nations have already booked their spot – Spain, Portugal, Morocco, Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay.

It was also announced that the tournament will be played in over 20 different venues across 20 different cities.



And this will be the first time that the World Cup is held in Africa since 2010 and the first ever in North Africa.

Sports.content:
ARGENTINA and Spain fans geared up for the biggest game of their lives by partying in Times Square.

Fans were pictured in their masses dancing and singing ahead of the highly anticipated World Cup final at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.



A sea of red shirts stood shoulder to shoulder belting out chants, taking videos on their phones and soaking in the atmosphere.

And they were opposed by thousands of blue and white Argentina fanatics ready to witness Lionel Messi’s World Cup swansong.



There were a few brief moments when the two sides came together.

One Spaniard took a sip out of an Argentina fan’s ‘Mate’ cup – an important symbol of Argentine culture.

Sports.title: ‘Not here to cause drama’ – Bukayo Saka reveals true feelings over being axed from England’s starting XI vs Argentina
Sports.content:
BUKAYO SAKA held his tongue over being left out against Argentina because he did not want to “cause any drama”.

The Arsenal star did not play a minute of the semi-final defeat to the South Americans, despite insisting he was fit to play.



Saka then scored a hat-trick against France in the madcap third-place play-off, which England won 6-4.

Asked why the difference in performance between the two games, Saka replied: “It’s a completely different game.



“When it was the semi-final, everything at stake, there’s so much pressure on that game, this game was much less.

“And obviously we fielded a different line-up… so there were so many different factors as to the different performances.

“In the end, the 11 that the manager picks, we have to deliver and the changes that were made, of course, were the changes.

“There is not really much that I want to say right now because I’m not here to cause any drama, but it’s what it is, and you just have to move on.”

England had hoped to go all the way in America but were forced to settle for bronze after beating the French.

Assistant Anthony Barry said the players played against Les Bleus with “broken hearts” following the dramatic late loss to Argentina.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

Saka wants to use that pain as fuel at Euro 2028 in two years.

He added: “I don’t think anything can lessen the pain that we felt from the other night. That one really hurt us, I’ll be honest.

“When we go into the next major tournament, this will definitely be fuel for us.

“It’s very tough to take, but we did show that we believed and I feel that we made the country believe as well that we could do it. So that belief hasn’t left us.



“We’ll be back next tournament to try and get over the line.”

Saka is now set to enjoy a well-deserved break from football before joining Arsenal’s pre-season preparations.

The winger will soon be gearing up towards Arsenal’s title defence, but first he will expect to feature in the Community Shield against Man City on August 16.

Sports.title: World Cup final chaos as furious fans forced to wait HOURS to enter stadium
Sports.content:
World Cup final chaos as furious fans forced to wait HOURS to enter stadium

The World Cup final between Spain and Argentina is due to take place on Sunday evening but supporters and members of the media were met with mayhem outside of the MetLife Stadium

View 2 Images Fans have ran into serious issues getting into MetLife Stadium (Image: Getty Images)

The 2026 World Cup final has already been blighted by chaos before the game, with supporters struggling to enter MetLife Stadium.

‌



The arena - which is located a way away from Manhattan - has been criticised throughout the tournament for its unsuitability for the final. And FIFA’s decision to hand the game to the stadium now looks even more baffling given the troubles that both fans and members of the media have faced in attempting to enter.

‌



Even five hours before kick-off, some members of security suggested that FIFA’s ticketing system was throwing out glitches, making it tricky to allow people entry.

‌



That forced organisers to encourage fans, workers and members of the media to get to the stadium as early as possible. But that only worsened the issue, with long queues forming around the stadium, with many of those taking hours to clear. Those not at the stadium early were also met with long delays at Penn Station, ahead of even travelling to the stadium itself.

The presence of US president Donald Trump also appeared to make the situation even worse. Despite a heightened security presence due to his attendance, there was a lack of real organisation, with many in attendance given wrong instructions on where to enter.

Argentina players refuse to give Falklands banner back after England World Cup controversy READ MORE :

It wasn’t just fans who bore the brunt of the problems. Accredited media also found it frustrating to gain admission due to Trump’s attendance.

‌



Extra Secret Service security checks were completed on their equipment, with many members of the press also facing delays of hours to get in.

Leading up to the final, there have also been concerns about the weather. New York was hit with heavy thunderstorms on the eve of the game, which saw Spain cancel their pre-match training session. Flash flooding also hit the region.

And with the stadium having no roof, the final itself would also face delays due to lightning protocols, albeit the weather cleared on Sunday. There have also been worries about the air quality ahead of the game, with a brutal smog having surrounded both New York and New Jersey due to wildfires in Canada.

‌



View 2 Images The World Cup final is set to take place at the MetLife Stadium (Image: Getty Images)

Away from the issues getting into the stadium, fans have also let their frustrations be known at MetLife being selected for the final. There is very little around the stadium - allowing for the American Dream Mall a 20 minute walk away - while prices for food and drinks inside are also extortionate, with ticket prices through the roof.

The stadium’s pitch has also been criticised throughout the tournament. Brazil star Vinicius Jr was among those to take aim at the playing service last month.

Sports.title: Arsenal eye shock transfer for England World Cup hero after Morgan Rogers snub
Sports.content:
Arsenal eye shock transfer for England World Cup hero after Morgan Rogers snub

Arsenal look set to miss out on a deal for Morgan Rogers with Chelsea swooping in but they could still sign a key member of England's World Cup squad in the coming weeks

View 2 Images Arsenal could swoop for free agent John Stones (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

John Stones has emerged as a surprise target for Arsenal following the World Cup, with the veteran defender available on a free transfer.

‌



Stones brought the curtain down on a decade of domestic dominance with Manchester City at the end of the Premier League season before heading to the World Cup with England, playing a key role in the side's run to the semi-finals of the tournament.

‌



With Stones now deciding his next move, the 32-year-old's availability and extensive top-flight pedigree makes him an attractive proposition for elite clubs — and Arsenal look to be in need of defensive reinforcements amid concerns over William Saliba.

‌



The Arsenal star played through a back injury at the World Cup before breaking down in France's semi-final defeat to Spain, and there are now fears that Saliba could be sidelined for up to five months.

Chelsea strike mega £117m Morgan Rogers transfer with Arsenal set to miss out on star READ MORE :

With Stones available, he is viewed as a cost-effective option to help Arsenal cope in Saliba's absence according to The Sun, who claim the newly minted Premier League champions could soon swoop for a player who has battled against them in title races of years past.

Mikel Arteta knows Stones well from his stint working as an assistant coach for Manchester City and the opportunity to continue playing in the Premier League with a club primed to compete for major honours would likely appeal to the player.

‌



Stones, who is understood to have numerous options on the table including from suitors abroad, will consider his next move now that England's involvement with the World Cup is over.

View 2 Images Morgan Rogers is set to join Chelsea rather than Arsenal (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

Arsenal's interest in Stones comes following the bombshell news that one of their primary summer transfer targets, Morgan Rogers, is on the cusp of a blockbuster move to Chelsea.

‌



The 23-year-old has been courted by both clubs for months with Arsenal keen to level up the left-hand side of their attack, an area Rogers is adept at operating in.

And while Arsenal have long been considered the red-hot favourites to land the former Middlesbrough star, it emerged on Saturday night that Chelsea have agreed a £117million for the Aston Villa attacker, with Stamford Bridge emerging as Rogers' preferred destination despite Arsenal's interest.

Sports.title: Why has David Raya not been starting at World Cup? Arsenal star's Spain snub explained
Sports.content:
Why has David Raya not been starting at World Cup? Arsenal star's Spain snub explained

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya is one of the Premier League's top shot-stoppers but remains a bench-warmer for Spain

View 4 Images David Raya has been relegated to the bench during Spain's World Cup campaign (Image: Getty)

Arsenal shot-stopper David Raya has been snubbed in Spain’s route to Sunday’s showpiece final thanks to the stellar performances of Unai Simon. Raya has carved out a reputation as one of the best goalkeepers in world football, playing an integral role in leading the Gunners to their first Premier League triumph since 2004 last term.

‌



The 30-year-old’s switch from Brentford three seasons ago coincided with Arsenal’s push for their elusive league title and he secured his third consecutive Golden Glove in the 2025/26 campaign with an astonishing 19 clean sheets last term. A momentous campaign at club level promised to be even more fruitful with the prospect of starring in between the sticks at the World Cup.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Sadly for the Arsenal 'keeper, though, things have not quite worked out that way. Simon was the preferred first-choice for Spain in their run to Euros glory in 2024, with Raya only starting their final group stage game despite flourishing in his maiden Arsenal campaign, but his performances heading into this tournament were becoming too impressive to ignore.

Nonetheless, Simon’s status as their long-established number one has resulted in Raya not playing a single minute in North America. But why has the Barcelona-born ‘keeper not made a lasting impact on the biggest stage?

Selection headache

‌



Luis de la Fuente had a crucial decision to make ahead of their curtain-raiser with Cape Verde, whether to stick with the man who had started the previous four tournaments or select a goalkeeper in Raya who has flourished in recent seasons. Simon had a lacklustre campaign as Athletic Bilbao shipped the most goals since their dismal 2012/13 campaign where they finished in 12th, conceding 58 times over the course of the league season.

Cesc Fabregas tells England's Thomas Tuchel exactly what he would NEVER do as manager READ MORE :

Raya was the polar opposite, conceding only one more goal than the Invincibles and flourishing when playing out from the back. Nevertheless, it has been the Bilbao ‘keeper who was has been trusted by his national team and the decision has ultimately been vindicated.

Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

‌



Spain have built upon solid defensive foundations with the meanest defence in the World Cup with their faultless rearguard only being penetrated against Belgium. Before Charles De Ketelaere’s leveller, Simon had his hands on a World Cup record of not conceding in over 650 minutes.

While Arsenal fans will see Raya’s lack of minutes as a blessing in disguise with several of their key stars struggling with fatigue this tournament, he did all he could to stake a claim for a starting role this summer. However, De la Fuente has prioritised international experience over club form with Simon delivering in the critical moments, notably when he came out of his box early to deny Kylian Mbappe breaking through the Spanish backline twice with vital clearances in the semi-finals.

Speaking about the goalkeeping dilemma ahead of the tournament, the Spain coach said: “I don’t believe in pressure. I feel zero pressure. The decision we make regarding the goalkeeper will be based on an assessment of each situation to determine which goalkeeper best suits our needs. All three have fantastic qualities. We have three of the best goalkeepers in the world, and whoever plays will offer us complete confidence.”

‌



View 4 Images Raya impressed last season during Arsenal's title-winning campaign (Image: Photo by Rob Newell - CameraSport via Getty Images)

Crunching the numbers

In terms of the statistical narrative, the two do not differ significantly. It’s important to recognise that Simon is in a side that faces more shots on goal and had to make 40 more saves over the course of the league season, preventing 2.17 goals, compared to Raya’s 0.66, which underlines the importance of Simon to his team.

‌



Raya registered 13 more league clean sheets and was much more convincing in his area coming for more crosses, claiming them or punching them, indicative of a ‘keeper who thrives in taking responsibility for incoming deliveries. However, Simon’s stats during this World Cup speak for themselves.

View 4 Images Raya (centre) has been usurped on the international stage by Unai Simon (left) (Image: Getty)

While he has played fewer games, he has posted an outstanding 90% save percentage with the 2023 Nations League winner actually conceding 0.71 fewer goals than expected. History shows that a formidable shot-stopper is often the backbone of a World Cup-winning team and Simon has repeatedly answered the call in the clutch moments.

‌



The final say

In truth, it is impossible to look past Simon for his show-stopping displays and Raya has simply been a victim of his success. He was understandably questioned prior to the tournament after several high-profile errors in La Liga last term which led to goals, putting him in the spotlight for all the wrong reasons.

View 4 Images Simon has justified his selection, conceding just once throughout the whole tournament (Image: Getty)

‌



In contrast to Raya’s incredible campaign, it looked as if the former Blackburn Rovers shot-stopper could finally make his international breakthrough. However, to say Simon has been immense this summer would be an understatement.

Aided by an evolving defensive partnership of Pau Cubarsi and Aymeric Laporte, La Roja are closing in on replicating their 2010 triumph where they only conceded once in the tournament and Simon has been at the centre of that. Spain are closing in on an international dynasty as they close in on back-to-back international tournaments and De la Fuente’s decision not to select Raya has ultimately proved dividends despite his undeniable quality.

Sports.title: Antonelli takes big Belgian GP win as Russell's woes deepen after Hamilton clash
Sports.content:
Kimi Antonelli overcame an unfortunately-timed Virtual Safety Car to overtake Charles Leclerc and win the Belgian Grand Prix on a day team-mate George Russell's title hopes suffered a major fresh blow.

Antonelli doubled his in-house advantage over Russell to 50 points after the Briton was spun out into the gravel at the fifth corner of the first lap in a collision with Lewis Hamilton that stewards judged the Ferrari driver was at fault for.

Hamilton was given a five-second penalty, which he served at his sole pit stop, and eventually finished fourth after overtaking McLaren's Oscar Piastri late on.

Hamilton and Ferrari faced a post-race investigation for an alleged unsafe Ferrari release at the same pit stop after he was given the signal to leave the box and knocked over a mechanic who was still trying to work on his car's front wing.

The mechanic was struck by the Ferrari's front-right tyre and was briefly knocked to his knees before being helped back up to his feet before Hamilton, who had stopped the car, fully exited the pit box. Ferrari were fined €30,000, of which a third was suspended for 12 months.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Ferrari pit crew were unable to attach Lewis Hamilton's front wing as the British driver also knocked over a mechanic after being given the green light

Hamilton moves back ahead of Russell in second to Antonelli in the standings - 45 points behind the Italian, with one race to go in Hungary this coming week before F1's summer break.

Max Verstappen, who briefly took the lead from Antonelli on the first lap out of Eau Rouge before the Mercedes almost immediately blasted back past, took third after he was also jumped by Leclerc during the VSC.

Isack Hadjar finished sixth in the second Red Bull from the back row, just holding off Lando Norris on fresher tyres after the McLaren had run all the way to lap 30 before stopping having started a penalised 13th on the grid.

Gabriel Bortoleto was eighth for Audi ahead of Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad and Alpine's Franco Colapinto.

Belgian GP Result: Top 10 1) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



2) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari



3) Max Verstappen, Red Bull



4) Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari



5) Oscar Piastri, McLaren



6) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



7) Lando Norris, McLaren



8) Gabriel Bortoleto, Audi



9) Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls



10) Franco Colapinto, Alpine

How faultless Antonelli was made to win the hard way

Mercedes' world championship leader had been the big favourite to win the race after qualifying on a dominant pole position but the 19-year-old's route to victory on Sunday did not prove quite as straightforward as many had expected across a tense 44 laps of racing at Spa-Francorchamps.

Antonelli had, though, always expected a battle to hold his lead through the first lap of the race from fellow front-row-starter Verstappen in particular due to the slipstream-friendly nature of the opening part of the undulating, power-sensitive Belgian lap.

He held the lead on the short initial run to La Source but, whether due to a tactical approach to his energy-deployment usage or not relative to his Red Bull pursuer, he was overtaken by Verstappen before the bottom of the uphill fast Eau Rouge.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Drama at the start of the Belgium GP as George Russell's title hopes take a huge blow

But Antonelli had more battery in hand for the long Kemmel Straight and duly breezed straight back past the Red Bull before the next braking zone from Les Combes. Leclerc, meanwhile, had made an impressive start from fourth place and also passed Verstappen for second at the same point.

Verstappen got back ahead of the Ferrari on lap six and, impressively given pre-race expectations, managed to keep Antonelli in view and was less than three seconds behind the Mercedes when he pitted on lap 17. Antonelli pitted a lap later and stayed ahead of the Red Bull to maintain the net lead.

But Ferrari had kept both their drivers out for longer and benefitted when, on lap 20, the Virtual Safety Car was initiated. This allowed their drivers relatively 'cheap' pit stops and, while Hamilton ran into problems in addition to having to first serve his penalty for the Russell collision, Leclerc was able to jump Antonelli and Verstappen into the lead.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes Kimi Antonelli discusses his Belgian GP win and admits he's in a 'good position' after opening up a 45-point gap in the drivers' standings.

The gap between Leclerc and Antonelli was three seconds but the Mercedes simply had too much speed and on lap 34 regained the lead with a pass down the Kemmel Straight.

Antonelli went on to win by 1.9s and said after his first win in four races: "It's great to be back on the top step after obviously a few difficult rounds.

"It was a hard-fought race. We lost first place with a VSC but then we managed to make our way back.

"It was a tough win because Charles was quick and we had to hold onto them."

Second place follows Leclerc's victory at Silverstone a fortnight ago and the Monegasque said: "I believed in the win until the end.

"We had a little bit of luck with the VSC at the right time for us but the pace was relatively strong.

"There were five or six laps on the hard tyres when I was struggling with the front axle, then it came back a little bit."

Sports.title: Russell blames Mercedes power issue for collision with Hamilton
Sports.content:
George Russell says a power issue with his Mercedes was to blame for leaving him vulnerable to a first-lap collision with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton that took him out of the Belgian Grand Prix.

Russell started third on the grid and retained his position through the first corner but was then passed by Hamilton and left side-by-side with McLaren's Oscar Piastri as they came to the end of the lengthy Kemmel Straight.

Russell broke late and attempted to reclaim third back around the outside of Hamilton, but the pair made contact which spun the Mercedes into the gravel and out of the race.

Despite Hamilton being given a five-second penalty by the stewards for causing the collision, Russell told Sky Sports F1 he was more frustrated with his car than his former team-mate.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell pointed to an issue with the car as a reason for his collision with Lewis Hamilton during the Belgian GP

"I just got totally swallowed up down the straight," said Russell, who dropped 50 points behind his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli after the championship leader won the race.

"I lost three positions down the straight down into Turn Five and then the incident was a racing incident.

"Maybe I could have gone a bit wider, maybe he (Hamilton) could have braked a bit more. The incident shouldn't have happened if I had the speed down the straight.

"Very, very disappointed."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Belgian Grand Prix

The incident came after Russell had bemoaned a lack of power costing him in qualifying on Saturday, when he was more than half a second off pole-sitter Antonelli in fourth.

Russell has appeared confused in recent weeks as to what is causing him to generally be unable to match Antonelli's pace.

He said on Thursday's media day at Spa that he was working on changing his driving style as he believes that was costing him time in 2026's new generation of cars, but on Saturday revealed that he had changed his mind and no longer thought his driving style was the issue.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Russell discusses his recent struggles with the Mercedes car and the gap between himself and teammate Kimi Antonelli

Asked how Mercedes can get to the bottom of the issue, Russell added: "I appreciate everyone is working hard to solve the problem, but I'm stood here [in the TV interview pen] on lap five of the race.

"It felt like I was in a good position to fight for the lead up to Turn One and then, suddenly, no power and it's all gone."

Wolff: Issue caused all Mercedes engines to lack power on straights

Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said there was an issue with all of the team's engines that influenced power on the straights.

As well as building their own engines, Mercedes also supply McLaren, Alpine and Williams with power units.

Wolff told Sky Sports F1: "The accident that happened was unfortunate for us. We lost a lot of constructors' points and George's drivers' points.

"We had an issue on all Mercedes engines that we lacked the power out on the straights. That hit him badly and it 100 per cent goes on us.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Karun Chandhok was at the SkyPad to analyse whether Lewis Hamilton should have been awarded a five-second penalty for his collision with George Russell on the opening lap

"We are trying our best as a team. We have the most powerful power unit, a strong car that is capable of winning.

"Everyone is giving their maximum to minimise the mistakes and still it happens because we are humans at work."

Mercedes have clearly had the fastest car over the opening 10 rounds of the season, but reliability issues have prevented them from building a points advantage to reflect their pace dominance.

Russell's DNF on Sunday was his second following an engine failure in Canada, while Antonelli retired in Barcelona because of an engine failure and then dropped from a likely victory to out of the points at Silverstone because of a wheel-guard failure.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli wins the Belgian Grand Prix

Wolff added: "We let Kimi down at Silverstone where George got a podium, which is maybe better than the result should have been.

"Then one DNF for Montreal, the other in Barcelona. That's a little bit of the story of our season. It's a technical sport, a mechanical sport.

"We came out with a product [power unit] that is so strong and I'd rather fix the reliability rather than accelerate a slow engine, or slow car.

"We are giving it 100 per cent and need to give it 100 per cent because we lost a lot of points with reliability. We should be much further ahead than we are."

Sports.title: McIlroy 'stuck in neutral' at The Open and reveals rest of season plans
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy has set his sights on a strong finish to the PGA Tour and DP World Tour seasons after being ‘stuck in neutral’ during a disappointing week at The 154th Open.

McIlroy was among the favourites to challenge for a second major of the year and first win at The Open since 2014, having already defended his title at The Masters in April, although was never in contention during a frustrating display at Royal Birkdale.

The world No 2 rallied from an opening-round 72 to post scores of 67 and 69 to head into the final day eight strokes behind leader Sam Burns, with McIlroy falling further down the leaderboard with a one-over 71 on Sunday.

Image: Rory McIlroy surged at the start of his final round on Sunday

"I was sort of stuck in neutral for most of the week," McIlroy admitted. "Obviously shot a good one on Friday to get myself in for the weekend and back in it, but even par over the weekend is not going to get it done.

"I just felt like any time I got a little bit of momentum out there, I seemed to make a bogey. Just one of those weeks I couldn't get it going."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy spoke to the media after his third round of The Open and said he was not impressed with Bryson DeChambeau's actions that led to his two-stroke penalty

McIlroy has finished no higher than tied-seventh in his six worldwide starts since becoming the first back-to-back winner at Augusta National since Tiger Woods, ending in that position at the PGA Championship and failing to contend at the US Open.

McIlroy will now return to action in the FedExCup Play-Offs before switching his focus to the DP World Tour, with back-to-back appearances at the Amgen Irish Open and BMW PGA Championship in September.

"The season feels very similar to last season," McIlroy admitted. "Obviously won the first major of the year and fell off a little bit after that. Any time you win a major in a year, you have to be pleased about that.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the final round of The Masters, where Rory McIlroy defended his title

"I haven't really took the time to enjoy that or celebrate that [major win]. Poppy [daughter] has got another four weeks off school until she goes back, so just going to enjoy the summer holidays with her and Erica. That's what I'm looking forward to the most.

"Then I'll get back to playing and I'm still in a decent position, I guess, in both title races. As long as I'm in the top 30 going into the Tour Championship and then I'm in a decent spot still in the Race to Dubai.

"I'll try to play hard until the end of the season and then try to win one or both of those titles."

McIlroy will fall short of the PGA Tour's 15-event minimum for the 2026 season, having made just 11 starts so far, with the 37-year-old unsure of what the repercussions will be for not fulfilling his requirement.

"There's been years where I've given it maybe more of my attention [to the PGA Tour] and years that I haven't," McIlroy explained. "I guess I'm just at a stage that I have other things that I prioritise.

Image: McIlroy mixed four birdies with three bogeys and a double

"The PGA Tour is in a lot of flux at the minute with a lot of their schedule and structure and everything like that. It doesn't matter where you are in the top 30 going into the Tour Championship.

"I just need to be in the top 30 going in there to have a chance to win a FedExCup, so why would I care about the first two? I came to that decision last year, and I'm just doing the same thing."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rory McIlroy discussed the PGA Tour's new-look schedule ahead of the US Open last month and shared his concerns about it

What's next?

The next PGA Tour event is the 3M Open at TPC Twin Cities in Minnesota, beginning Thursday, with early coverage on Sky Sports+ before switching to Sky Sports Golf at 7pm.

The 3M Open is part of a triple-header of live golf on Sky Sports, with the ISPS Handa Senior Open and ISPS Handa Women's Scottish Open also live.
