Sports.title: Top ten highest goalscorers of all time: Cristiano Ronaldo eyes 1000 career goals as Lionel Messi continues to break records
Sports.content:
Top ten highest goalscorers of all time: Cristiano Ronaldo eyes 1000 career goals as Lionel Messi continues to break records

Cristiano Ronaldo is now 41 and Lionel Messi isn't far off 40, but they are still scoring goals for fun as the GOAT debate rumbles on...

Messi is a World Cup winner after leading Argentina to glory in Qatar in 2022, but former Manchester United star Ronaldo, who is still missing a World Cup success, continues to stake his claim as the best ever in Saudi Arabia.



7 Ronaldo and Messi are two of the best scorers in football history

Both are footballing greats and they are still netting goals at unbelievable rates for Al Nassr and Inter Miami respectively, as well as on the international stage.

But it's Ronaldo who sits well above his rival at the top of the all-time scoring table, as he gets ever closer to reaching the remarkable 1000-goal landmark.

No one has scored more goals recognised by FIFA than Portugal captain Ronaldo, who brought up his 900th strike for club and country against Croatia in the Nations League in September 2024.



Messi has surpassed a host of legendary names throughout his incredible career too, but Ronaldo still remains at the very top.

Both goalscoring greats are looking for more before they retire, while Luis Suarez and Harry Kane are the only active players who could get near the top ten scorers of all time.



Suarez has reached the landmark of 600 goals, with England's top scorer Kane having over 500 career goals to date.

According to the statistics from the IFFHS, here's who makes the list of the top ten highest goalscorers of all time...



10. Joe Bambrick - 626 goals

Northern Irish forward Bambrick will be a name that not many will have heard of these days.

The ex-Chelsea and Walsall striker played between 1926 and 1939, netting his 600+ goals across that period.

Bambrick scored 33 goals for Chelsea in 61 appearances, with them all coming in the old First Division.

He also netted 11 times in 11 games for Northern Ireland on the international stage.



9. Gerd Muller - 634 goals

The striker’s most important goal of the 68 he banged in for West Germany was the winner in the 1974 World Cup final against the Netherlands in Munich.

During a historic 15 years at Bayern, Muller netted a record 365 goals in 427 Bundesliga games and 66 goals in 74 European matches.

His record of 40 goals scored in a single Bundesliga season stood for 49 years, and was broken by Robert Lewandowski in May 2021.

Kane is now playing his football in Germany and he came very close to join Lewandowski in breaking Muller's record.



7 Müller won the Ballon d'Or in 1970 and is a German legend Credit: AFP

8. Jimmy Jones - 639 goals

Similar to No.10 in this list, Bambrick, Jones is another Northern Irish former striker who loved to score goals.

He played from 1943 until 1965, playing for 10 different teams and netting over 600 times in his career.

The forward, who passed away in 2014, spent some time at Fulham and scored most of his goals for Glenavon.



Jones also made three caps for the Northern Ireland national team.

7. Robert Lewandowski - 697 goals

If Lewandowski played in a different generation than Messi and Ronaldo, he would be much more appreciated than he is.

The Polish international is his country's most-capped player and top goalscorer and is a legend back home.

He is also Bayern Munich's second-top goalscorer behind only the great Muller, not bad for a free transfer from Borussia Dortmund.

The 37-year-old left Bayern in the summer of 2023 for a switch to Barcelona, where he continued to score goals despite ageing.



Lewandowski scored 120 times for Barca in four seasons, while the Pole is also the third-top goalscorer in Champions League history.

Perhaps when he retires, we will all appreciate just how good Lewandowski was.

7 Lewandowski is one of the greatest goalscorers of the modern era Credit: Getty

6. Josef Bican - 722 goals

The legendary striker scored an incredible 395 in 217 games for Slavia Prague from 1937 to 1948.



He also starred for multiple clubs in Czechia, racking up an unbelievable amount of goals.

This means that Bican was football’s leading goalscorer of all time for decades.

Although it's said he scored close to 1,500 goals in total during his playing days, only around half of those were recognised by FIFA.

5. Ferenc Puskas - 725 goals

A Hungarian icon, Puskas now lends his name to the award for the most beautiful goal of each year.



The striker made his name in Budapest before cementing his legend at Real Madrid.

He scored over 150 goals for Los Blancos, averaging almost a goal a game.

Two of Puskas' most famous goals came in Hungary's famous 6-3 win over England, with the 1953 match at Wembley later being coined the 'Match of the Century'.

7 Puskas celebrates his first goal in the Match of the Century Credit: Getty Images - Getty



4. Romario - 756 goals

Romario led Brazil to World Cup glory in 1994, scoring five goals in the tournament.

He also enjoyed a stellar career at a number of top clubs around the world.

The forward played for 10 teams in total, making over 700 appearances.

His time at PSV gave him the most success in front of goal as he scored 98 goals in just 110 matches.



Romario also netted 55 times in 70 caps for his country.

3. Pele - 762 goals

One of the greatest ever and a three-time World Cup winner.

Pele only played for two clubs while leading Brazil to glory throughout his career.

He scored nearly a goal per game during his 656 competitive games for Santos, though he claims to have scored more than 1,000 times.

However, it is widely accepted that hundreds of those goals came during tour or friendly matches. Pele would have told you otherwise!

The icon passed away in 2022, but his legacy lives on in the footballing world.



7 Pele made his debut for Brazil when he was just 16, winning his first World Cup at 17 Credit: Getty

2. Lionel Messi - 924 goals

A true legend, Messi has won countless trophies to go along with his goals, including a record eight Ballon d'Or awards.

Now with Inter Miami in the United States, the Argentine has a few years left to add to his remarkable tally and is now over 900 career goals.

Messi scored seven times at the World Cup in Qatar, with two in the dramatic penalty shootout win over France in the final surely proving to be the most special in his entire career.



He netted over 650 times for Barcelona before moving on to PSG where he scored 32 more.

The icon now plays in America's MLS and continues to score goals and win trophies, while also still starring for Argentina on the international stage, helping them win the 2024 Copa America.

He broke the all-time World Cup goalscoring record during the 2026 tournament in USA, Canada and Mexico.

7 Messi is now the all-time World Cup record goalscorer, taking Miroslav Klose's record at the 2026 tournament Credit: Getty



1. Cristiano Ronaldo - 976 goals

A modern great for Portugal, Manchester United and Real Madrid, Ronaldo has won everything in the game and is still going strong today.

Ronaldo is the only player to score at six separate World Cups - and he is not done yet with talk of retirement being premature, according to the man himself.

In fact, Ronaldo has broken more boundaries, securing the most expensive contract in sports' history with Saudi Arabian side Al Nassr.

He has reached the incredible milestone of 500 career league goals while at the club and hit 100 goal contributions for them in January.



On the international stage, he has also moved on to 233 international caps - a world record - and he hasn't stopped scoring, netting 146 times for his country.

Ronaldo has become the first player ever to score 900 career goals and he is eyeing 1000 before he retires after turning 41, with his 976th career goal being his first in a World Cup knockout game during Portugal's 2-1 win over Croatia.

Sports.title: Mayhem at World Cup final before Trump arrives as staff misdirect fans outside stadium and tension simmers over ticket issues - but Tom Cruise has no trouble getting in!
Sports.content:
Mayhem at World Cup final before Trump arrives as staff misdirect fans outside stadium and tension simmers over ticket issues - but Tom Cruise has no trouble getting in!

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

World Cup final day got off to a chaotic start at MetLife Stadium with fans forced to wait for hours outside of the venue amid reports of technological glitches scanning tickets and security staff unsure of how to manage the crowds.

Organizers this week urged fans lucky enough to have a ticket to arrive up to four hours before the start of the game at the 80,000-seater stadium in New Jersey, a short drive outside of Manhattan, for Sunday's showdown between Spain and Argentina.

As the build-up to the game expected to be watched by billions around the world ramped up, fans were waiting for over four hours to have their tickets scanned in order to enter the stadium for the showpiece game.

The attendance of President Donald Trump meant that airport-style security measures were also being enforced for everyone making their way inside of the venue.

But the delays were compounded amid reports of glitches in FIFA's ticket-scanning system, meaning those who were fortunate enough to be at the front of the long lines still faced frustrating delays.

Daily Mail also witnessed tensions simmering between fans, media members and security staff, with officials on the ground telling anyone who complained: 'Take it up with FIFA'.

Thousands of fans and media members faced massive lines to enter the stadium for the World Cup final on Sunday amid several reports of security struggling to manage the situation

There were reports to tech issues and security misdirecting people around the stadium

Argentina fans arrive at MetLife Stadium before Sunday's hugely anticipated final vs Spain

But those members of security staff also appeared to be confused over how to manage the thousands of people arriving for the game.

There were multiple instances of organizers on the ground misdirecting people over where they should begin lining up to enter the stadium with over three hours to go until the start of the game.

Sky's Rob Harris also posted on X from the stadium: 'Fans told to get to the World Cup final stadium now 4 hours before KO - already security staff saying FIFA system glitches not scanning passes and long queues forming. With extra security. People being misdirected around the stadium with a lack of stewarding and staffing.'

Brazilian journalist Mariana Spinelli said it took her four hours to make it in, writing on X: 'We've been in line for 2 hours for the x-ray to ENTER the stadium. Everything disorganized, a total chaos. If this were in South America, they'd call us animals, third-world country. Since it's in the US nobody says anything. A nightmare of organization, pathetic.'

Media members also faced extra checks from the secret service given the need to bring laptops and filming equipment inside of the stadium. DHS police and state police were also seen at the venue.

This all played out as other fans decided to leave it late to get to the stadium. With four hours to go utnil the game began, many supporters were still at Penn Station in Manhattan waiting to board a train into New Jersey and towards the stadium.

The game is set to be the most expensive to attend in the history of sport - on Sunday morning, the cheapest ticket available on most resale websites was starting at around $7,000.

FIFA encouraged fans to arrive early in order to participate in the World Cup closing ceremony, scheduled to begin around 90 minutes before the game itself kicks off.

Extra security checks were in place ahead of the attendance of President Trump for the game

Tom Cruise had no such issue making his way inside before his closing ceremony appearance

But it is standard procedure for fans to arrive early for additional security checks whenever Trump attends a sporting event - and he has made it to plenty in his second term as President, ranging from the Ryder Cup to the Super Bowl.

Even on the live television coverage, the stadium was bare with a little over an hour until that closing ceremony began.

There weren't quite as many issues for the VIP guests, though. Tom Cruise was pictured sauntering into the venue - renamed as 'New York/New Jersey Stadium' for the tournament - ahead of his anticipated appearance in the closing ceremony.

Soccer greats such as Brazil World Cup winner Ronaldo, former England captain John Terry and former Argentina player Diego Simeone all appeared carefree as they entered the stadium in good time before the game.

Fans were slow to fill the stadium despite a call for them be in place for the closing ceremony

There were plenty of fans who were determined not to let the chaos ruin their day, too. Thousands of Argentina fans have made the journey to the stadium for what will likely be star man Lionel Messi's last ever appearance in a World Cup at the age of 39.

Argentina are narrow underdogs against Spain, the European champions, despite being the holders after winning the 2022 tournament in Qatar.

Trump is expected to hand the World Cup trophy over to the winning team after the game.

Sports.title: 'Numb' George Russell's Formula One world championship dream plunges into jeopardy as Kimi Antonelli seizes on team-mate's opening lap crash with Lewis Hamilton to take commanding lead after Belgian Grand Prix win
Sports.content:
George Russell claimed he is ‘numb to disappointment’ but his pained face told a different story after his first lap collision with Lewis Hamilton ended his Belgian Grand Prix.

Poor George is growing accustomed to summoning words to describe slings and Silver Arrows of outrageous fortune he cannot fully comprehend.

His world title dream is in rising jeopardy and questions crowd his bamboozled mind.

Why is he not as fast as Kimi Antonelli, the race winner and championship leader, in the same Mercedes machinery?

Why is he suffering dramatic loss of pace in a straight line?

Why are all the expectations he embraced as the pre-season favourite eluding him week after week?

The story of his cameo at Spa nailed those doubts further into his frontal lobe. Starting third he was cleanly away – ‘a great first corner’, as he noted wryly – before he was practically reduced to running on the spot along the Kemmel Straight.

George Russell crashed out of the Belgian Grand Prix after colliding with Lewis Hamilton

Russell was sent into the gravel after being clipped by the Ferrari in the opening lap in Spa

Sunday's result serves as a major blow to Russell's championship hopes

He slipped back to sixth, as if stuck in treacle, on the approach to Les Combes, the right-left combination. He was fractionally ahead of Hamilton’s Ferrari at this stage, but they were overlapping.

His rear-right wheel entangled itself with Hamilton’s front-left. Russell spun around into the gravel, where he was beached. He held his gloved palms open in an expression of torment before climbing out of the cockpit unhurt, physically at least.

Hamilton was handed a harsh five-second penalty for his role in the clumsy footwork, but went on to finish fourth – despite knocking over one of his mechanics in the pits. So, the seven-time world champion leapfrogged Russell as Antonelli’s closest challenger, 45 points back. Russell is 50 from the top. It was the third time in 10 races he had failed to finish.

‘For whatever reason the battery decided not to recharge at Turn One,’ lamented a nonplussed Russell.

‘I exited the first corner 35 per cent down. The turbo didn’t sort itself out, so no power. I got to the top of Eau Rouge with zero per cent battery and quite frankly it was dangerous.

‘I got swamped by three cars and I shouldn’t have been in that position. It is why I am most angry.

‘The incident with Lewis was a racing incident. He was more to blame than I was. But he didn’t do anything reckless or on purpose.

A triumphant Antonelli, doused in champagne, shows off his driver's trophy at Spa

Lewis Hamilton’s day was certainly eventful, having skirmishes with Leclerc and Russell

‘It is something every day now. I am numb to disappointment. When it happens so often you get used to it.’

Russell’s travails here in Spa related to this year’s mind-bendingly complex engines, in which battery power is spent and recaptured each lap. They are so unfathomable that not even his most pointy-headed boffins can explain the intermittent lack of deployment that seems to be afflicting Russell more than anyone else.

He complained on Saturday of a mystery problem that uniquely cost him – not Antonelli – time on the straights, and then in the race came a glitch he and his team principal Toto Wolff both confirmed was a separate issue.

Will Mercedes, so far lost for answers, find solutions ahead of Budapest coming next weekend? They certainly owe Russell an explanation and a remedy.

While the Englishman was kicking his heels in the paddock, 19-year-old Antonelli was in clear command on the track. His only concern came when a Virtual Safety Car, brought about by debris, permitted the Ferraris a cheap stop. Charles Leclerc lucked into the lead as a result.

But Antonelli, his confidence soaring as the season ripens, made the decisive pass on Leclerc along the Kemmel Straight with 10 laps remaining. Thus the Italian secured his sixth victory of his campaign. Leclerc took second place, ahead of Red Bull’s Max Verstappen.

Hamilton’s day was eventful. Having survived his skirmish with Russell, he and Leclerc went wheel-to-wheel soon afterwards. The red pair nearly touched, hearts in mouths. Leclerc was feisty, as he also showed in an earlier brush with McLaren’s Oscar Piastri.

Hamilton pitted with Leclerc and served his penalty there and then. That done, he was shown the green light to go. The mechanic holding the gun on the front-left tyre was still in his path and his right knee was caught by the accelerating Ferrari. He promptly fell to the floor while practically hugging the wheel.

‘Oh, God, I am grateful my mechanic didn’t get hurt,’ said Hamilton. ‘I am looking at the lights, and am supposed to go when the car is dropping to the ground. I went. Then I saw him and stopped as soon as I could.

‘All I could think about was when Kimi (Raikkonen) broke a mechanic’s leg (in Bahrain eight years ago). I thought that had happened initially, but he got up and moved.’

The welcome medical bulletin did not prevent Ferrari landing a £25,500 fine, with £8,500 suspended for 12 months, for the unsafe release.

Piastri came home fifth, a place ahead of Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar and two in front of defending champion Lando Norris, the old pal whose maiden title success Russell is trying to emulate. If only he were not driving with the handbrake on.

Sports.title: Donald Trump makes World Cup final prediction between Argentina and Spain - with the help of son Barron
Sports.content:
Donald Trump makes World Cup final prediction between Argentina and Spain - with the help of son Barron

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Donald Trump has backed Lionel Messi and Argentina to beat Spain in the World Cup final on Sunday.

Speaking to Fox reporter Jenny Taft, Trump said: 'Well, I knew you were going to ask me so I thought about it a lot. I hate to get involved even though poltically it doesn't matter so much.

'I would say that it is hard to bet against Messi. I watched that pass, it was exacrtly perfect (to Lautaro Martinez to score the winning goal against England). But that was perfect, if you had a strike zone it was exactly where it had to be.

'I just think it is very hard to bet against Messi, he is great.'

While discussing the all-time greats of the game Trump, who is attending the game, added that his son Barron, 20, talks a lot to him about soccer and shares a lot of his knowledge about the game with him.

'Messi is great and Ronaldo is great and I hate to say this but I watched Pele when he was with the Cosmos,' Trump said. 'I got to see Pele play. These are great players.

Donald Trump backs Lionel Messi and Argentina to win the World Cup final on Sunday

Trump pictured with son Barron and Zlatan Ibrahimovic at UFC 250 at the White House in June

'There are some others. I get this information from my son, my son Barron is a tremendous soccer fan.

'You really have some other really incredible players playing here but I would say right now, when you look, I have always liked Ronaldo, I've always like Messi.

'I met Messi just recently and I have known Cristiano. They have a pretty good life - much easier than my life, actually!'

Trump recently hosted Messi and Inter Miami at the White House to celebrate their 2025 Major League Soccer title.

Trump added that he is friendly with Argentina's leader, Javier Milei. The same cannot be said of Spain.

Trump launched a stinging attack on the country at a UN summit earlier in July for not contributing enough money to NATO.

'Spain is a terrible partner in NATO. They don’t participate. They don’t pay. I don’t want anything to do with Spain. Cut off all trade with Spain, please, including visits,' he said.

'Don’t even talk to them. They’re hopeless, bad people.'

Trump hosted Messi and his Inter Miami team at the White House back in March

Then, on his way back to the United States on Air Force One, Trump said Spain had tried to improve their standings with him.

'I did have issues, and ​I still do. But Spain, they came back all the way today. Spain was very generous today,' he said.

'They honoured a request for lots of payments, and if they didn't, we wouldn't have even ⁠talked to them.'

Days later, though, and Trump could find himself center stage for an historic moment for Spain, who are the favorites to win the competition on Sunday.

Trump is expected to hand the trophy over to the winning team after the game.

Sports.title: Emiliano Martinez reveals he has been playing with 'extremely painful' fractured finger throughout the World Cup - but ignored surgery advice
Sports.content:
Emiliano Martinez reveals he has been playing with 'extremely painful' fractured finger throughout the World Cup - but ignored surgery advice

How much is David Beckham set to pocket from his World Cup brand deals? Take on our quiz in our newsletter HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Argentina and Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez has revealed he has been playing through 'extreme pain' at the World Cup after fracturing his finger on the eve of the tournament.

The former Arsenal shot-stopper has been an ever-present for the defending champions in North America, who will claim their second World Cup trophy in as many tournaments if they can beat Spain on Sunday night.

Martinez will start in goal, but is some way off being fully fit after picking up an injury while playing for Aston Villa.

'My hand still hurts every day; I knew it was going to be extremely painful,' he said in the build-up to the final. 'I avoided surgery, even though all the specialists I consulted in the United States and England told me I needed to have it.

'I couldn't train during the group stage, but from the Round of 16 onwards after Egypt, I stopped thinking about it, and I feel much better.'

Martinez picked up the issue during the warm-up ahead of Aston Villa's Europa League final win over Freiburg.

Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez has said he has been playing through 'extreme pain' at the World Cup

He strapped his finger to play in that game, but would miss Argentina's World Cup warm-up matches before making the tournament.

'The coach sent me a message saying, 'No matter what state you're in, I want you on my team',' Martinez continued.

'To me, that means more than saving 10 penalties or making the front page of the newspaper. And if my moment doesn't come but we win the final, it will mean just as much.'

The 33-year-old played a key role in the 2022 final win over France, saving a late effort from Randal Kolo Muani before stopping a penalty in the shootout.

This year, however, he is enjoying himself more, and has his sights set on taking the trophy home again.

'We've been improving year after year with this team,' Martinez continued. 'Sometimes I tear up just thinking about what we've achieved. There are still moments of joy and celebration ahead.

'I'm enjoying this World Cup much more than the last one. I suffered a lot after the Saudi Arabia match in Qatar.

'I didn't face many shots, yet I conceded goals. I only played a decisive role during the penalty shootouts. I think I'm playing better with my feet now. I'll step onto the pitch on Sunday, and you'll see me smiling.

'I feel very calm. A goalkeeper's role goes beyond just making saves during the match; you have to come off your line and project confidence. These are footballing aspects that reassure my teammates, I need to show them I'm composed.'

Sports.title: Heartwarming moment England stars urge fourth-choice goalkeeper Jason Steele to collect a bronze medal after win over France - even though unsung hero wasn't in the squad!
Sports.content:
England stars including Jude Bellingham urged goalkeeper Jason Steele to join the team on stage to collect their bronze medals at the World Cup in a heartwarming moment.

Steele, 35, has never been capped by the senior team but has been in and around camps with Tuchel as a bridge between management and the players.

The Brighton shot-stopper is essentially fourth choice for the Three Lions, but wasn’t part of the official squad for the tournament in the USA and Mexico.

He has, however, been training with the team, while also cheering them on during games and playing a key role behind the scenes.

Steele watched on as the players were awarded with their bronze medals after beating France 6-4 on Saturday, but was quickly ushered on to the podium.

The likes of Bellingham and Rogers called for Steele to join them, and the former Sunderland man ran across the pitch to collect a medal, which was placed on him by Jordan Henderson.

The England squad make sure goalkeeper Jason Steele comes to collect his bronze medal 🥉🤝 pic.twitter.com/u8E7JVF9cE — Match of the Day (@BBCMOTD) July 19, 2026

England players called over reserve goalkeeper Jason Steele (centre) to collect a bronze medal after the win against France

Steele played for England at youth level but has never played for the senior team. He received his first call-up in March, and was taken to North America as a training goalkeeper.

Last season, he played five games for Brighton, all coming in cup competitions.

He has been a regular in previous seasons, however, and has more than 350 professional appearances to his name.

Tuchel said after naming his squad in May: ‘We chose three goalkeepers plus Jason Steele.

‘I want to take the opportunity to thank Jason for being brilliant and thank Brighton for being so co-operative and supportive.’

Steele is set to be second-choice goalkeeper at Brighton again next season, supporting Bart Verbruggen.

His deal at the club runs until the end of the next campaign.

Sports.content:
Steve Borthwick’s spiky post-match comments after England’s win in Argentina were unlike him.

I worked closely alongside Steve with both Japan and England, so I know very well he’s a methodical man. He’s not often prone to emotion or strong statements in the media. That’s why his latest press conference has made headlines.

When questioned by journalists on his team’s four second-half yellow cards in their 31-24 victory over the Pumas, Steve responded: ‘As ever, you guys (media) concentrate upon the negativity. I love it. You’re my negativity committee. It’s lovely coming in and talking to you again.’

There was real emotion in those words. I’ve no doubt Steve would have been feeling under severe pressure going into the game in Santiago del Estero. Equally, I’m also sure he’d have felt a degree of vindication by the result in what was a must-win game.

That’s why he went on the front foot post-match. I think it was a good move. I don’t mind it at all. Over the years I’ve not been afraid of throwing a few bombs out there in press conferences. I’ve learned that it’s not always the best idea but at times, there’s nothing wrong with saying how you feel.

Coaches are only human and when you’re under pressure, as Steve has been this year, sometimes that all boils up to the surface. I’ve been in Steve’s shoes as England coach and the pressure is immense. It’s the same for all the coaches in the country’s three main sports – football, cricket and rugby.

Eddie Jones was impressed by Immanuel Feyi-Waboso's performance for England in their victory over Argentina

Steve Borthwick hit back at the 'negativity committee' in the wake of England's victory

You’ve seen the heat Thomas Tuchel and Brendon McCullum have also had to deal with this summer. Tuchel has led England’s footballers to their best World Cup finish since 1966, but he’s still copped plenty of flak for his supposed negative tactics in the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

McCullum has lost his job as England Test cricket coach after a poor run of form. As an England coach in any sport, it’s tough to win. If you deliver victories, they’re seen as expected. If you lose, you should be sacked.

Steve has already experienced plenty of highs and lows as England rugby boss and I’ve no doubt that rollercoaster ride played a part in his latest comments. As a coach, press conferences are your chance to get the messages you want to give across to the players and the fans.

You go into them with a plan. So too do the journalists. Your job is to get the headlines you want and not the ones the media are aiming for! That doesn’t always happen and there are occasions when emotions take over and your plan goes out the window.

I don’t know if Steve planned to say what he did, but I would doubt it. I think he was entitled to say what he did because I thought England’s latest win was very impressive.

The media analysis has focused on the four second-half yellow cards given to Jack van Poortvliet, Alex Coles, Henry Pollock and Emmanuel Iyogun which at one point left England down to 12 men. They have received 14 cards in their last 10 Tests, so the issue was a valid discussion point for the press.

But as much as the media are entitled to ask questions on what they see as the main issue, as a coach you are also allowed to focus on your point of view. If I was in Steve’s shoes, I’d have been very, very pleased. The context of the game taking place just after England's heartbreaking football World Cup defeat by the same nation added an extra layer of emotion. As such, I thought their start was absolutely outstanding.

In the first half, they were direct and purposeful, scoring three tries and playing as an England team should. It was really impressive. I thought Immanuel Feyi-Waboso was out of this world. You don’t often see a winger dominate a game as he did. He was always looking for work and his strong carrying put England on the front foot. So too did Ellis Genge and Ollie Chessum. Those three players were my standouts. The second period was different.

Argentina went to the air and had some joy winning the ball back there. That allowed them to put pressure on England, which led to the yellow cards. It’s far from ideal to lose four men to the sin bin and better teams than Argentina would have punished England.

Remarkably dramatic end to the game, which saw TMO overturn Angus Gardner's on-field decision of a try, giving England the tightest of wins.



Should the try have stood? 👇 pic.twitter.com/w0MiNVOamD — ITV Rugby (@ITVRugby) July 19, 2026

Had Henry Slade not tackled Bautista Delguy into touch at the death, England might have drawn the game. But the bottom line is they didn’t and I thought England did very well to get out of trouble with the tries from Feyi-Waboso and Marcus Smith. That relief at coming through such adversity would also have played a part in what Steve said to the media.

Referee Angus Gardner awarded a try to Delguy on the field, but television match official Brett Cronan insisted to him the player was in touch. I think the correct decision was reached in the end.

At the same time, I also think we’ve got to get a clearer protocol on when the TMO should come in. My view is he or she should only be able to make a decision on an incident three phases or fewer before a try is scored or for an out-and-out red card.

The TMO should always be able to tell the on-field referee what they’ve seen. But the main official has to have ownership of the game. Constant checking with the TMO is not good for the game. It takes far too long.

Two wins from three matches this summer was a decent way for Steve and England to bounce back from what was, statistically, the country’s worst-ever Six Nations. But what will be occupying Steve’s mind in the next few months is how his team can make the jump to being able to compete with international rugby’s top sides.

At the moment, I don’t think England can. The final round of the Nations Championship at the weekend showed that South Africa, New Zealand, Ireland and France are well ahead of the rest. Then, there is quite a big gap to the likes of England.

Four England players were sent to the sin bin by referee Angus Gardner during the second half of Saturday's clash

England need to find a way to improve their discipline ahead of next year's World Cup

South Africa have been able to use countless players and still win. France have similarly impressive depth. New Zealand have had a promising start to life under Dave Rennie. Steve’s challenge is to be really, really clear on how he can get closer to these teams. England have to be able to put pressure on teams for longer periods. At the moment, they release the valve too often.

They did it at times in their defeat by South Africa, but not for long enough. Even against a team like Argentina, who haven’t been playing well, England let their opposition get on top. That’s where the ill-discipline and yellow cards came from.

As I wrote after the South Africa game, I wouldn’t be worried about England’s discipline as an overriding issue. Yellow cards are a byproduct of being under pressure. What Steve has to work out is how to stop that happening in the first place.

If he doesn’t solve that conundrum, England won’t be genuine contenders to win next year’s World Cup which will always be the target for the RFU’s top bosses. And at that point, the pressure will soon return.

Sports.title: Arsenal to receive millions in FIFA compensation after disastrous World Cup blow
Sports.content:
Arsenal to receive millions in FIFA compensation after disastrous World Cup blow

Arsenal will be handed millions of pounds in compensation as a result of one of their key players suffering a serious injury at the 2026 World Cup

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta will be without William Saliba for the start of the new season after an injury to the defender (Image: ANTONIN THUILLIER, AFP via Getty Images)

Arsenal are expected to receive over £4million as a result of William Saliba's back injury at the 2026 World Cup. The 24-year-old has been battling through the pain barrier since March, but broke down during France's 2-0 semi-final loss to Spain on Tuesday.

‌



The centre-half was spotted limping off the pitch just 30 minutes into the action, substituted for Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix. It has now emerged that Saliba could be sidelined for up to five months.

‌



He could also require surgery on his back. It mirrors a similar injury he picked up toward the back end of 2022/23.

‌



Bukayo Saka speechless before walking away from BBC interview over England World Cup remark READ MORE :

France boss Didier Deschamps confirmed after the match that Saliba's pain had become "unbearable" during the Spain fixture and the severity of the problem became apparent on the pitch. Then ahead of the World Cup third-place play-off against England, Deschamps offered a further update on Saliba's situation, stating.

He said: "William Saliba got injured and it's problematic. He went through some examinations.

"The injury did not worsen. He faced that injury since March. He had some pain and unfortunately the pain was not bearable."

‌



Arsenal are yet to give any indication of a recovery timeframe, though it's understood Saliba faces could be unavailable until mid-November at the earliest. While the Frenchman's absence will represent a significant setback for Arsenal and Mikel Arteta, the club are set to receive a substantial sum in compensation from FIFA given the back injury was aggravated during the World Cup.

View 2 Images William Saliba's injury worsened during France's clash with Spain at the World Cup (Image: Shaun Botterill, Getty Images)

Since 2012, FIFA's Club Protection Programme has provided cover for the wages of players who sustain injuries while on international duty. There are, however, certain conditions that must be satisfied beforehand.

‌



One stipulates that the player must remain sidelined for a minimum period of 28 consecutive days and that the injury must have been sustained during an 'accident.' Given that Saliba is anticipated to be absent for between four and five months, and that the injury deteriorated while he was competing at the World Cup, Arsenal look well placed to lodge a compensation claim with FIFA for the duration of Saliba's recovery.

It means Arsenal could pocket at least £4m from FIFA to cover Saliba, who is reported to be earning around £250,000 per week at the Emirates Stadium following the signing of a lucrative new deal last September.

‌



While it won't entirely make up for Saliba's absence during that period, it does ease the financial strain and affords Arsenal greater flexibility in the transfer window should they wish to bring in a replacement for the Frenchman.

Aston Villa and England defender Ezri Konsa has been mooted as a summer target after turning heads for the Three Lions at the World Cup. Villa, however, are determined to hold on to the 28-year-old, who is valued at upward of £50m.

Whether Arsenal will opt for a short-term stand-in for Saliba, or pursue someone of Konsa's calibre who can deputise for the former Marseille defender or even slot in at right-back, remains to be seen.

Conor McGregor announces return date as full extent of injury is revealed

Conor McGregor's comeback fight against Max Holloway lasted just 69 seconds after the Irishman injured his knee throwing the first kick of the fight

View Image Conor McGregor after injuring himself

Conor McGregor is targeting a return next summer after revealing he tore his ACL against Max Holloway.

‌



McGregor returned to the cage last weekend following a five year absence but hurt his knee throwing the first kick of the fight. The bout was stopped after just 69 seconds, handing McGregor a TKO loss and another spell on the sidelines. The Irishman has now revealed he tore his ACL and damaged his meniscus.

‌



"It was the ACL and meniscus," he wrote on social media. "It is the same injury as the first Holloway fight, only this time the opposite leg. Quite shocking. I returned to competition within nine months to fight Diego Brandao back then.

‌

I did leg extension machine work the other day to no issue. So I can walk without aid, and activate my quad under resistance. All very positive.

"I am at maximum discipline and have maintained it fully since the bout. I wonder was I saved from something worse here. I believe so. I would have attended the after party as “the man” and who knows then. I believe I was saved."

McGregor had previously announced his determination to return to the cage for the final fight on his UFC contract. "Surgery. Prehab. Return to martial arts practice. Go again. Final fight of the contract. Please God!" he said.

My faith is unconditional and I am thankful I get to prove it! My lifestyle changes are permanent and not just until. I am thankful I get to prove it. I am in Sin City and remain completely devoid of all sin.

Sports.title: Scottie Scheffler rages at The Open as tempers flare in dramatic scenes
Sports.content:
Scottie Scheffler rages at The Open as tempers flare in dramatic scenes

Golf star Scottie Scheffler was fuming after an errant shot during his final round at The Open on Sunday as he attempted to stay in contention around Royal Birkdale

View 2 Images Scottie Scheffler was fuming during the final round of The Open (Image: Sky Sports)

Scottie Scheffler raged after sending his tee shot into the rough on the 17th hole at The Open. The world number one couldn't believe his eyes after he sliced the ball to begin his penultimate hole as he attempted to remain in contention for the Claret Jug.

‌



"What?! Why can...how does that even happen? The ball's slicing. One bounce! One bounce!" he shouted in disbelief. Scheffler fell to his knees, venting, then got up and bent over in frustration.

‌



Things did not get easier from there as he attempted to play his recovery. Taking a metal wood, Scheffler attempted to navigate the mound he found himself behind, but could only send it toward the hospitality tent.

‌



After that wayward effort, Scheffler was forced to mark up a new ball and take a provisional drop. He found the crowd of fans on his second attempt. Unable to find his original ball, a lengthy conversation with a rules official and his caddie, Ted Scott, followed.

The 30-year-old was allowed to take a drop after it was established that his original ball was on the temporary immovable object. It was established that the ball did not need to be found exactly, and instead, a new entry point was used.

Why is it called The Open and not The British Open? READ MORE :

By finding the edge of the temporary immovable object, Scheffler was then able to measure two club lengths, with the ball required to be dropped within the second club length.

‌



Scheffler responded well to his adversity and found the green with a smart approach shot. Oozing class on the green, he was then still able to record a birdie on the par five to bring himself within one shot of the clubhouse lead.

Things were more straightforward on the 18th for Scheffler, who was unable to find the magic required to leave himself in contention. The defending champion could only record par after requiring two putts to find the hole for a final round 67, finishing on -7 for the tournament.

View 2 Images World number one Scottie Scheffler lifted the Claret Jug at Royal Portrush last year (Image: Getty)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Scheffler was unable to find his groove with his putter despite providing himself with a number of opportunities with the quality he showed getting to the green across four days. Speaking after day two, he was pleased to be knocking on the door but ultimately, he could not find the final key to finish in top spot.

“I did a lot of good stuff," Scheffler said on Friday. "I gave myself a lot of opportunities. Wish I holed a few more putts.”

Article continues below

“Just continue to knock on the door, continue to give myself opportunities,” he said. “If I continue to strike it like I did today and yesterday over the next couple of days, I’ll be in a good spot.”

Scheffler produced a better performance than he managed in preparation for the tournament, however. The American failed to make the cut at the Scottish Open just a week before his attempt to defend his Open title.

Sports.title: Spain vs Argentina kick-off time decision as FIFA respond to World Cup final 'threat'
Sports.content:
Spain vs Argentina kick-off time decision as FIFA respond to World Cup final 'threat'

Spain take on Argentina at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on Sunday evening, with thunderstorms threatening FIFA's planned 8pm kick-off time for their showpiece event

View Image Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain will go ahead as planned (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

The 2026 World Cup final will go ahead at its scheduled 8pm kick-off time, despite fears of disruption bythunderstorms. Spain and Argentina are set to get underway at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey on Sunday evening, as this summer's tournament in North America reaches its climax.

‌



World football's most prestigious tournament hasn't been without its teething problems due to unpredictable weather, with a number of matches being postponed or delayed for hours as a result of thunder and lightning. As per US law, any lightning strkes within an eight-mile radius presses pause on play for at least half-an-hour until the most recent detected strike.

‌



That was witnessed during France's group stage clash with Iraq last month, with proceedings being halted for almost two hours due to stormy conditions in and around Philadelphia's Lincoln Financial Field. England's round of 16 battle with Mexico at the Estadio Azteca, meanwhile, was also postponed by an hour due to storms.

‌



Argentina players refuse to give Falklands banner back after England World Cup controversy READ MORE :

BBC's Joe Hart in bizarre video before World Cup final with pundit DRENCHED in monsoon weather READ MORE :

Sunday's final encounter between Spain and Argentina was also cast into doubt as a result of forecasted thunderstorms across New Jersey. Smoke drifting south of the border through Canadian wildfires also brought fears that the location of the showpiece final could be moved altogether due to diminished air quality.

However, FIFA have now confirmed that no changes will be made to the 8pm kick-off time, nor the venue, as conditions continue to be monitored alongside the National Weather Service. It comes as thunderstorms has already disrupted both finalists' preparations.

Spain were scheduled to hold an outdoor training session on Saturday at the Melanie Lane Training Ground, only for it to be suspended due to lightning moving into the locale. A statement was subsequently issued by the Spanish Football Federation.

‌



It read: "The Spanish national team's training session on the pitches at the Melanie Lane Training Ground in New Jersey has been suspended in accordance with the US storm safety protocol. The players are currently taking part in a warm-up session indoors."

Argentina also had to make changes to their own training session in Morristown, kick-starting their preparations 45 minutes late as a result of the adverse weather. It comes as the European and World Champions go head to head on Sunday evening.

‌



Luis de la Fuente's Spain secured their spot in the final thanks to a 2-0 rout over France on Tuesday, Mikel Oyarzabal and Pedro Porro making the difference in that encounter. Argentina, meanwhile, enjoyed a 2-1 win over England on Wednesday, with late goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez cancelling out Anthony Gordon's opener.

Sports.title: Pedro Porro's private life and allegation of cheating with ex-Chelsea star's girlfriend
Sports.content:
Pedro Porro's private life and allegation of cheating with ex-Chelsea star's girlfriend

Tottenham defender Pedro Porro has been one of Spain's standout performers at the World Cup, but his life off the field has also made headlines

View 7 Images Tottenham defender Pedro Porro was once forced to deny having an affair with Joao Felix's girlfriend Magui Corceiro

Tottenham Hotspur's Pedro Porro is one of the standout defenders at the World Cup this summer. The 26-year-old has arguably been the best right-back at the tournament since replacing Marcos Llorente after Spain's dismal 0-0 opening game draw with Cape Verde.

‌



Porro has stepped up and contributed by playing the entirety of five out of the six matches, during which he has scored two goals. One of those came in the semi-final victory over France, where he earned a man of the match award for his heroics.

‌



Whatever the result in the final against Argentina, this will undoubtedly go down as his breakout tournament, with Spurs likely receiving considerable interest in their full-back once it concludes.

‌



Now, Mirror Football takes a look at Porro's equally fascinating life beyond the pitch, specifically his current girlfriend and allegations of an affair involving another famous footballer's partner, which he was forced to deny.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Spain star's brutal comment about Michael Olise in dressing room after World Cup victory READ MORE :

Sensational Spain dominate France to reach World Cup final and set up possible England rematch READ MORE :

Affair rumours

In 2022, Porro denied reports that he was romantically involved with Joao Felix's then-partner, Margarida (Magui) Corceiro. At the time, Porro was playing football for Sporting Lisbon, where actress Corceiro and then-Atletico Madrid star Felix were from.

‌



The stunning model, who would later go on to start a relationship with future F1 world champion Lando Norris in 2023, fuelled speculation that she had been unfaithful to Felix with Porro after allegedly being spotted kissing the full-back in the VIP section of a Lisbon nightclub — while still in a three-year relationship with the Portugal striker.

The previous day, Porro had already set tongues wagging by ignoring several young Sporting supporters at the end of the final fixture of the season to hand his match-worn shirt directly to Corceiro, before pulling her in for a hug.

7 View 7 Images Magui Corceiro was in a relationship with Joao Felix (Image: AFP via Getty Images) 7 View 7 Images Corceiro is a fan of Sporting Lisbon in Portugal (Image: magui_corceiro / Instagram)

‌



Porro, who was single at the time, shot down claims that Sporting fan Corceiro had been unfaithful, yet oddly admitted that he shared a "special relationship" with the stunning blonde. He said: "The situation that is happening yesterday and today is very uncomfortable... I have a special relationship with her, no one is being unfaithful to anyone.

"My image is not going to be stained by anything and less by things like these. I can do whatever I want. Stop staining the image of the three of us because it is not like that."

Corceiro herself insisted the two were nothing more than close friends, having first crossed paths several months earlier at a group dinner. She was adamant that, had she wished to be unfaithful, she would not have done so in full view of an entire nightclub.

‌



"If I wanted to be kissing someone, in an intimate moment, it would not be in Lust In Rio, much less in the VIP area with that little balcony and in view of the entire nightclub," she said when asked about the allegations. "I also don't understand why those gentlemen who took the initiative to record that video and report it in such a nice way didn't remember to record me talking and hugging the other people who were there, the other guys, the players.

7 View 7 Images Margarida is an actress and model (Image: magui_corceiro/Instagram) 7 View 7 Images Corceiro denied the rumours (Image: magui_corceiro/Instagram)

‌



"Because if we want to talk about Magui Corceiro always with the players, and that this is a scene, there was a lot of material." Corceiro then followed up on her furious response with a very blunt and categorical statement of: "There were no kisses, there was nothing."

She continued: "I have just begun to understand the proportions that this is taking. It's getting out of control, and it's leaving me in a very boring position, and Joao too. On the one hand, I feel ridiculous for giving justifications to people who don't know me at all, but you guys are not understanding what's going on.

"This is being surreal, the messages that they are sending, they are sending death threats... people are crazy. I met Porro a few months ago unexpectedly at a group dinner and since then we have had a great time, we are very good friends, I love him, he is incredible and the people who know him know him very well."

‌



Felix and Corceiro officially announced their breakup in June 2023, with the forward having moved to Chelsea that January. Following an unsuccessful loan spell at AC Milan, Felix joined Saudi club Al-Nassr in 2025.

Girlfriend's World Cup support

7 View 7 Images Maria Hurtado is the mother of Porro's child (Image: mhurtado5/Instagram) 7 View 7 Images Hurtado has attended all of Porro's matches for Spain at the World Cup (Image: mhurtado5/Instagram)

‌



Porro drew a line under the entire episode after completing his move to Spurs in January 2023. Since late 2023, he has been in a relationship with Maria Hurtado.

In September 2025, the pair welcomed their first child together, a baby boy. Porro reportedly also helps raise Hurtado's daughter from a previous relationship. The brunette beauty lives with the Spurs star in north London, where she regularly shares fashion and lifestyle snaps on Instagram.

She has amassed 22,500 followers on the platform and has shared numerous pictures of herself cheering on Porro at his World Cup games this summer alongside her children. Porro appeared to dedicate his goal against France to her with a love heart-shaped hand gesture.

Article continues below

Hurtado shared a photo of the celebration, together with pictures of the couple sharing a kiss after the final whistle, with the caption: "We are so proud of you. One more step and no matter what, you've already made history," along with a love heart.

Sports.title: Argentina players refuse to give Falklands banner back after England World Cup controversy
Sports.content:
Argentina players refuse to give Falklands banner back after England World Cup controversy

Argentina players have refused to return the controversial Falkland Islands banner to the fan who smuggled it into the World Cup semi-final against England

View 2 Images Argentina players celebrated with the banner following the win over England. (Image: MB Media, Getty Images)

The Argentine fan who created the controversial Falkland Islands banner is reported to have had a request denied to have it returned to him. England lost 2-1 to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final in Atlanta on Wednesday night, missing out on the opportunity to face Spain in Sunday’s final at MetLife Stadium.

‌



There was controversy after the game in Georgia after some members of the Argentina squad unfurled a banner which read: “Las Malvinas son Argentinas,” which translates to "The Falklands are Argentine" in English.

‌



Argentina refer to the Falklands as Mavinas, and the unfurling of the banner has led to plenty of backlash across the football and political world.

‌



The banner has been deemed to be offensive by many, with 255 British soldiers losing their lives during the Falklands War in 1982. The UK Government released a statement in response to the scenes, declaring: "The World Cup might not be ours, but the Falkland Islands definitely are."

BBC's Joe Hart in bizarre video before World Cup final with pundit DRENCHED in monsoon weather READ MORE :

Spain star calls out Donald Trump and confirms if he'll shake his hand at World Cup final READ MORE :

The banner's creator, identified only as Santiago to protect his identity, has revealed how he managed to deliver the banner to the Argentina players inside the Atlanta stadium.

Santiago claims he created the banner using a hotel bedsheet and paint bought from a nearby shop before stuffing it down his trousers to smuggle it inside the ground.

‌



"When I saw [Gonzalo] Montiel, I threw it to him and he caught it. He passed it to [Giovani] Lo Celso, who was the first to hold it up,” Santiago told Perfil, via the Buenos Aires Times.

He continued: "When I saw Lo Celso open it up and his teammates holding it on the pitch, I felt a joy I can't put into words – how could a piece of bedsheet mean so much to every Argentine.”

"It was crazy. I never imagined that flag would go around the world because of a silly idea we had in a hotel room," Santiago added.

‌



View 2 Images Argentina players unfurled the banner after beating England in the World Cup semi-final (Image: Getty )

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Santiago is said to have subsequently submitted a request to Claudio Tapia, president of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), seeking the return of the banner.

‌



Yet Santiago was reportedly told that "the boys don't want to give it back."

FIFA moved to address the backlash surrounding the banner by announcing an investigation will take place.

"As is standard procedure, FIFA's independent Disciplinary Committee is currently assessing the match reports and considering the relevant circumstances before deciding on potential further steps," FIFA's statement read.

‌



Despite this, the White House has insisted the Argentine players were exercising a First Amendment right to freedom of expression when they made their Falklands protest.

Argentina are set to face Spain in the World Cup final in New Jersey on Sunday evening, with both sides remaining undefeated throughout all seven of their matches in the competition, including the group stages.

Sports.title: Heartbreaking reason Spain star Lamine Yamal's dad won't attend World Cup final
Sports.content:
Heartbreaking reason Spain star Lamine Yamal's dad won't attend World Cup final

Lamine Yamal is looking to outgun Lionel Messi in the World Cup final as Spain collide with Argentina for the biggest prize in football

View 2 Images Lamine Yamal with his dad Mounir Nasraoui after winning Euro 2024 with Spain

Lamine Yamal's father will not attend the World Cup final in person - as he hasn't been able to end any match all tournament.

‌



Mounir Nasraoui has revealed he did not feel fit to travel this summer due to his health. It means Nasraoui is set to cheer on the 19-year-old Barcelona superstar from home.

‌



He explained: "I'm an epileptic. I have to take a lot of medication every day, and I can have an epilepsy seizure.

‌



"I could be here, right now, under the effects of stress or emotion, and have a seizure without realising it. So you always have to think things through carefully.

"Before traveling, you have to think about me, about him, and about all the people around us, you know? I might end up causing problems. So it's better to stay home and watch all this from here."

Spain and Argentina World Cup final training plans rocked by electrical thunderstorms READ MORE :

Spain star Aymeric Laporte calls out Argentina over England World Cup antics READ MORE :

Around a month after Yamal's last major tournament, Euro 2024 - which he won, dad Mounir was stabbed in a parking lot. The authorities arrested four people in connection with the incident.

‌



He remains very close to his family despite his superstardom. His brother Keyne, who is three years old, has been one of the heroes of this World Cup due to his celebrations in the stands.

"I come from an apartment where the kitchen and the bedroom were the same space," Yamal recently stated, citing his humble beginnings.

"I see my mother happy, I see that my brother can have the childhood I would have liked to have, and that's what makes me happiest."

‌



View 2 Images Mounir Nasraoui, the father of Lamine Yamal, suffers with epilepsy

Fatima, Yamal's paternal grandmother, left Morocco on a bus that she wasn't legally allowed to board. She would work shifts just so her son could join before he ended up having Yamal as a teenager.

Now that 19-year-old is about to walk out on the biggest stage of all. While Yamal's parents split when he was three, his football career took off soon after.

‌



He joined Barcelona's youth ranks at seven, though he was actually scouted at the age of seven and at the age of 15, he made his big breakthrough into the first-team.

In doing so, he became the youngest player to make their debut for the Catalan giants since way back in 1922.

Yamal has scored just one goal at this World Cup but after shaking off a thigh issue, he is expected to start against Argentina as he looks to add a second international trophy to his cabinet.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
