World.title: Influencer Andrew Tate and brother arrested in Miami
World.content:
Washington – Radical social media influencer Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan were on Sunday in custody in the US, officials said, as Britain seeks their extradition to face new charges of rape, sex trafficking and assault.

Karena Thomas, assistant chief constable of the UK’s Bedfordshire Police, said the pair had been detained \”pending ongoing legal proceedings.\”

The US Marshals Service confirmed the arrests.

US news outlet TMZ posted video of law enforcement officers placing the self-professed misogynist and his younger sibling in handcuffs and escorting them into waiting vehicles in Miami on Saturday.

Asked by an onlooker if he had something to say, Tristan Tate did not respond, the footage posted on X showed.

UK prosecutors, who are now due to seek the brothers’ extradition, said the arrests came after they brought forward 38 further charges against the pair.

The Tate brothers now face 59 charges in total — 42 against Andrew and 17 against Tristan, British authorities said on Sunday.

\”We have decided to prosecute Andrew and Tristan Tate for further offences including rape, arranging or facilitating trafficking for sexual exploitation and offences relating to indecent images of a child,\” Malcolm McHaffie, head of the UK’s Crown Prosecution Service’s (CPS) Special Crime Division, said in a statement.

\”The CPS has requested the extradition of the Tates from the US,\” he said, adding that the latest charges stem from receipt of new evidence from Bedfordshire Police that brings the total number of alleged victims in the Tates case to seven.

Earlier this year, police in Hertfordshire, north of London, said they were reopening a probe into rape and sexual assault allegations made by women against Andrew Tate between 2014 and 2015.

They also face separate rape and human trafficking allegations brought by different women and investigated by Bedfordshire Police, which covers their hometown of Luton, also north of London.

\”There is no place for male violence against women and girls, and we will continue to work tirelessly to support victims and investigate all reports made to us,\” Bedfordshire Police’s Thomas added.

– ‘Face justice’ –

The Tate brothers are also accused of tax evasion and money laundering in the UK.

Their attorney, Joseph McBride, said in a press release that the brothers \”are innocent.\”

\”We are confident that once a competent judge sees the facts, and once the Department of Justice confronts this egregious abuse of its own authority, Andrew and Tristan Tate will walk free,\” McBride said.

The Tates are dual British-US citizens who have been avid supporters of US President Donald Trump.

Lawyer Matt Jury, of McCue Jury & Partners who represent four alleged British victims of Andrew Tate, said Tate was \”now facing the real prospect of extradition to the UK after years of public campaigning by the four British women I represent.

\”They have spent years fighting for action to be taken, and I now urge the authorities to ensure this case proceeds as quickly as possible.

\”Andrew and Tristan Tate are accused of some of the most serious offences, including multiple counts of rape and human trafficking. It is time they face justice,\” he was quoted by the PA news agency as saying.

In March 2025, the US state of Florida launched a criminal investigation against them. The status of that investigation is unclear.

Andrew Tate is one of the most prominent proponents of the so-called \”manosphere\” network of communities, many of them online, that focus on traditional masculinity, anti-feminism, and self-improvement.

He promotes his divisive views, often incorporating alpha-male and aggressively misogynistic themes, to millions on social media including 10.8 million followers on X.

In Romania, where they have been based in recent years, the Tates face allegations of trafficking minors, sexual intercourse with a minor and money laundering.

World.title: Iraqi dinar declines against US dollar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar declined on Sunday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly declined in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,520 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,526 Iraqi dinars on Sunday’s morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,525 Iraqi dinars and 1,515 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate dropped, fluctuating between 1,523 and 1,522.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Calm Antonelli takes sixth win of the season with victory at Belgian GP
World.content:
Spa-Francorchamps – Italian teenager Kimi Antonelli ended a three-race winless streak on Sunday to extend his lead in the Formula One drivers’ championship with a solid fighting victory for Mercedes in the Belgian Grand Prix.

The 19-year-old Mercedes driver came home 1.9 seconds ahead of Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc with four-time champion Max Verstappen finishing third for Red Bull.

Antonelli’s teammate George Russell, who began the race in second place in the championship, just 25 points behind the Italian, crashed out of the race on the opening lap after tangling with Hamilton.

Hamilton was fourth for Ferrari after an incident-filled race in which he almost hit a mechanic during a pit-stop. The incident was referred to the stewards leaving the seven-time world champion with the possibility of a further penalty.

Isack Hadjar, who began at the back of the grid, did superbly to work his Red Bull up to sixth, just holding off reigning world champion Lando Norris, who started 13th, in the second McLaren.

Gabriel Bortoleto (Audi), Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls) and Franco Colapinto (Alpine) rounded out the top 10.

It was Antonelli’s sixth win of the season and came from his sixth pole of the year, the first driver to win from pole in Belgium since 2021.

It lifts him to 204 points in the championship, 45 clear of Hamilton with Russell third on 154.

\”It feels very nice to be back on the top step,\” said Antonelli.

\”We just have to keep performing, keep bringing the results and then we will see what will happen at the end of the year.\”

The race started in cool conditions under a grey sky with rain in the air as Antonelli made a good start to lead up to La Source, but he had no answer when Verstappen deployed his power pack to pass him through Eau Rouge.

The Dutchman was then immediately vulnerable to a counter-attack and both the Italian and Leclerc drafted past him into Les Combes where behind them Hamilton clashed with Russell.

– ‘Racing incident’ –

The four-time champion continued in fifth, but Russell bounced off into retirement as a Safety Car (SC) was deployed.

Hamilton reported that he “had no front end” control as a result of a car ahead moving across him and the incident was investigated by the stewards who gave Hamilton a five-second penalty.

A downcast Russell, whose title bid had taken a heavy blow, said: “It was a racing incident, but it shouldn’t have happened if I’d had the speed down the straight.”

Racing resumed on lap five with Piastri fighting and resisting Hamilton before Verstappen swept past Leclerc for second. Piastri then chased Leclerc and they touched at Les Combes, where the Monegasque defended and the Australian lost a piece of front wing end plate.

The stewards investigated again, but took ‘no further action’ while Hamilton advanced and passed Piastri for fourth on lap nine as the race settled after a frantic start with Antonelli two seconds clear of Verstappen at the front ahead of both Ferraris.

Further Virtual Safety Cars (VSC) intervened and on lap 20, Ferrari went for a ‘double-stack’. Leclerc went through cleanly but Hamilton, who had to serve his five-second penalty, made a messy exit touching a mechanic on exit.

The mechanic was reported to be fine but the stewards decided to investigate again for an unsafe release.

That left Norris, who had started 13th with a 10-place grid penalty, for taking a new battery, leading ahead of Leclerc, Antonelli and Verstappen until the Ferrari cruised by to take command on lap 23.

Antonelli swept past Norris three laps later and surged after Leclerc while Hamilton, who had requested a wing adjustment in vain during his pit-stop, fell back to sixth.

Norris finally pitted to swap his old hards for mediums on lap 31, rejoining eighth after a slow stop due to a sticky left rear, Hadjar rising to sixth behind Hamilton.

Leclerc led until lap 34 when, as he feared, Antonelli’s superior power carried him through at Les Combes.

But he hung on tight, within a second of the silver arrow, while Hamilton passed Piastri for fourth with five laps to go

World.title: Iraq proposes Energy City project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi announced the Energy City project on Thursday as part of a government plan to enhance energy infrastructure and strengthen partnerships with major international firms.

Al-Zaidi announced the Energy City initiative during an official visit to the United States, which included discussions with US officials and executives from American energy businesses.

This visit is part of Baghdad’s efforts to attract new investments that support plans to increase oil production, develop the gas sector, and enhance electricity generation capacity.

The Iraqi government is depending on the new project to turn the al-Faw Peninsula into an integrated center for the oil, gas, and electricity industries, taking advantage of its strategic location on the Arabian Gulf and proximity to oil export routes and the Development Road project.

The development takes place as Iraq continues to implement plans to eliminate gas flaring, expand domestic gas output, and reduce dependency on imported fuel for power plants, all while increasing refining capacity.

Al-Zaidi’s announcement took place during his participation in the Iraqi-American Chamber of Commerce’s Joint Economic Dialogue Forum in Houston, Texas, to finalize over $60 billion in deals with US energy companies.

The prime minister explained that the project includes integrated complexes for crude oil refining, gas production, processing units, and power plants, as well as connections to strategic oil pipelines and the Development Road, strengthening Iraq’s position as a regional energy and logistics hub.

Al-Zaidi highlighted that Iraq is seeking strategic partners, rather than just contractors, who can assist with technology transfer and contribute to the creation of new job opportunities.

Chairman of the Bilateral Chamber of Commerce David Phillips confirmed the Texas business community’s and large American firms’ willingness to invest in Iraq, notably in oil, gas, and energy projects.

World.title: US-Iran strikes: latest developments
World.content:
Dubai – US and Iranian strikes extended into Sunday, with Washington saying it was punishing Tehran for the deaths of two US servicemen in Jordan and Gulf states announcing responses to Iranian attacks.

Here are the latest developments:

Missile reported intercepted

Israeli and Jordanian forces intercepted an Iranian missile aimed at the Jordanian city of Aqaba on Sunday, the Israeli military told AFP.

When asked by AFP about reports of explosions near the Israeli city of Eilat, a military spokeswoman said both Israeli and Jordanian forces had intercepted a projectile.

The Jordanian military said it had downed \”three Iranian missiles that targeted the kingdom’s territory\”, without specifying where.

Sirens sounded in the Jordanian capital Amman on Sunday, an AFP correspondent said,

Kuwait, Bahrain attacked

Kuwait said Iran hit a power and water plant on Sunday causing a fire, while Bahrain also accused Tehran of targeting civilian infrastructure.

It was the third attack in as many days on a power and water facility in Kuwait, according to authorities, who als said an oil facility had been hit on Saturday.

Earlier on Sunday, Iran’s army said it had targeted two US bases in Kuwait with drones in response to American attacks on Iranian territory.

Iranian nuclear plant attacked

Iran’s Atomic Energy Organisation said the United States attacked an under-construction nuclear power plant in Darkhovin, in the country’s southwest.

Iran says ships ‘stopped’

Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said four ships attempted to transit the Strait of Hormuz without their permission and two \”had an accident and were stopped in place\”.

The other two abandoned their journey, they said.

US strikes on Iran

The United States conducted its eighth consecutive night of strikes on Iran.

Its CENTCOM military command said they were partly to \”punish\” Iran for an attack on Friday on a base in Jordan which killed two US soldiers and left another missing in action.

The strikes were also to \”degrade Iran’s ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz\”, CENTCOM said.

Iranian news agencies Fars and Tasnim reported US attacks on Sirik, a port located on the Strait of Hormuz in southern Iran.

World.title: Russia pounds Kyiv with ballistic missiles in escalating air war
World.content:
Kyiv – Russia fired two dozen ballistic missiles at Kyiv overnight on Sunday, killing one person and wounding 16, in an ever-escalating air war that is taking an increasing civilian toll on both sides.

The latest bombardment highlights a dual challenge for Ukraine in its fifth year of war. It is facing intensifying Russian missile attacks alongside rare domestic political instability triggered by a sudden wartime shakeup of its defence leadership.

In the morning, AFP journalists in Kyiv saw charred apartment blocks with windows blown out and mangled, overturned cars.

\”The missiles just kept coming one after another, the explosions were powerful, it was horrible,\” 47-year-old Kyiv resident Ganna Zagorodnia told AFP.

\”I thought that life was just about to end.\”

In a statement on social media, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky said that \”overnight, Russia carried out one of its largest ballistic missile attacks on Kyiv,\” launching more than 40 missiles, 25 of them ballistic.

Zelensky added that one person was killed and 16 others wounded in the attack, which police said targeted six districts.

Elsewhere in Ukraine, afternoon Russian strikes killed four and wounded 20 at a post warehouse in Kharkiv, the country’s eastern second-biggest city, said local military governor Oleg Syniegubov.

In the Black Sea city of Odesa, a teenager was killed and 12 were wounded, including a two-year-old child, after a Russian attack on an amusement park, said governor Oleg Kiper.

Russia, which denies targeting civilians, said it struck military facilities and logistics hubs in Kyiv and port infrastructure used by the Ukrainian army in Odesa.

– Generals back commander –

Even as the war raged, thousands have been gathering in big cities across Ukraine for three consecutive days to protest at the removal of popular defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov.

Demonstrators also called for the resignation of Ukraine’s chief commander Oleksandr Syrsky, who reportedly had demanded Fedorov’s dismissal after the two clashed over how to counter the Russian invasion.

Following the protests, two experienced top Ukrainian generals — the navy and the air assault force chiefs — backed Syrsky in rare political statements, calling for unity and saying divisions are playing into the enemy’s hands.

\”It is particularly painful to hear peremptory judgments from people who have never issued combat orders, never taken responsibility for the lives and health of the personnel,\” said air assault force commander Oleg Apostol, referring to Fedorov’s critisism of Syrsky.

Echoing that, navy commander Oleksiy Neizhpapa said: \”doubts about the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) during wartime are unacceptable. The AFU is perhaps the only institution that stands firmly on its feet, no matter what.\”

Fedorov, 35, who never served in the army, accused the 60-year-old, Russian-born general Syrsky of dividing the country.

He criticised slow bureaucracy and a lack of flexibility, questioning whether Ukraine could defeat Russia with Syrsky in charge of the army.

– Air defence hunger –

Since the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran, Ukraine has suffered from a shortage of air defence projectiles for its US-designed Patriot systems, which are essential for fending off ballistic rounds.

Exploiting the shortage, Russia has intensified its air raids on Kyiv in recent weeks, launching barrages of balistic missiles — fast, hard to intercept weapons — roughly once a week.

\”Protection against ballistic missiles is our constant and top priority right now. Interceptors are needed every day,\” Zelensky said.

Overnight on Sunday, out of 25 Russian ballistic missiles, 17 were intercepted, the air force said — a rate suggesting Ukraine’s air defence situation might be improving.

On the Russian side, a Ukrainian strike killed one person in the Kursk region, near the Ukrainian border, regional governor Alexander Khinshtein said on Telegram.

Another drone salvo hit the Caspian Pipeline Consortium’s terminal near the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiysk — a key export route for Kazakh oil, partly owned by Chevron and Shell.

Kyiv has in recent months intensified its strikes on Russian territory, disrupting the lives of ordinary Russians — strikes it calls retribution for more than four years of bombardments against its territory.

World.title: Iraq gives priority to electricity interconnection with Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Electricity Minister Ali Saadi Wahib stated that the government prioritizes the electricity interconnection project with Saudi Arabia as part of its efforts to diversify energy sources.

In an interview with Asharq News in Washington, Wahib stated that Iraq’s electricity grid now has a shortage ranging between 35,000 and 40,000 megawatts.

Baghdad is working to diversify its electricity sources through regional interconnection projects. Wahib said that Iraq has a 600-megawatt interconnection project with Turkey and approximately 500 megawatts with Jordan, in addition to a 600-megawatt interconnection project with the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) grid, which is still underway.

The electrical interconnection project with Saudi Arabia, projected to have a capacity of 1,000 to 2,000 megawatts, has not yet entered the execution phase. However, it has become a priority for the Iraqi government, according to Wahib.

The project includes the construction of transmission lines and power stations to import electricity from Saudi Arabia. The minister stated that the government is serious about enhancing interconnection capabilities and diversifying energy sources with neighboring countries.

Wahib noted that the project is expected to be included in the 2027 budget.

World.title: Starlink assigns IP addresses to users in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Starlink has officially changed its network routing to issue local Iraqi IP addresses to customers that connect from within Iraq.

This technological shift took place after SpaceX signed a licensing deal with Iraq’s Communications and Media Commission (CMC), the country’s regulatory agency that oversees and develops media, broadcasting, and telecommunications sectors.

The regulatory structure allows Starlink to operate legally throughout the country.

Earlier, users in the region connected to the satellite network via European networks and were issued Bulgarian IP addresses.

Starlink data from Iraq is now routed through particular connections, reducing the need for remote international points of entry.

By avoiding the traditional European routing pathways, local customers should see much lower latency and faster overall connection rates.

The Iraqi government approved earlier Starlink’s operating license, allowing it to deliver world-leading internet services to Iraqi citizens.

As the decision paves the way for Elon Musk’s satellite network to enter the Iraqi market, it also supports the country’s digital transformation.

Starlink is a satellite internet group managed by Starlink Services, LLC, an international telecommunications service and fully owned subsidiary of the US aerospace corporation SpaceX.

As part of the Iraqi government’s digital transformation, the Iraqi government is pushing major technology companies, notably those located in the United States, to operate in Iraq and collaborate with the Iraqi private sector.

World.title: 'Rise in instability in Iran': Indian embassy sounds alarm; urges people to leave, postpone travel
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Indian Embassy in Iran on Sunday issued a revised travel advisory, urging Indian nationals to postpone all travel to the country.

It also advised Indians already in Tehran to consider temporarily leaving the country using available commercial flights, as the security situation continues to deteriorate amid the escalating conflict in the Middle East.

The advisory comes as military hostilities between the United States and Iran have intensified, with fresh strikes, retaliatory attacks and growing concerns over the security situation across the region.

In its advisory, the embassy said, "The recent days have seen an increase in levels of instability and conflict in Iran."

It advised Indian nationals planning to visit Iran 'for any purpose' to postpone their travel until the security environment improves.

The embassy also urged Indians already in Iran to 'consider temporarily exiting Iran, using available flight options.'

For those choosing to remain in the country, the mission advised exercising the highest level of caution, closely monitoring local developments and avoiding areas witnessing increased military activity, particularly along Iran's southern coast.

"Indian nationals who choose to remain in Iran should exercise the highest possible level of caution.





They should carefully monitor the news to maintain full situational awareness, and should avoid locations seeing higher levels of military activity such as those along the southern coast of the country. Instructions issued by local authorities should be complied with carefully," the advisory read.

The embassy also asked all Indian nationals in Iran who have not yet registered with the mission to do so immediately and regularly follow its official website and social media channels for further updates.

The advisory was issued as the conflict between the United States and Iran escalated further on Sunday.

According to Iranian authorities, the United States carried out fresh strikes on the under-construction Darkhovin nuclear power plant and other military targets, while the US Central Command (CENTCOM) said it targeted Iranian coastal surveillance systems, air defence networks, maritime assets and missile and drone facilities.

Iran, meanwhile, announced retaliatory drone attacks against two US military installations in Kuwait and claimed to have intercepted a US MQ-9 drone over Ahvaz. It also warned that the Strait of Hormuz remained under the control of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), amid heightened tensions over maritime security.

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said it was investigating reports of the attack on the Darkhovin nuclear facility and added that the site contained no nuclear material during its last inspection. The UN nuclear watchdog said the reported strike was not believed to pose any radiological risk but reiterated its call for military restraint around nuclear-related sites.

The latest escalation has raised fresh international concern over the widening conflict in the Middle East as the war completes nearly five months.

World.title: 'We intend to work with PM Modi': Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar announces entry into NDA with 20 Mamata rebels
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Once a Mamata loyalist and now an NCPI leader after rebelling against the Mamata Banerjee-led

, Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar on Su

y announced that she would join the ruling NDA in the Lok Sabha ahead of Monsoon Session.

She said 20 former TMC MPs, who have formed a separate parliamentary group under the NCPI, would also join the PM Modi-led alliance in the Lower House.

She said the group intends to work with the NDA under the leadership of Prime Minister

and Union home minister Amit Shah.

The announcement marks a significant step in the Mamata rebels' realignment amid the continuing exodus from the TMC following its crushing defeat to the

BJP

in the West Bengal assembly elections in May.

Addressing the media, Kakoli said the group had decided to back the NDA and work under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah.

"We, 20 AITC MPs, are joining the NDA alliance. Leaving AITC, we align ourselves with NCPI... we intend to work with the NDA, supporting the initiatives of PM Modi and our Home Minister Amit Shah and be involved in their work of nation-building. We stated in the all-party meeting that we would work together.





There are 8 women among our group of 20, and we will stand by the government on whatever issues they take up," she said.

Speaking about the NCPI parliamentary party meeting, Kakoli said the group's focus would be on constructive participation during the Monsoon Session.

"There will be discussions and debates on 5-6 bills... Everyone should debate, but we shouldn't waste the House's time, as that causes significant loss to the country and the public.

In the interest of the nation and for the progress of the people, we will debate the upcoming issues, whether they concern taxes or the registration of births and deaths, but we will ensure the House functions smoothly. That is what we discussed," she added.

The development comes amid an unprecedented rebellion within the Trinamool Congress after the party, led by

Mamata Banerjee

, suffered a stinging defeat to the BJP in the West Bengal assembly polls after 15 years in power.

While Ritabrata Banerjee has emerged as the face of the rebellion within the party organisation by staking claim to the leader of the opposition post in the assembly against the wishes of the party leadership. Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar also has led a large section of TMC MPs in the Lok Sabha away from the Mamata Banerjee-led camp. The rebel faction has since aligned itself with the NCPI and is now extending support to the BJP-led NDA in Parliament.

World.title: ‘No state has witnessed such a political change since Independence’: Amit Shah on Bengal
World.content:
Union home minister Amit Shah in Kolkata

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday described the change of guard in West Bengal as "unlike any political change since 1947", months after his Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) ended the Trinamool Congress' (TMC) 15-year rule in the state."The change in Bengal is unlike any political change witnessed in any state across the country since Independence," Shah said in Kolkata while virtually laying the foundation stone for a curd production plant under the Amul Bengal Dairy Project."West Bengal was once a beacon for the entire country in every field. In education, West Bengal remained decades ahead of the rest of the nation. Whether it was the freedom struggle or the country's cultural and spiritual renaissance, Bengal gave India some of its greatest leaders and freedom fighters," he added.Shah described the Left Front, which ruled West Bengal for over 30 years (1977-2011), as a "foreign ideology" and the TMC, which was in power from 2011 until it was voted out in April this year, as "corrupt and ideologically bankrupt.""First Bengal was ruled by the foreign ideology of the Left for three decades, then by the corrupt and ideologically bankrupt TMC for 15 years," the minister added in a sharp attack on the previous governments in the state.The Amul Bengal Dairy Project, he noted, would mark a milestone for the state's dairy sector and boost the income of milk producers.The Rs 700 crore project will process 30 lakh litres of milk daily and produce 10 lakh kg of curd and other cultured dairy products every day. It is expected to benefit more than 1.25 lakh dairy farmers in West Bengal, including over 30,000 women, while strengthening the cooperative dairy network in eastern India.During his three-day visit to West Bengal, Shah held discussions with the Centre and the state government officials on governance issues, including measures to curb infiltration, strengthen law and order and improve women's safety.The event marked the conclusion of Shah's three-day visit to West Bengal, during which he attended official programmes and held meetings on key issues.

World.title: 'NCPI recognised by EC': Sudip Bandyopadhyay hits back after opposition's walkout over TMC rebels' presence
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) leader

on Sunday defended his party's participation in the all-party meeting ahead of the Monsoon Session, saying the NCPI is recognised by the Election Commission and dismissing the oppposition's protest over the presence of rebel

(TMC) MPs.

His remarks came after several opposition parties staged a symbolic walkout from the all-party meeting to protest the invitation extended to Bandyopadhyay and fellow NCPI leader Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar. The opposition later rejoined the meeting, saying the walkout was meant to register its protest.

Speaking to reporters, Bandyopadhyay criticised the opposition's decision to walk out.

"I have never seen a walkout taking place during an all-party leaders' meeting.

The NCPI is recognised by the Election Commission. Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar is going to submit all documents to the Lok Sabha Speaker," he said.

The former TMC leader also claimed that his erstwhile party had been reduced in strength after 20 of its Lok Sabha members joined the NCPI.

"I also demanded (at the all-party meeting) that a small party should not be given seats in the first row. Just eight (MPs) are left in the party (TMC) after its 20 out of 28 moved out," Bandyopadhyay told reporters.





Responding to the opposition's objections over the NCPI's participation in the meeting, he said the matter would become clear once Parliament convenes.

"Whatever they are telling, let them say. Whatever the Lok Sabha Speaker has to say, only tomorrow the Parliament will open and you will find whose seat is where," he said.

On the TMC's demand seeking the disqualification of the 20 rebel MPs, Bandyopadhyay said the decision rests entirely with Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla.

"If the Speaker thinks that it is fit for disqualification, he will disqualify. And if he thinks that from tomorrow we should sit as a separate bloc in the first row, we'll find tomorrow. Wait for 24 hours," he said.

He added that Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar would submit all the required documents to the Lok Sabha Speaker on Sunday.

Dastidar welcomed the government's decision to invite the NCPI to the all-party meeting.

"We express our gratitude for being invited to the all-party meeting.

It is a sign of respect toward our newly formed coalition of 20 MPs," she said.

The all-party meeting convened by the government ahead of the Monsoon Session witnessed a symbolic walkout by opposition parties after Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla approved separate seating for the 20 rebel TMC MPs who have formed the NCPI.

TMC MP Mahua Moitra questioned the government's decision to invite the rebel MPs, arguing that the Lok Sabha Speaker had not yet approved their merger and that disqualification petitions against them were still pending.

Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju defended the invitation, saying, "The NCPI requested recognition from the Lok Sabha Speaker; how can you ignore them? It is the government's duty to invite everyone."

The NCPI held its parliamentary party meeting at Samvidhan Sadan on Sunday ahead of the Monsoon Session, which begins on Monday. While Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has approved separate seating for the 20 rebel TMC MPs.

World.title: Flash floods rip through Jammu and Kashmir as rain fury leaves trail of destruction - watch
World.content:
Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe the government is doing enough to assist flood-affected residents? Yes, significantly No, not enough 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Flash floods and landslides triggered by torrential rain caused widespread devastation across Jammu and Kashmir's border districts of Poonch and Rajouri on Sunday, with rescue teams racing to reach stranded residents as the weather emergency deepened. Officials said the death toll from the rain-related disasters has risen to 11, while several people remain missing.The worst damage was reported from Surankote tehsil in Poonch district, where multiple cloudbursts, landslides and flash floods swept through villages, damaging homes and cutting off roads.Dramatic visuals from the affected areas showed vehicles being swept away by raging floodwaters, piles of mangled cars, homes collapsing under the force of the floods, and residents stranded as overflowing rivers inundated entire neighbourhoods.Multi-agency rescue teams, including the army, police, national disaster response force and state disaster response force, have been deployed to trace the missing and evacuate affected families.Union home minister Amit Shah reviewed the situation with Lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha and chief minister Omar Abdullah, assuring all possible assistance from the Centre."Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah spoke with the Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir, Shri Manoj Sinha, and Chief Minister Shri Omar Abdullah regarding the situation caused by heavy rainfall and assured them of all possible assistance from the Central Government," Shah's office said in a post on X.Chief Minister Omar Abdullah said the administration's immediate priority was to save lives."Since first light this morning, I've been closely monitoring the situation arising from the extremely heavy rain... the first priority of the administration is to safeguard precious lives," Abdullah said on X."The government will do everything possible to aid & assist affected people who have suffered property loss/damage due to the rains & flash floods," he added.In Rajouri, rescue teams pulled two stranded people to safety from the Muradpur area after flash floods caused water levels to rise rapidly.Deputy commissioner Abhishek Sharma told news agency PTI, "Two persons were safely rescued from the river at Muradpur, Rajouri, after they became stranded due to the flash floods triggered by heavy rainfall."Authorities have urged residents to stay away from rivers and other flood-prone areas as water levels remain dangerously high.Continuous rain since Saturday has triggered multiple cloudbursts and flash floods, washing away several structures along the Poonch River and damaging key infrastructure, with rescue and relief operations continuing across the worst-hit districts.

World.title: Calcutta HC halts demolition of Abhishek Banerjee's Amtala office
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Calcutta high court on Sunday directed authorities to halt all demolition work at

(TMC) MP

's office in South 24 Parganas' Amtala, until further orders.

The direction came hours after an anti-encroachment drive was launched at the closed office premises amid heavy security arrangements.

Officials had begun the demolition exercise as part of the anti-encroachment operation in the area.

Following the high court's intervention, the demolition work has been stopped, and no further action will be taken at the site until the court issues fresh directions.

A day earlier, senior Trinamool Congress leader Abhishek Banerjee had alleged that the demolition of the party's Amtala office was politically motivated, asserting that the building was constructed legally on land purchased by the party after obtaining all necessary permissions.

Accusing the local administration of acting in collusion with the BJP-led government, Abhishek had announced that the TMC would challenge the demolition before the Calcutta high court.

The South 24 Parganas district administration had demolished the TMC MP's party office in Amtala on Saturday, claiming that the structure had been built without an approved building plan and in violation of applicable rules, according to a senior official.

World.title: Rajya Sabha MPs' salaries, perks cost exchequer Rs 262 crore in two years
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Over Rs 262 crore spent on Rajya Sabha MPs' salaries, allowances and other benefits during the last two financial years, with more than Rs 151 crore going towards allowances and travel alone, according to a reply obtained under the Right to Information (RTI) Act.

The RTI response showed that expenditure on sitting Rajya Sabha members rose sharply from more than Rs 98 crore in 2024-25 to over Rs 163 crore in 2025-26, marking an increase of nearly Rs 65 crore in a year.

The expenditure covered salaries, domestic and international travel, office expenses, medical reimbursements and other facilities provided to MPs.

In 2024-25, the government spent over Rs 25.71 crore on salaries, Rs 8.2 crore on medical bills, Rs 24.99 crore on travel expenses and more than Rs 33.33 crore on allowances.

In 2025-26, salaries increased to over Rs 44.6 crore, while medical bills stood at Rs 9.6 crore. Travel expenses rose to Rs 36 crore, and allowances exceeded Rs 58.78 crore, according to the reply provided by the Rajya Sabha Secretariat in response to an RTI application filed by Chander Shekhar Gaur.

Rajya Sabha members are entitled to benefits under 21 different expenditure heads, including salaries, allowances, domestic and foreign travel, office expenses and medical reimbursements.

Other expenditure heads include printing and publication, digital equipment, fuel and lubricants, professional services, repair and maintenance, subsidies and other revenue-related expenses.

World.title: Fishers seeks withdrawal of nod for large fishing vessels off Kerala coast
World.content:
The State camp of the All India Fishermen’s Federation (AITUC) has demanded that the Union government withdraw its decision to permit large fishing vessels to operate off the Kerala coast. They warned that the move would threaten marine resources and jeopardise the livelihoods of traditional fishermen.

In a resolution, the federation said India requires only about one lakh fishing vessels in its regulated fishing zone, but more than three lakh vessels are already operating. They added that allowing large fishing vessels with substantial government subsidies would accelerate the depletion of fish stocks and push Kerala’s fishing fleet into crisis.

The federation also demanded the constitution of the Vembanad Lake Protection Authority, the withdrawal of the proposed Port City Project, and the abandonment of the proposed seaplane project in fishing zones. They alleged that the Port City Project aims at coastal mining and displacement and called for measures to prevent recurring fishing accidents and deaths at Muthalapozhi and ensure the safety of fishermen.

Inaugurating the valedictory session, AITUC State general secretary K.P. Rajendran criticised the State government for assigning English titles to coastal development schemes in the State Budget, despite the Budget being presented in Malayalam.

AITUC national general secretary R. Prasad led the study session. State president T.J. Angelos presided. CPI(M) State executive member C.N. Chandran, federation general secretary T. Raghuvaran, CPI district executive member P. Ajayakumar, and others addressed the gathering. Senior leaders of AITUC, the CPI, the Kerala Pravasi Sangham, the Kerala Mahila Sangham, and affiliated organisations also attended.

World.title: West Bengal BJP government is implementing the promise of ‘Sonar Bangla’, says Amit Shah
World.content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in West Bengal is implementing the promise of ‘Sonar Bangla’ (golden Bengal) on the ground, Union Home Minister Amit Shah said on Sunday (July 19, 2026). The Minister was virtually laying the foundation stone of a ₹700-crore Amul dairy project at Sankrail in Howrah.

“I have come to tell the people of West Bengal that whatever we had promised during the elections, the government is implementing the promise of ‘Sonar Bangla’ on the ground,” the Minister said.

During the campaign for the 2026 Assembly election, the BJP leadership, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Mr. Shah, had spoken about returning West Bengal to its golden age.

Tracing the political history of West Bengal, Mr. Shah said that that the idea of ‘Sonar Bangla’ envisioned by Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore had been destroyed by the previous Communist and the Trinamool Congress (TMC) regimes.

The change that the people of West Bengal had brought about was unlike any political change witnessed in any State of the country since Independence, the Home Minister said.

​Take east: On the BJP government in West Bengal

Mr. Shah, who was on a three-day visit to the State, said the Central and the State government had held detailed discussions on governance and security. “We have discussed and taken several steps to stop infiltration, strengthen law and order, and improve women’s safety,” he said.

Amul had laid the foundation stone of the country’s largest yogurt production project, and yogurt will be produced by processing 10 lakh litres of milk, Mr. Shah said.

“Small dairy farmers will benefit. I told the Chief Minister (Suvendu Adhikari) to give two 15-acre plots [to Amul]. Then the entire east India milk production system will be from here,” he said.

Mr. Adhikari took a swipe at former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, who has said she would not let West Bengal turn into Gujarat.

“Those who used to say that they will not let Bengal become Gujarat, they are watching on TV from home today. Amul is investing ₹700 crore today for the development of West Bengal,” Mr. Adhikari said.

The Chief Minister urged the Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation Limited to set up two ice-cream plants, one in south Bengal and another in north Bengal, and said that his government would provide 15 acres of land for setting up the plants.

State Industries Minister Tapas Roy, Finance Minister Swapan Dasgupta, Cooperative Minister Ashok Kirtania, Health Minister Sharadwat Mukherjee, and BJP State president and Rajya Sabha MP Samik Bhattacharya were present on the occasion of virtually laying the foundation stone of the Amul project.

This is the third major investment announced after the BJP government came to power in West Bengal. Lux Cozi recently laid the foundation stone for a mega manufacturing hub in Dankuni, with a planned investment of ₹600 crore. The Shyam Steel Group has also announced a project at its Mejia plant in Bankura district, with a total investment of ₹15,000 crore.

World.title: Special registration drive for migrant workers at fishing harbours in Kannur
World.content:
The district administration has decided to launch a special registration drive for migrant workers at fishing harbours as the first phase of an intensified campaign to bring all the workers under the State’s unified registration system.

The decision was taken at a recent review meeting on migrant worker registration chaired by Additional District Magistrate P.N. Purushothaman at the Collectorate.

Officials said around 10,000 migrant workers are employed across the district’s eight fishing harbours. The Fisheries and Labour departments will jointly conduct a special registration camp to collect the workers’ details and issue Aadhaar-based identity cards.

The meeting also reviewed the progress of registration in other sectors. A second phase of mass registration drives will cover industrial units, construction sites, commercial establishments, and other workplaces with the cooperation of various government departments.

The meeting also decided to integrate data collected by different departments to avoid duplication. Employers and those providing accommodation to migrant workers have been instructed to ensure that all workers are registered on the portal. Awareness campaigns in the workers’ native languages will also be organised, while inspections will be conducted at labour camps to ensure hygiene and sanitation standards.

So far, 33,601 migrant workers have been registered in Kannur district through special camps and direct data collection by the Labour department. At fishing harbours, including Ayyikkara, Azhikkal, Puthiyangadi, Thalai, Gopalpet, and Palakkode, 3,177 workers have been registered through 63 registration camps. Officials said the remaining workers would be covered under the special drive once they return after the end of the trawling ban, as many have temporarily gone back to their native States.

World.title: Neha, a prominent face of the CJP protests, presses on with hunger strike
World.content:
As the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) started its current protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on June 20, at the peak of Delhi’s punishing summer, the focus was mostly on the founder of the party, Abhijeet Dipke, who had by then become an online sensation.

As the sun went down, the Delhi Police started removing people from Jantar Mantar, and the protest was reduced to a small band of people gathered on and around the main stage. But one lesser-known face, standing right next to Mr. Dipke on his left with an “AISA” badge pinned to her kurta, continued chanting slogans louder than most of the others. She was Ms. Neha.

Ms. Neha, who was back then not that familiar, at least to the rest of the nation, has since then become a prominent face of the protest.

As the protest progressed, 29-year-old Ms. Neha, who is the national president of the All India Students’ Association (AISA), the students wing of the CPI(ML) Liberation, began an indefinite hunger strike with five other AISA members on June 28, the same day as activist Sonam Wangchuk.

Over the next three weeks, three of her colleagues gave up the hunger strike due to health issues and Mr. Wangchuk was forcibly removed from the protest site on Saturday (July 18, 2026) morning, leaving Ms. Neha and two of her colleagues continuing the hunger strike for the 22nd day on Sunday (July 19). The three, who now take others’ support to walk, stay in a makeshift tent close to the main stage of the protest.

She is the only woman still continuing the hunger strike on its 22nd day.

Though such a long hunger strike is a first for Ms. Neha, she is not new to protests.

Army man’s daughter

Hailing from Uttarakhand, Ms. Neha did her schooling in different parts of the country as her father was serving in the Army.

Coming from a non-political background, she moved to Delhi to pursue her undergraduate degree from the University of Delhi. It was here that she became politically active through a theatre group. “Good thing about theatre is it tells you about politics in the languages that we speak, the songs that we sing, and our body language, everything,” she said.

Ms. Neha continued to be part of the theatre group ‘Sangwari’, which has a lot of members from AISA, and became active in student politics too. She continued student politics during her Masters’ programme from Dr. B.R. Ambedkar University Delhi (AUD) and now during her PhD at the Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU).

Her colleagues said that she was active in the anti-CAA (Citizenship Amendment Act) protests in Delhi and also the farmers’ protest in 2020-21. Ms. Neha was elected secretary of the Delhi unit of AISA in 2021 and national president of AISA in December 2024.

“What sets her apart from others in the AISA is that she is very charismatic and also connects with people very easily. I’m not saying that others in AISA can’t do it, but someone else may get agitated when they are talking about an issue that is infuriating. But she knows how to present it and how to modulate her tone, when to stress and where to stop. Maybe that comes from theatre, but that helps her to convey the message better,” an AISA activist said.

Incidentally, Ms. Neha and others had protested at the same Jantar Mantar in the summer of 2024 demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over paper leaks and they had even gone on a hunger strike then too.

“But we were detained by police as we were coming out of the Metro Station for a march to Parliament,” an AISA member said.

The fight against ‘politics of hatred’

When asked about AISA’s association with the CJP during the ongoing protest, Ms. Neha told The Hindu that they had been building this movement for a long time. “The student organisations, specifically of the Left, along with AISA, have built this movement from the ground up, bit by bit, through memorandums and protests over the years,” she said.

“So when something like the CJP comes up, it’s great for us. It’s great for the students. It’s great for us as a student organisation that there is such a massive outpouring of support to the CJP, and our involvement with it was an inevitable continuation of our fight for a better education system... Even the founder of the CJP also says ‘we were there at the right place at the right time’,” she said.

Ms. Neha said that all the BJP had done was “politics of hatred”. “And for us, influencing the conscience of the people, people realising that coming together makes everything possible, making people remember that this is our legacy and not the divisive politics that the BJP has taught us and trained us to do. That is important for us. That is the learning we take from here. That is what we will build upon from this moment on. And that is why we fight every fight.”

World.title: 13-year-old found dead in Kasaragod
World.content:
A 13-year-old Class 7 student was found dead at his family’s rented labour quarters near Perla in Kasaragod on Sunday (July 19, 2026). The Badiadka police have registered a case of unnatural death and begun an investigation.

The boy, whose parents worked as rubber tappers, was alone at home after they left to buy ingredients to prepare payasam he had requested earlier in the day. When they returned and received no response, they broke open the locked door and found him. He was rushed to hospital, where doctors declared him dead.

According to relatives, the boy had recently undergone medical tests after developing lumps on his neck and had been distressed after doctors reportedly suspected cancer. The police said all aspects of the incident are under investigation.

Those in distress or having suicidal tendencies could seek help and counselling by calling any of the following numbers: State’s health helpline 104, Maithri - 0484-2540530, Thanal Suicide Prevention Centre - 0495-2760000

World.title: Will end fast if education accountability issue raised in Parliament Monsoon Session: Wife Gitanjali conveys Wangchuk’s message
World.content:
Activist Sonam Wangchuk will call off his indefinite hunger strike if political leaders meet him at the Safdarjung Hospital and assure him that the issue of education accountability will be raised during the Monsoon Session of Parliament beginning Monday (July 20, 2026), his wife Gitanjali Angmo said on Sunday (July 19, 2026).

Jantar Mantar protest LIVE updates - July 19, 2026

Addressing protesters at the Jantar Mantar, where the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has been spearheading a movement against the alleged NEET paper leak, seeking education reforms, Ms. Angmo said Mr. Wangchuk has conveyed that he would end his fast provided there is a commitment from political parties to take up the issue in Parliament.

“If political leaders meet Sonam at the hospital and assure him that they will raise the issue of education accountability during the Monsoon Session, he will end his hunger strike tomorrow,” Ms. Angmo said.

She also conveyed Mr. Wangchuk's appeal to the supporters of the movement ahead of the CJP’s proposed ‘Chalo Sansad’ march on Monday (July 19, 2026), urging them to maintain peace and discipline.

“Sonam has requested all of us to take out tomorrow's march peacefully and ensure that the protest is not misused,” Ms. Angmo said.

On concerns over Mr. Wangchuk's health, she said the activist is stable. “Sonam’s health is perfectly fine. I tried my best in the High Court to have him shifted to a private hospital, but I could not succeed,” she said.

On Saturday (July 18, 2026), Delhi Police forcefully admitted Mr. Wangchuk to the Safdarjung Hospital after three weeks of fasting at the CJP protest site at Jantar Mantar.

Ms. Angmo and the CJP have said that Mr. Wangchuk is continuing his fast at the hospital, refusing to receive any drip.

Wangchuk stable, being given required medical intervention: Safdarjung Hospital

The activist was stable, but needed round-the-clock medical care and close monitoring due to the physiological stress and systemic effects of his prolonged hunger strike, Safdarjung Hospital authorities said.

A health bulletin issued by VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital said Mr. Wangchuk’s vital parameters were stable and his blood parameters had shown marginal improvement. A multidisciplinary team of experts from Safdarjung Hospital and Delhi AIIMS is supervising his treatment, it said.

“Sonam Wangchuk is receiving the required medical care at VMMC and Safdarjung Hospital. His vital parameters are stable. While his blood parameters have shown minor improvement, it requires close monitoring.” “Accordingly, all necessary medical care is being provided, and his clinical condition is being closely monitored,” a health bulletin issued by Safdarjung Hospital at 7 p.m. said.

Despite days of fasting, Mr. Wangchuk remains alert, Charu Bamba, Medical Superintendent, VMMC and Safdarjung Superspeciality Hospital, told reporters in the morning. “As you know, he has been admitted with us since yesterday morning. Like yesterday, he is fully alert, conscious and oriented. His vital parameters, including blood pressure, pulse rate and oxygen saturation, are all normal,” she said.

Ms. Lamba, however, added that some of his blood (laboratory) parameters are slightly abnormal. “They are just below or above the normal range, and we are carrying out further investigations. Our team is providing him with continuous treatment,” she said.

“Since he is weak and is still on a fast, he requires constant monitoring and further evaluation,” she added.

The CJP and Mr. Wangchuk have been demanding accountability over the alleged NEET paper leak, action against those responsible, and broader reforms in the education system.

Monday's proposed march to Parliament coincides with the opening day of the Monsoon Session, which will continue till August 13.

Over the past few weeks, the agitation has received support from several opposition leaders and student organisations, while the Delhi High Court has also been monitoring Wangchuk's medical condition through periodic status reports.

World.title: INL links ‘move’ to reconstitute Waqf Board to Munambam
World.content:
The Indian National League (INL) on Sunday (July 19, 2026) alleged that the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) government was attempting to reconstitute the Kerala State Waqf Board as part of a larger plan linked to the Munambam land dispute.

In a statement, INL State general secretary Kasim Irikkur alleged that Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan, who wanted to hand over the Munambam Waqf land to resort and bar owners, had conspired with Waqf Minister N. Samsudheen and the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) to reconstitute the Waqf Board after realising that the existing board was unwilling to compromise on the Munambam issue.

The INL alleged that a petition filed by BJP leader Shone George in the Kerala High Court had been used as a pretext to facilitate the move. It also claimed that the Additional Solicitor General, appearing for the Union government, and the State’s Advocate General had relied on provisions of the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, legislation that the Congress and the IUML have been opposing, to support arguments against the present board.

The party further alleged that an affidavit was filed before the High Court in the name of Revenue Under Secretary T.P. Pushpavalli, through Government Special Pleader P.M. Saneer, without the knowledge of Revenue Minister A.P. Anil Kumar and at the instance of Mr. Samsudheen . According to the INL, the affidavit indicated that the State Waqf Board would be reconstituted under the provisions of the 2025 Act.

The INL also accused the IUML of taking contradictory positions by contending that the present board was invalid for not including two non-Muslim members while simultaneously challenging the legal provision in the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, mandating such appointments before the Supreme Court.

Alleging that the move was intended to gain control over the Waqf Board and its properties, the INL claimed that it was part of a broader agenda of the BJP-led Union government and RSS to weaken minority rights.

World.title: ‘Right to raise voice peacefully’: Shabana Azmi joins CJP’s Jantar Mantar protest
World.content:
Veteran actor Shabana Azmi on Sunday joined the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) protest at Jantar Mantar, extending support to protesters demanding education reforms and accountability over alleged examination irregularities, a day before the outfit’s planned ‘Chalo Sansad’ march.

Azmi visited the protest site Sunday evening, joining a growing list of public figures expressing solidarity with the agitation. Actor Prakash Raj, Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra, CPI(M) leader Brinda Karat and AAP leader Manish Sisodia also visited Jantar Mantar during the day.

Addressing the gathering, Azmi said she was standing with students because their demands deserved to be heard. “I have come here because I believe the concerns being raised by the students are important. In a democracy, people have the right to raise their voice peacefully,” she said, urging the authorities to engage in dialogue instead of confrontation.

Also Read | Hunger strike Day 21: Police shift Sonam Wangchuk to hospital

Azmi also met the All India Students’ Association – AISA president Neha Bora, who is sitting on an indefinite hunger strike with fellow students Aameen and Manish, on the 22nd day of their voluntary fasting. Visuals from the protest site showed the actor greeting and offering support in a heartfelt gesture to the students.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Neha (@neowsibora)

In a post on X, Neha also thanked Azmi for extending her support and solidarity to the movement.

During his visit, actor Prakash Raj also led protesters in raising the slogan “Aali re aali, aata Pradhan chi baari aali” (loosely translates to: “Now, Pradhan’s time has come”), targeting Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Extending the slogan with a satirical reference to his popular dialogue “Aata majhi satakli!” (Marathi for “Now I’ve had enough” or “I’ve finally snapped”), Raj drew loud cheers from the crowd as protesters echoed the chant in support of the movement.

Aali Re Aali Aata Pradhan Chi Bari Aali Prakash Raj says, “Aata Majhi satakli!” At Jantar Mantar pic.twitter.com/2n5HmPysiA — Cockroach Janta Party (@CJP_for_India) July 19, 2026

The protest site witnessed a surge in attendance on Sunday, with supporters gathering ahead of Monday’s proposed march to Parliament on the opening day of the Monsoon Session. CJP spokesperson Saurav Das claimed that nearly 20,000 people had gathered in and around Jantar Mantar by evening, although the figure could not be independently verified.

The demonstration has been ongoing since June 20, with the CJP demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination, reforms in the examination system, and justice for affected students.

The protest took a turn on Saturday after activist Sonam Wangchuk, who had been on an indefinite hunger strike, was shifted from Jantar Mantar to Safdarjung Hospital by Delhi Police. Police said the move was carried out in compliance with Delhi High Court directions and on medical advice because of Wangchuk’s deteriorating health.

Speaking at the protest on Sunday, Wangchuk’s wife Gitanjali Angmo said he would end his hunger strike on Monday if political leaders met him at Safdarjung Hospital and assured him that the issue of education accountability would be raised during the Monsoon Session of Parliament.



“If political leaders meet Sonam in the hospital and assure him that they will raise the issue of education accountability during the Parliament session, he will end his hunger strike tomorrow,” Angmo said.

She also conveyed Wangchuk’s appeal to supporters to keep Monday’s mobilisation peaceful. “Sonam has requested all of us to take tomorrow’s march peacefully and ensure that this protest is not misused,” she said.

Meanwhile, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, who began his own indefinite hunger strike after Wangchuk was removed from the protest site, urged supporters to stay at Jantar Mantar overnight to ensure the march proceeds peacefully.

“Our protest is going on. Please come here in large numbers. Stay here for the night. If you don’t come, they will try to end the protest,” Dipke said in a video message. He added, “Our protest and march will be peaceful. I request everyone to follow the rules and follow the guidelines.”



Delhi Police, however, said no permission had been sought or granted for the proposed march and reiterated that prohibitory orders remain in force in the New Delhi district. Authorities have deployed multi-layered security around Parliament and Jantar Mantar ahead of Monday’s planned mobilisation.
